projects.name: 加速火把 (Accel Torch)
projects.summary: 仿 Torcherino 的三档加速火把：右键调范围与速度（100%~640000%），三档各有独立外观与粒子。Right-click to set reach and speed (100%~640000%): three tiers, each with its own look and particles.
projects.description:
A toolkit of three accelerating torches for Horizon, inspired by [Torcherino](https://modrinth.com/mod/torcherino). Written in Rust as a native mod: original code and textures, no assets or code taken from the original.

## The three tiers

| Tier | Block | Speed steps | Reach per axis | Largest area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accel Torch | `accel_torch:accel_torch` | 100% / 200% / 300% / 400% | 1 or 3 | 7x7x7 |
| Advanced Accel Torch | `accel_torch:advanced_accel_torch` | 4000% / 8000% / 12000% / 16000% | 1 to 9 | 19x19x19 |
| Super Accel Torch | `accel_torch:super_accel_torch` | 160000% / 320000% / 480000% / 640000% | 1 to 27 | 55x55x55 |

A reach of 1 covers 3x3x3 with the torch in the middle, 3 covers 7x7x7, and the super torch's 27 covers 55x55x55.

A percentage is how many extra random ticks each block in the area gets per tick: 100% means one extra `randomTick` per block per tick (vanilla's own chance is 3/4096, so about 1365 times faster), 40000% means 400 extra calls.

## Using it

- Right-click a torch to open its panel: the reach on X, Y and Z (odd numbers, + and - step by 2), speed, and the on/off switch. Every click saves at once.
- The panel takes the plain right click, so `sneak + right-click` is what places a block against a torch, the same way a crafting table works.
- New torches start switched off, at the smallest speed step and a reach of 1 on each axis (3x3x3).
- Two items, the Accel Clock and Super Accel Clock, and five recipes; see the gallery.
- Each tier has its own texture and its own spark particles; particles only show while the torch is on.

## How it works

- The torch is a block entity. While on, each tick it calls `LevelRef::block_random_tick` for blocks in its box, the same random tick a chunk gets, so crops, saplings, grass spread, ice and lava behave exactly as they would with a much higher random tick rate.
- One random-tick budget is shared by every torch on the server: at most 3000 calls and 3 ms of work per tick, reset each server tick and enforced across all torches, so stacking them cannot drag the server below 20 TPS. Measured: 5 maxed 27x27x27 super torches still take 5.01-5.04 s per 100 ticks (20 TPS). That budget is split equally between every torch that ticked in the previous tick, so the first torch in the server's tick order cannot starve the others; a torch whose share is smaller than its area keeps its own cursor and carries on from the cell its last pass stopped at, so the whole area is still covered over a few ticks.
- Settings live in the block entity's data (`active`, `speed`, `sx`, `sy`, `sz`), sync to clients through the update tag, and are re-read from the server when the panel opens, so a torch replaced with `/setblock` never shows stale values.
- A change packet is only accepted from a player in the torch's level and within 6 blocks of it; anything else is ignored (with a chat note) rather than failing the payload, which would disconnect the sender.

## Requirements and limits

- Horizon 26.3, API 0.2, side both; native mod, so it compiles on first launch (a few seconds).
- Built and tested against Horizon build `0a875da` / mixins `e59da90`.
- Native code runs with your permissions; the source is in the linked repository, and this page's file is the exact source.

## Credits

Inspired by [Torcherino](https://modrinth.com/mod/torcherino) by lukegrahamlandry and [Torcherino (Unofficial)](https://www.mcmod.cn/class/11277.html) by skniro; no code, textures or data from either project is included. Textures and code by Wen.

projects.name: accelerateddecay
projects.summary: A Horizon port of accelerateddecay.
projects.description:
A port of [Accelerated Decay](https://github.com/nanite/AcceleratedDecay) by ErrorMikey (nanite) for Horizon — leaves fall when their log is cut.

**Implemented so far**

- Ready leaves (`distance == 7` and not `persistent`) are removed **one real second** (20 ticks) after a `#minecraft:logs` block is broken, over the mod's 26-neighbour flood fill, which expands only through already-ready leaves.
- The flood keeps per-tick read and removal budgets, retries, a search radius, a merge cap and an age limit: safety valves the port added for pathological modded trees, which the upstream scan does not have.
- A removed leaf's water goes with it (water for a waterlogged leaf, air for a dry one), the same legacy-block rule upstream applies.

**Deviations and gaps**

- **Removal is a plain block set, not a player break.** The pin has no drop-loot, item-entity or cancelable-break API, so a removed leaf drops nothing, no block-break level event fires and no `BLOCK_DESTROY` fires. Recorded as an API gap (a `machine_destroy_block`-style helper).
- The mod ships no blocks, items or data of its own, so this is a code-only mod with no content archive; it also has no config file upstream, so none is written.
- The flood runs on the server tick with the port's budgets, so a very large tree decays over several ticks rather than in one.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/accelerateddecay/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, the full GNU GPL v3 with ErrorMikey's notice) and are also in this repository. GPL-3.0-only; the complete corresponding source is this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

projects.name: Accurate Placement
projects.summary: Hold right click with a block and every new spot you look at gets one, however fast you move.
projects.description:
Placing blocks fast is all about timing: vanilla places a block every four ticks while you hold right click, so moving fast skips spots and moving slowly stacks extra blocks. **Accurate Placement** times it for you: hold right click and every *new* spot you look at gets a block at once.

- **A new spot, a block**: bridging, building walls and floors, or sweeping along a row; no spot skipped, however fast you move.
- **No extra blocks**: staring at one spot places nothing more.
- **A single click stays a single block**: right after the click it waits as vanilla does, unless you turn the view.
- **Building backwards**: walking backwards while placing toward yourself places one block per step.
- Doors, chests, buttons and other blocks you click still work as usual.

It works **only in your own worlds** (singleplayer and worlds you host). On a remote server it does nothing: the game places blocks at its normal rate, so it cannot trip a server's anticheat. This version has no settings screen: remove the mod to turn it off.

An update for the current Horizon API of [Accurate Block Placement](https://github.com/Lutziano888/horizon-accurate-block-placement) by Lutziano888 (MIT), whose registry entry is archived. That is a port of [Accurate Block Placement: Reborn](https://github.com/KadTheHunter/AccurateBlockPlacement-Reborn) (MIT) by Clayborn, Flourick, schwar and KadTheHunter. All the original licence notices are kept.

A native mod: it needs a Horizon Nightly, not the v0.2.97 release. Each version is made for one Nightly, and the launcher builds it for the Horizon your instance plays.

versions.changelog: First version, built for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-21 (8f83e5c). Fast placing works only in your own worlds; on remote servers the game places at its normal rate.

projects.name: Actually Additions
projects.summary: The Coal Generator and Crusher of Actually Additions, with working recipes, real FE and persistence.
projects.description:
A port of [Actually Additions](https://github.com/Ellpeck/ActuallyAdditions) by
Ellpeck for Horizon. This first slice is two machines, carried from the mod's own
jar together with their blocks, items, models, textures, loot tables, recipes and
advancements:

- **Coal Generator** — burns any furnace fuel (modded fuel included) into a
  60,000 FE buffer at 20 FE/t, returning the crafting remainder.
- **Crusher** — a 60,000 FE buffer, 40 FE/t and 100 ticks per operation, reading
  the mod's own `actuallyadditions:crushing` recipes (47 of the jar's 49; two
  name items from later slices) and rolling the second output at its chance.
- A generator pushes FE into an adjacent crusher; there is no Energy Laser Relay
  in this slice, so adjacency is the stand-in.
- Right-click with fuel or an input to insert it; a wrong item is refused. There
  is no screen yet, so `/actuallyadditions info <x> <y> <z>` prints stored FE,
  burn and crusher progress. That command is a port addition, not upstream.

Both machines keep their FE, burn state and crusher output across save and
relaunch. Not yet ported: the GUI/menus, `lit` state and particles, a comparator
output for FE, FE kept in the item when a machine is broken, the machine
crafting recipes' ingredients, the Double Crusher and the other ~45 machines,
relays/cables, redstone control and the booklet. The one `.hnmod` embeds its
content package, so it installs the blocks and the behaviour together.

MIT — the original copyright and licence notices travel inside the bundle
(`mixins/actuallyadditions/LICENSE` and `data/actuallyadditions/license/`), with the
asset provenance in LICENSE-NOTICE.md.

versions.changelog: This version adds pulse mode, so the reconstructor can fire once on each rising edge of a redstone signal instead of freezing while it is powered, and the toggle is a click with the reference's configurator item rather than a new item of its own. Two of the brief's premises did not survive the artefact: the mod has no wrench, and the item that toggles is a config value defaulting to a redstone torch, so nothing was carried and no extra item part was added — the branch sits where the reference puts it. The saved flag rides the existing state allowlist rather than an item component, because a component route exists here but would give one flag two homes. Proven in game on the edges themselves: with the torch the machine reads pulse on and the toggle item is still in hand; with no signal across a hundred and forty ticks the cycle does not move; the first rising edge spends exactly one thousand and forty and makes one crystal, the falling edge does nothing, and the second rising edge makes another. The same rig without the toggle runs its cycle through the same window, which is the differential. It also answers the review on conversion order for both halves: the source is removed and checked before the result appears, the price is charged only after success, and the item half restores the whole stack if the spawn is refused.

projects.name: ambientsounds
projects.summary: The environment engine with cave and wind ambient beds that fade in and out.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [AmbientSounds](https://github.com/CreativeMD/AmbientSounds) (LGPL-3.0-only, by **CreativeMD** and **AriaFreeze**) for Horizon. This first slice is **the environment engine** and two ambient beds, `cave` and `wind`.

**Implemented so far**

- **The environment scan** runs on the mod's own cadence from its engine file (`environment-tick-time` 40, `sound-tick-time` 4, `block-scan-distance` 40, `biome-scan-distance` 5) and classifies the player by sky access, depth below the surface, rain/thunder and the surrounding biome.
- **Two ambient beds** play through Horizon's music layers with a real fade: in a sealed cave the `cave` bed rises to full gain over 20 ticks, on an open platform it aims to zero and fades out, and **during a thunderstorm the `wind` bed takes over**.
- **Vanilla music is held** while a bed plays and is released when it fades; an "engine off" setting makes the mod silent.
- **Two of the mod's 120 sound files are carried** (about 2 MB of 85 MB), and the build checks that every carried byte is the jar's own.

**Not yet ported**

- the other 118 sound files and their beds (animals, water, weather, suspense);
- the air-pocket block scan and its block groups (so the cave bed currently follows depth and sky, not every cave shape);
- the cross-fade between takes, the pitch curves, the config GUI and the other regions.

**Licence.** LGPL-3.0-only. The port ships the LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts and a notice naming **CreativeMD** and **AriaFreeze**, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256; it is a derivative under the same licence and its complete source is published, with no further restriction added.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

projects.name: AppleSkin (Horizon)
projects.summary: Shows the saturation hidden behind your hunger bar, and what a food item will restore.
projects.description:
Vanilla keeps your saturation invisible: you see twenty hunger points and nothing about the buffer sitting behind them. AppleSkin draws it, so you can tell when a golden carrot is worth eating and when it is wasted.

- Saturation in gold along the top of the hunger bar, half an icon per point, filling right to left as the hunger icons do.
- Food values in tooltips: `Hunger +N` and `Saturation +N.N`, read from the item's own `minecraft:food` component, so food from content mods shows its numbers too.
- Settings under Options > Mods > AppleSkin: the mod on or off, the saturation overlay, the tooltip lines.

It only reads the numbers the game already has and draws on the HUD. Nothing leaves your computer, and it works on any server because it is entirely client-side.

An independent MIT implementation that follows [AppleSkin](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin) by squeek502 (The Unlicense) without copying its code or artwork; see the NOTICE in the source.

versions.changelog: First release: saturation on the hunger bar, food values in item tooltips.

projects.name: artifacts
projects.summary: A Horizon port of artifacts.
projects.description:
A port of [Artifacts](https://github.com/ochotonida/artifacts) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- Three artifacts, each with the upstream effect rules in a pure runtime: `artifacts:bunny_hoppers` (jump strength +0.40 multiplied-base, safe fall distance +10, fall damage multiplier unchanged), `artifacts:feral_claws` (attack speed +0.30 multiplied-base) and `artifacts:shock_pendant` (cancels a hit whose damage type is in the lightning tag).
- Upstream equips artifacts in its own equipment slots (Curios on 1.21.1). This slice **defers the slot system**: the main inventory and off hand stand in for the worn slots, and each artifact counts at most once, like one slot.
- The attributes are re-applied every player tick, so dropping or disabling an artifact removes its modifiers.
- A right click moves a main-hand artifact into an **empty off hand** (refused when the off hand is occupied).
- The items' models, textures, language entries and creative tab.

**Not yet ported**

- **Inventory instead of slots.** A player can carry all three at once, and a second copy of one artifact adds nothing (one slot per kind).
- **Upstream's own equipment slots** (and Curios) are not carried; the off-hand equip is the stand-in.
- The other artifacts of the mod, their configs and the durability/repair behaviour are later slices.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) Wouter Pauwels`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 3: the off hand is now the only worn slot. Until this version any artifact anywhere in the inventory counted, so carrying one was the same as wearing it — the Feral Claws gave +30% attack speed from a backpack slot. Now only the off hand grants an effect, and a carried duplicate adds nothing. Equip path unchanged; the off hand is not replaced when occupied, and an unknown id is refused.

projects.name: Horizon Auto Fishing
projects.summary: Reels in when a fish bites and casts again, with break protection, inventory rod swapping and random delays.
projects.description:
Horizon Auto Fishing automates fishing input: it sends raw use_item packets to reel in on the bite and cast again, and uses inventory clicks to swap rods and throw away junk. You cast first by hand — the mod never casts on its own — and it takes over from there.

Many servers forbid AFK or automated fishing, or may flag it with an anticheat, so using this mod can get you banned. Check the server's rules first.

Break protection keeps a rod from being used once the protect-at threshold (default 5) or fewer durability remain, and the all-rods modes swap a worn-out rod for the freshest rod in your hotbar or inventory. Delays get a small random extra (up to 5 ticks by default). The opt-in junk filter throws away only the items you list — while it is on, it discards the whole stack of a listed item, one stack per tick, even when you are not fishing.

versions.changelog: Fixes the mode migration 1.0.4 shipped with: the mode now lives under a new key, and the first load after updating migrates a mode saved by 1.0.3 to it — all four values keep the mode they had, before any automation runs. The old 1-4 slider stays beside the named choice and the two stay in sync. A value stored by 1.0.4 cannot be told apart from a 1.0.3 value, so 1.0.4 users should check the mode name on the /autofish status line once. Everything else is unchanged from 1.0.4.

projects.name: Auto Login
projects.summary: Logs you in on join when a password is saved and consent is given, and watches for login/register prompts in chat, per server.
projects.description:
Auto Login logs you in on join when a password is saved for that server and player and you allowed it on that server — no prompt needed. When no password is saved, it watches for login and register prompts — in chat, in the action bar and on the boss bar — and acts on them: when the server asks you to register, it first asks you to allow it on that server; once allowed, it generates a random password, sends /register, and saves it for next time. On a Friends world it sends nothing: a friend-invite connection has no stable address, so no credential is looked up or sent there.

Manual commands /autologin and /autoregister do the same on demand, and /autologin allow, set, pattern, delay, toggle and status configure it without rebuilding; /al is a short alias for /autologin.

Passwords are stored in plain text on the device, one line per server, in the mod's own data files — use a password made just for that server.

versions.changelog: Packaging fix: the .hmod archive now includes the repository's MIT LICENSE. Nothing else changes — the Friends-worlds fix and the per-server consent model carry over from 1.1.7 and 1.1.6.

projects.name: Bells & Whistles
projects.summary: Bells & Whistles' decorative station, metro and train blocks for Horizon: 36 blocks — the andesite/brass/copper grab rails, bogie steps and door steps,…
projects.description:
Bells & Whistles' decorative station, metro and train blocks for Horizon: 36 blocks — the andesite/brass/copper grab rails, bogie steps and door steps, the headlight, the ornate iron trapdoor, the station platform, the metro casing/panel/trapdoor/window set and eighteen pilots — with their block items, self-drop loot tables, 44 carried recipes, the climbable and mineable/pickaxe tags and one creative tab. The blocks copy vanilla templates (ladder, lever, iron trapdoor, carved pumpkin, end rod, iron block), because the original's Create classes do not exist here; the headlight therefore keeps a lever's powered state and toggles on right click, and the nine Create-only polished-cut pilots have no recipe. There is no block entity, entity, menu, renderer, config or network code: the original mod at 0.4.7 ships none.

**Implemented so far:** the slice in the package, as described above.

**Not yet ported**

- **Create is not ported.** The wrench behaviour, Create's panel placement helper and copycat face-hiding, and the train-door forms (`folding_metro_door`, `sliding_metro_door`) are deferred — the two door forms are not registered by `ModBlocks` at 0.4.7 anyway.
- **The headlight uses `minecraft:lever`.** Its `powered` state and right-click toggle are a template artefact; the light is constant 15.
- **Custom shapes** for the rails, headlight and pilots are not declared.
- **Nine pilots have no recipe** (Create's polished-cut stones).
- **Recipe materials are substituted**; the recipes are not upstream's exact ingredients, because Create is absent.
- **Stonecutting recipes are carried but not crafted in the e2e.** The crafting path is proved for six recipes; the stonecutter menu path is not exercised.
- **The creative tab's position** differs from upstream, which inserts into vanilla tabs; Horizon content mods cannot.
- **Map colour** is the template's (upstream copied mossy cobblestone/stone colours) and was not visually checked headless.

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0`, not "or later" — the pinned jar's own `neoforge.mods.toml` declares `license="GPL-3.0"`, its `LICENSE` is the GPL version 3 text, and the "or any later version" wording appears only in that text's generic application example, not in a project-specific grant.

Ported to Horizon 0.2 from the upstream mod; pinned to game 26.3, Horizon SDK `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. The full corresponding source ships in this repository beside the artifact.

Based on the original project: https://github.com/aesefficio/BellsAndWhistlesMod

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the carried-recipe family: 44 files were carried and only 6 had ever been crafted, with all 10 stonecutting files unexercised. Every one now crafts in a real game — 30 through a crafting table and 10 through the stonecutter menu — asserting the output id and count and that the inputs were consumed. Four real defects surfaced on the way. Upstream names `c:ingots/brass` and `c:ingots/copper`, and the carry mapped both to copper, so four brass grids were byte-identical to their copper counterparts and one could never win; brass now maps to gold, one-to-one with copper. Four `*_pilot_from_cut` files were byte-duplicates of their base file and are dropped. Andesite's door step filled vanilla's `andesite_slab` grid, which is the vanilla-shadow class, and now uses a two-wide pattern; the validator gained a rule that fails any such grid. And the headlight pair is kept as one grid with a test pinning it. The harness fact is recorded too: a station must be opened with `interact` beside it, not `use`, or every slot click silently misses.

projects.name: betterdeserttemples
projects.summary: The desert temple: 198 carried templates, its jigsaw pools and its loot, generating in game.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [YUNG's Better Desert Temples](https://github.com/YUNG-GANG/YUNGs-Better-Desert-Temples) (LGPL-3.0, by **YUNGNICKYOUNG** and **Acarii**) for Horizon. This is a **content carry**: the temple's 198 structure templates, its jigsaw pools, its structure set and its loot, with the Java pieces rewritten as data.

**What works**

- The temple generates: `locate structure betterdeserttemples:desert_temple` finds one, and `/place structure` writes it — measured at **1,262 cut sandstone, 302 smooth sandstone, 174 blue terracotta, 119 yellow terracotta, 11 sandstone walls, 10 iron chains and 2 spawners** placed, with the processors' removals applied (no diorite, no stained glass, no blue or yellow concrete survive).
- Its chests roll the carried loot tables (14 stacks measured in one chest).
- The placement rule keeps upstream's intent — random spread with a salt and spacing, and no temple within 48 blocks of a river or ocean at y 120.

**Not carried**

- the entity processors (banner, armour stand, item frame, pharaoh) — no data form at this target;
- four approximations: sponge clusters, the purple/quartz pillar and yellow-glass fills below each piece, and acacia waterlogging;
- vanilla desert pyramids still generate (the target has no key to disable another mod's structure set), and the mod's mining-fatigue effect is not applied.

Licence: LGPL-3.0. `LICENSE`, the GPL-3.0 text and a NOTICE naming both authors, the upstream URL and the jar's SHA-256 travel inside the package.

projects.name: YUNG's Better Dungeons
projects.summary: YUNG's Better Dungeons for Horizon, slice 1: the small dungeon. The port registers its own structure type (betterdungeons:small_dungeon_type), which…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [YUNG's Better Dungeons 1.21.1-NeoForge-5.1.4](https://github.com/YUNG-GANG/YUNGs-Better-Dungeons) by **YUNGNICKYOUNG and Acarii** (**LGPL-3.0-only**), slice 1: the small dungeon.

**Implemented so far**

- The mod's structures are assembled by `yungsapi:yung_jigsaw`, a Java structure type 26.3 does not have, so the port registers its own type, `betterdungeons:small_dungeon_type`, which does the assembly the Java type did: it draws a start element from the jar's carried template pool by the jar's rules, rotates and places the pieces and hands the result to the engine.
- It carries sixteen `.nbt` shells and loot piles, two template pools with their weights and `max_counts`, and four processor chains, and it decorates the result with the eleven `betterdungeons:*` processors the data calls — the dungeon banners, the mob spawner, the chest and banner caps, the ceiling props, the support legs, and the rule processor that turns air into cave air.
- A saved bounding box's span is checked in 64-bit and clamped per axis before any allocation, so a malformed save cannot make the support leg scan to the void.
- The port was proven in game at 0.2.1: the launcher-built package passes, and a game without it fails at the first step.

**Not yet ported**

- **Only one of the five structures.** `skeleton_dungeon`, `zombie_dungeon`, `small_nether_dungeon` and `spider_dungeon` are not carried; the last two use the mod's own Java structure types with hand-written pieces, so they are a later slice with their own structure types.
- **The two `remove_*_feature_in` biome modifiers** are not carried: they remove vanilla dungeons by tag, which is a separate feature the engine's biome-modifier registrar would express.
- **The config file** is not carried — the defaults are compiled in, so there is no config screen and no `enableHeads` / `enableNetherBlocks` / `enableOreProps` toggle at run time.
- **`start_height`'s `x_offset_in_chunk` / `z_offset_in_chunk`** are not implemented beyond the default 0 the jar omits; a pack that sets either is refused.
- **Saved pieces are re-derived from the template**, not from a stored block list, so a structure saved by a different mod version loads its template through this port's processor chain.
- **Liquid settings**: the jar's `liquid_settings: ignore_waterlogging` is carried and reported, but the port writes the template's own states rather than implementing waterlogging behaviour, so the engine's liquid handling is what applies.
- **`spawn_overrides`** are carried empty and not read, because the engine ignores them for a mod's structures.

Upstream's licence and notice travel inside the package. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

projects.name: bhc
projects.summary: A Horizon port of bhc.
projects.description:
A port of [Baubley Heart Canisters](https://github.com/Traverse-Joe/Baubley-Heart-Canisters) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The four miniature hearts are **consumable heals, not permanent hearts**: `HeartType` gives each tier a `healAmount` (red 20, yellow 40, green 60, blue 80; soul 0) and `ItemHeart` uses the eat animation over 30 ticks.
- Finishing the use heals that amount, shrinks the stack by one (not in creative) and forces the health sync; it never touches `MAX_HEALTH` — the mod's only permanent-heart behaviour is the **canister** bonus, which the port applies from the inventory.
- The heart canisters and the soul canister items, with the mod's models, textures, recipes, language and creative tab.

**Not yet ported**

- **Inventory scan instead of Curios.** Upstream grants the bonus only while a Heart Amulet is equipped; with Curios and the amulet deferred, the port's main-inventory/off-hand scan stands in for the amulet's colour slots. A player can therefore carry all five colours at once.
- **Soul canisters count.** `getHeartCount` sums every stored canister, including the soul slot, so soul contributes 2 health each.
- The amulet, the belt and the soul-heart variants beyond the canister are later slices.

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, the melted-heart chain: the items and recipes that turn a dropped heart into a permanent one, which is the mod's actual reward loop. Everything is vanilla data — four plain items, smelting and shaped and shapeless recipes, one tag — so no Rust rule changed and the smelting is served by the engine's own lookup. Verified in game from both sides rather than one: a heart enters the furnace and the read a little later still shows one in and none out, then the pair flips to none in and one out, with the same shape at each of the four cooking times, plus a stick in a lit furnace as the control that must produce nothing. The table legs use a different colour in the recipe's centre, which is what proves the hearts tag rather than one specific heart, and the six tier conversions run both ways with two negatives that consume their grid and yield nothing. Two of our brief's numbers were wrong and the artefact corrected them: the cooking times are a hundred through four hundred ticks rather than a single figure, and there are six conversions rather than three, so carrying three would have invented a one-way chain. One engine fact is recorded with it: the older object-shaped ingredients are dropped silently by the loader, so every carried recipe uses the plain string form.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the bookcase and the shelf become storage. The bookcase takes 16 slots of books only and answers a comparator with the highest slot holding a redstone book; the shelf takes 4 slots of anything; both are reachable by hoppers on every face, spill their contents when broken, and the redstone book item ships with its shapeless recipe. Proven in game with the values read from the world rather than the code: the bookcase menu shows 16 slots, a plain book in slot 5 leaves the wire at 0 while a redstone book in slot 3 raises it to 3 and moving it to slot 1 drops it back to 0, the bookcase refuses stone where the shelf accepts it, a hopper moves three books and the break drops two, and a vanilla barrel beside it shows 27 slots and takes the stone the bookcase refused. The enchanting bonus is left as a measured gap rather than faked: the pin declares the hook but the game never calls it and counts a static tag of provider blocks instead, so putting the bookcase in that tag would make an empty bookcase worth a whole bookshelf — the leg asserts the gap so it fails when the pin fixes it. Two findings are recorded for other ports: opening a mod container needs the mod's own `right_click_block` calling `open_menu`, because a plain click opens nothing even with the menu declared, and a block whose contents the engine already spills must not also carry `block_entity_data` or it double-carries.

projects.name: Big Nukes
projects.summary: Nuclear bombs whose shockwave digs real craters and leaves fallout. Launch missiles, build a superbomb, survive in a bunker.
projects.description:
**One mod, one file, on Horizon's new mod API.** 0.4.0 carries its textures, models, sounds, text and recipes inside it. Your bombs, zones and bunkers stay.

- **Make** the bombs: mine uranium below y=16, enrich it in a centrifuge, and put the parts together on the assembly table.
- **Blast** with a demolition charge (radius 16), a tactical warhead (50), an atomic bomb (250), a neutron bomb that kills but leaves the buildings standing, or a dirty bomb. The flash, the mushroom cloud and the ring of the shockwave are seen from far beyond your render distance, and the wave leaves a crater, ash and fires behind it.
- **Set them off** by fuse, by a keypad's code, or by a remote from any distance. Fire a missile, or a splitting missile with three warheads, from a silo at coordinates up to 4096 blocks away, or call a bomber onto a strike beacon. A siren wails at a launch.
- **Build** the Sunbreaker round its core: 26 implosion shells and 98 neutron reflectors, radius 600 to 1000. At 1000 it breaks through the bedrock.
- **Survive** the radiation: a Geiger counter, a hazmat suit, anti-rad, iodine tablets, and a decontaminator that turns the ash back to grass.
- **Weather** what follows the first blast: radioactive storms, mutants in the zones and falling satellites, which a powered radar warns of.
- **Hide** in a bunker: reinforced and armored concrete, a multilayer wall that holds even the Sunbreaker away from its center, a hermetic door, and an air filter powered by a fuel generator that keeps 95% of the radiation out of a sealed room.

The Big Nukes Guide tells it all in the game. English and Russian.

**Commands:** `/bignukes guide` gives the guide. Operators have `/bignukes blast <radius> [x y z]`, `/bignukes maxpower [16|50|250|1000|1024]`, the largest blast a world allows, and `/bignukes events`, which turns the storms, mutants and satellites on or off.

Native source mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, press Build there, and confirm the native-code warning. The launcher compiles it against the Horizon build it is pinned to, named in each version's changelog. It runs with your account's permissions.

All the art and sounds are original. No Minecraft code or assets are included. MIT licensed.

A waves.json that doesn't read is kept aside as waves.json.broken before the world starts afresh, instead of being written over; if it can't be, nothing is saved in that world and the players are told.

projects.name: Extreme Reactors
projects.summary: Extreme Reactors' basic reactor and energizer: the mod's own simulation, fuel, waste, heat and FE, ported.
projects.description:
A port of [Extreme Reactors](https://github.com/ZeroNoRyouki/ExtremeReactors2) for Horizon. The project was called *Big Reactors* before 1.9, and the jar's mod id — and the namespace of every block and item it registers, `bigreactors:basic_reactorcasing` — is still `bigreactors`; the registry id keeps that id so it matches the pack and the content namespace, while the listing uses the project's current name.

**Implemented so far**

- The smallest reactor the mod expresses end to end, with the jar's own numbers: a 3×3×3 basic reactor runs the upstream simulation, reaching ≈126.8 FE/t at steady state and burning ≈0.028 mB of fuel per tick (one ingot ≈ 35,700 ticks).
- The six blocks the reactor is built from, carried from the jar: `basic_reactorcasing` (the shell), `basic_reactorcontroller` (the machine: fuel, waste, heat, energy, on/off), `basic_reactorfuelrod` (the fuel column), `basic_reactorcontrolrod` (the assembly cap) and `basic_reactorsolidaccessport` (where fuel goes in), plus the two items.
- A declared FE buffer (API 142), a container, the formation check, and the controller's tick.
- The **energizer**, the fourth multiblock: its 3×3×3 to 32-cubed forms, the cell count and capacity, the controller and its four blocks, on/off with FE in and out.
- The e2e holds 100 ticks at 8,026 FE ± 60, turns 2 mB of fuel into 2 mB of waste, and reads a housing at ~410 °C.

**Not yet ported**

- **Turbine, reprocessor and fluidizer** — three more multiblocks, each its own machines slice; the reactor's active (steam) mode goes with the turbine.
- **Fluids** — the 10 fluid blocks, coolants, steam, the fluid ports and the reactor's active cooling mode.
- **Ores and the metal chain** — yellorite ore (worldgen), the ore blocks, raw yellorium and the reprocessor's cyanite → yellorium loop. The ingots are obtainable by `give` only until then.
- **The reinforced variant** (1.0 efficiency, 1,000-block maximum, 30,000 FE part capacity), **control-rod insertion**, **solid moderators** and **waste ejection**.
- **GUIs** — the controller's screen, the port's in/out mode, the redstone port and the computer ports; and the Patchouli guide book.
- Only `bigreactors:yellorium_ingot` is accepted as fuel; the `c:ingots/yellorium` and `c:ingots/uranium` tag route upstream uses is not read.

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: The four findings of the review on this pull request, each reproduced against the delivered 0.2.4 before it was fixed. One formation record per machine: the shape is built once and shared through an Arc behind every block that answers for the machine, controllers and ports alike, so four controllers no longer hold four copies of a five-thousand-block shell, which was three hundred and eighty-one mebibytes of duplicated coordinates. Ports are visited once per machine per tick, claimed by a single master controller, and a switched-off machine visits none at all — asserted as a count of visits, not a wall time, so it cannot be satisfied by a faster machine. A port's capability access now re-derives its membership from the world instead of trusting a saved coordinate and a formed bit, so a port left outside after a machine is rebuilt smaller answers nothing; the in-game run shows the detached old port reading not formed while the new one works. And the reactor takes only the fuel its tank has room for, writing the remainder back into the slot, which the access port now shows as three ingots where the old package left it empty.

projects.name: Blazematica
projects.summary: Schematics for Horizon: ghost blocks, a build checker, paste, hover info, the materials list, area saving, Easy Place and a printer
projects.description:
Schematics for Horizon. Load a schematic, see it as ghost blocks where you want to build it, and check your build against it as you go.

- **Load** `.litematic` (versions 1 to 7), Sponge `.schem`, legacy `.schematic` and vanilla structure `.nbt` files from your schematics folder.
- **Place** the ghost: move, rotate and mirror it, keep several placements, restored per world and dimension.
- **Layers** along X, Y or Z, one at a time or everything above or below.
- **Check** your build: missing, wrong and extra blocks are marked, with a progress line.
- **Materials**: what the build needs, what's missing and what you carry.
- **Save** an area as a `.litematic` with two corners.
- **Paste** the whole build at once with /lm paste (single player with cheats, or as an operator).
- **Hover info**: look at a block and the HUD says what should be there.
- **Easy Place** and an optional **printer** that places the missing blocks for you.

Open it with M, or start with /lm help. Commands: /blazematica and /lm.

Client side only. The printer and Easy Place place blocks the way a player does; paste sends /setblock as your own commands, so the server decides whether you may.

The mod API can't draw this much geometry each frame or give a mod the game's full block models, so besides the mod API this mod adds a support module to Horizon's game code and patches four of its functions (the client tick, the world draw, the render needs and the play mouse); the manifest lists each. It works on the Horizon build it is made for.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/blazematica

Ported by TheApple05 from Horizonmatica by keksi2k (https://github.com/keksi2k/horizonmatica, MIT), which it builds on and keeps the history of. On top of it: paste, hover info, layers along X and Z, Java's modified UTF-8 in schematic text, bounded file reading and uncompressed .nbt. Its commands don't clash with Horizonmatica's; to build both together, both have to be made for the same Nightly. Inspired by Litematica by masa and Sakura-Ryoko and Litematica Printer by aleksilassila: it contains none of their code or assets and is not made or endorsed by them, or by keksi2k.

projects.name: botania
projects.summary: The mana loop: an endoflame, a mana spreader and a mana pool at the mod's own rates.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Botania](https://github.com/VazkiiMods/Botania) for Horizon. This first slice is **the mana loop**: a generating flower, a mana spreader and a mana pool.

**Implemented so far**

- **The endoflame** burns fuel for the jar's **800 ticks** (1600 burn time / 2) and produces **3 mana every 2 ticks** into a 300-mana buffer, from an item thrown inside its 7×7×7 box; crafting remainders and the spreader item are refused, as upstream does.
- **The mana spreader** within 6 blocks takes the flower's mana into a **160-mana burst**, which travels at **0.2 blocks/tick** and starts giving **4 mana/t** to the pool from flight tick 60.
- **The mana pool** stores **1,000,000** mana, and `/botania info` reads the flower, spreader and pool state; the readout shows `N/1000000`.
- **Measured in game:** no fuel produces 0, dirt is not consumed, coal burns for at most 800 ticks, the first burst is exactly 160, a pool with **no spreader stays at 0**, and a 13-block burst arrives as 136.

**Not yet ported**

- the apothecary, runes, the lexicon and the rest of the flower/functional-flower catalogue;
- the other spreader and pool variants, and all of the mod's recipes (a carried recipe for livingrock or petals would reference ingredients the port does not ship);
- the mana burst entity (this slice simulates the burst's travel), particle and sound effects, and the GUI;

projects.name: Bridging Mod
projects.summary: A port of Bridging Mod for Horizon: a right click in the air with a placeable block item fills the gap the player looks into, so a bridge can be built…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Bridging Mod 2.7.0: right-click in the air with a placeable block item while looking into a gap over an edge, and the block lands in the gap instead of requiring a block to aim at. Upstream does this on the client, while this port computes the same target from the acting player's eye ray on the server, so it works in single player and on a server with no client mod. Upstream: https://github.com/squeeglii/BridgingMod — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- A right click **in the air** walks the eye ray from 20 % of the reach to the reach, in vanilla's main-hand-then-off-hand order.
- The first cell along that ray is taken when it is replaceable, outside the player's box, and next to a solid non-liquid block on a side the view points into.
- The held block is placed there, one item is consumed (none in creative), the place sound and the `used` statistic fire, and a stack's `minecraft:block_entity_data` is applied only for a player who may use game-master blocks.
- Every placement check runs before anything is written: build permission, item use at the position, the world border, a dedicated server's spawn protection, and an unobstructed destination.
- Torches are skipped as upstream does, a cell inside the player's own body is skipped while the search continues, and anything the assist cannot place falls through to vanilla.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.2 with a control game that does not fill the gap and a selftest that inverts the assertion.

**Not yet ported**

- The placed state is the block's default state plus the item's `minecraft:block_state` component rather than vanilla's `getStateForPlacement` from a fake hit, because the pin has no query for one, so a bridged stair or log keeps its default facing and loses that much fidelity.
- The state's own survival rule is not consulted, because no `canSurvive`-shaped query exists at this pin.
- `minecraft:placed_block` never fires, because the SDK refuses `minecraft:` criteria, so advancement triggers do not see a bridged placement.
- `EntityPlaceEvent` is not fired, so a mod that cancels placements does not see a bridged one.
- On a LAN guest the crosshair check uses the server's eye ray rather than the guest's reported hit, since no forced-hit read is exposed.
- The client effects, the keybind and config screen, and the slab and perspective alignment helpers are not ported, because they are client-only by design.
- The special-item compatibility layer for DankStorage, BankStorage, PlaceableItem and Sable is not carried, and a refused placement is silent, since a native mod may not add a logging crate.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: buildinggadgets2
projects.summary: A Horizon port of buildinggadgets2.
projects.description:
**The build and area modes are held in this version, on purpose.** Horizon's API at the pinned build has no placement call that takes an actor **and** lets a protection mod cancel an individual position: `player_place_block` documents that no survival, obstruction, build-permission or spawn-protection check runs, and the call that does run them (`player_perform_action`) only works for a fake player, which a mod cannot create. Rather than write through protection, a click now plans the cells, reports how many would be allowed and how many were placed, and spends nothing. Selection, all eight mode plans, ranges, the wheel and the world-border rule all work; the hold lifts when the pin gains a cancellable placement call.

A port of [Building Gadgets 2](https://github.com/Direwolf20-MC/BuildingGadgets2) (MIT, by Direwolf20 and the Building Gadgets contributors) for Horizon. This port includes the **building gadget** and its eight planning modes.

**Implemented so far**

- Sneak-right-click a block to select its state. The gadget rejects air, unbreakable blocks, non-source fluids and blocks covered by the deny tag. A normal right-click plans the selected mode and reports its eligible cells.
- On a dedicated server, the gadget reads only the `spawn-protection` setting from the server’s `server.properties` to calculate the eligible count.
- The selection/range state is stored **as an item component** (`buildinggadgets2:gadget_state`), so it travels with the gadget and survives a relog, and the mouse wheel changes the range through the `mouse_scrolling` client hook (`scroll.rs`).
- `/buildinggadgets2` readout commands for the harness, with the carried model, texture, language and recipe inside the one `.hmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The selection stores the raw state id, so transient properties (age, lit, waterlogged, open, …) are not cleaned the way upstream's `cleanBlockState` does.
- The undo stack, the anchor, the paste/rotate gadget, the cut/paste gadget, the destruction gadget, the exchange gadget and their screens are later slices.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-NOTICE.md`.

versions.changelog: This version gives the Cut Paste gadget its collection plan, keeping the same shape as the destruction, exchange and copy plans that came before it. The artefact names the item gadget_cut_paste, with a recipe whose centre is shears, and the kept cells are the ones that are not air, not unbreakable by destroy speed and not in the deny tag; the render-block line stays blocked because the pin cannot query block classes. Proven on the count pair: a piston head and bedrock in the layer leave one cell, two ordinary stones leave three, and nothing is placed or removed in either case. A harness bug needed fixing first — shears do not stack, so the crafting helper had to re-find a fresh stack rather than reusing the old one.

projects.name: bwncr
projects.summary: A Horizon port of bwncr.
projects.description:
A port of [Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded](https://gitlab.com/kreezxil/BadWitherNoCookie) (MIT, by Kreezxil and Eleksploded) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The decision data and the harness surface for upstream's sound silencing: the wither spawn (`entity.wither.spawn`, exact) and wither death (`entity.wither.death`, case-insensitive) sound names, plus the wandering trader's ambient and the llama's ambient, with `/bwncr listen|heard|silence` recording and printing the decisions the hook will use.
- The three carried language files (`en_us`, `es_ar`, `pt_br`) from the jar, inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported, and this is the important part**

- **The suppression itself is not carried.** The pin has no client-side "a sound is about to play" hook: `native-hooks.json` contains no sound or audio entry, and `play_sound_to` is still pending and unstamped. The named hook request is NeoForge's `PlaySoundEvent` — sound id, category, position, volume, pitch, **cancellable**. Until that hook is stamped this port silences nothing; `/bwncr` reports the decisions such a hook would make.
- `/bwncr listen` prints through `/bwncr heard` rather than live: upstream sends each name to the player's chat as it arrives client-side, and this slice collects them instead.

So: installing this mod currently changes no sound. It exists to hold the decision table and the command surface for the slice that lands when the hook does. MIT — the licence is declared by the jar the pack ships (`META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, `license="MIT"`; upstream publishes no LICENSE file), and the notice travels inside the archive at `mixins/bwncr/LICENSE`.

projects.name: centered_crosshair
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Centered Crosshair.
projects.description:
centered-crosshair, ported 1:1 to Horizon from JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair (MIT (c) 2023 JustAlittleWolf, https://github.com/JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair).  Upstream is entirely render-side and tiny (4 Java files, 176 LOC). Vanilla draws the crosshair with integer blit coordinates, `x = (w - 15) / 2` in gui-scaled pixels, where `w` is an integer that already lost its fraction to `floor(windowWidth / guiScale)`. When the gui-scaled size is even the sprite lands half a pixel off the true window centre. This port keeps the sprite centred at the real centre, computed from the raw window size, quantised to quarter pixels, and drawn through a subpixel textured-quad path with the sprite's u/v nudged by a 1/32768 half-texel so linear sampling reads the sprite edges cleanly.  Upstream structure mapped 1:1:

Port by sparticle. Upstream: https://github.com/JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair (MIT).

Source-only .hmod built on the current SDK (Horizon f00125f)

Licence: MIT. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-centered-crosshair

projects.name: Client Seed Loader
projects.summary: Far terrain (LODs) on multiplayer servers, generated locally from a seed you know.
projects.description:
Horizon's far terrain on servers only shows chunks you've already visited. Client Seed Loader fills in the rest from a seed you know, using Horizon's own world generator.

**Use**

- `/lodseed set <seed> [dimension]` saves a seed for current server.
- `/lodseed clear [dimension]` forgets it.
- `/lodseed radius <chunks>` limits generation around you.
- `/lodseed status` shows seed, checks and chunk count.

Far terrain must be on in Video Settings.

**What it does**

- Real chunks from server always win over generated ones.
- Checks your seed against server's seed hash. On a mismatch, it compares a few generated chunks with real ones and tells you if terrain matches.
- Caches generated chunks on disk, so they load instantly next time.

**What it doesn't do**

- Sends nothing to server and makes no network requests.
- Builds and other changes to world only show once server sends those chunks.
- Writes only to `config/client_seed_loader.toml` and `horizon-mod-data/client_seed_loader/`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the eye overlay: standing in cloud glass now tints the whole frame, which is the one behaviour the port was missing and the only reason the mod exists visually. The colour is the block's own declared tint at half alpha, drawn over the frame. Proven where it has to be proven — in pixels, since no registry or command read can see an overlay: with cloud glass only at the player's eye the frame moves 154.8 toward the tint, with vanilla glass at the eye it stays at 222.3, and with cloud glass only at the feet it stays at 242.6, so an implementation that reads the wrong block position fails rather than looking plausible. The previous package fails the same assertion at the same spot. One honest deviation is recorded: the SDK has no layer above the camera overlays, so the fill draws in the crosshair layer in first person and the hotbar layer elsewhere, which is the same paint position as upstream's own choice.

projects.description:

projects.description:

**Not yet ported**

- **The ROM**: 105 Lua files (`bios.lua`, 20 `rom/apis`, 23 `rom/modules`, 60 `rom/programs`) and the shell. That needs a real Lua 5.2 VM, and the pin's lock blocks the engine route (see the port's record), so the engine is the unblocker.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the peripheral surface: a computer can now ask a block beside it what it is and call a method on it. A capability key of this package's own, a peripheral trait with a type name, a method list and one call at a time, the six-side geometry relative to the computer's facing, and the three interpreter builtins getType, getNames and call, with a harness block shipped as the probe. Proven in game with three neighbours at once: a harness on the right answers its type and its methods and round-trips a string and adds two numbers, while a plain stone on the left and air above answer nil for every call, and an unknown method is a named error rather than silence. The stone neighbour is asserted present before the call, so nil cannot be an empty side. A second carriage-return-shaped trap is recorded with it: the one-block terminal is sixteen columns, so the type wraps mid-name and the assertion compares the exact bytes rather than a substring. This is the surface a whole family of add-ons was waiting on; three deviations are stated rather than hidden, including that getNames answers one tab-separated line because the interpreter has no tables yet.

projects.name: continuity
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Continuity.
projects.description:
Exact 1:1 Horizon Rust port of [Continuity](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity)
by PepperCode1 (LGPL-3.0-only). Every upstream Java class maps to one Rust
module with the same names, logic, defaults, and control flow; the Minecraft
client / Fabric renderer surfaces the engine binds sit in `src/seams.rs` with
one seam per upstream call.

## What it carries

- The full properties layer: `BaseCtmProperties` and the Connecting /
  Compact / Random / Repeat / Overlay property families with the exact
  parsing order, defaults, and error paths of the upstream classes.
- The full `CtmLoaderRegistry`: all 25 loader registrations (`ctm`+`glass`,
  `ctm_compact`, `horizontal`/`bookshelf`, `vertical`, the `h+v`/`v+h`
  aliases, `top`, `random`, `repeat`, `fixed`, and the 10 overlay variants)
  with the `createLoader`/`createCustomLoader` helper chain and the two
  built-in resource packs.
- The processor layer: Simple / Compact / Top / StandardOverlay /
  SimpleOverlay quad processors with caching and processing predicates,
  DirectionMaps, QuadUtil, MathUtil, RandomIndexProvider, and the five
  sprite providers.
- The model layer: `CtmBakedModel` + `EmissiveBakedModel` with the
  `ModelWrappingHandler` bake wrap, `ModelObjectsContainer`, and the
  feature states the entity renderer mixins toggle.
- The resource layer: `CtmPropertiesLoader` (pack priority order,
  `java.util.Properties` parsing), `ResourceRedirectHandler`,
  `CustomBlockLayers` + `EmissiveSuffixLoader` reload listeners, and the
  `BakedModelManagerReloadExtension` with the atlas/sprite loader contexts
  (AtlasLoader/SpriteLoader/BakedModelManager mixins, emissive control,
  stitch carry).
- The config screen, the ModMenu entry, and the falling-block / piston
  entity renderer mixins.

## Mod API wiring (rebuild)

- The four config booleans (connected textures, emissive textures, custom
  block layers, manual culling) are settings on Horizon's Options > Mods
  page, same defaults.
- `client_setup` runs the core init: the 25 CTM loader registrations, the
  model-wrapping plugin, and the custom-block-layers reload listener.
- `setting_changed` reads the wrap toggles where the mod API allows
  `setting_bool` (it is a world-only read, unreachable in Setup and
  Reloading) and rebuilds the wrapping handler; `client_setup` applies the
  defaults and `client_resources_reloaded` re-applies the stored flags on
  every reload, the original's `ValueFlag::ReloadWorldRenderer` effect.
- The config file is no longer rewritten at startup: the settings page
  owns the values now (upstream saves on every load; that write is the one
  deliberate deviation).

## Tracked gap

The quad wrap itself runs in the engine's model-bake pass; the pinned mod
API has no baked-geometry hook (horizon-rust/horizon#19759,
`model_baking_completed` gives no view of the baked geometry and edits
nothing; lineage #4953 / #6303 / #6360), so models bake un-wrapped until
that lands and connected/emissive textures do not apply yet.

Source .hmod built on the current SDK (Horizon f00125f, mixins e59da909,
api 0.2). 134 cargo tests green.

Licence: LGPL-3.0-only. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-continuity

versions.changelog: Slice 2, every living traveller rides: villagers and other living entities now travel the tube beside players, where only server players did. The rules are the jar's own — a default blacklist holding the wither and the ender dragon, living entities only, a spectator never riding, sneak refusing the pull, and a ride table keyed by entity UUID — with the entity sweep every ten ticks and a traveller standing in the cell its feet are in. Proven in game: the player reaches x 223.0 at half a block a tick while a villager follows from 199.5 to 223.0 on the same path, a dropped item and a wither stay put over forty ticks, sneaking holds the traveller at 199.5 until the key is released, and both the tube and the entrance recipes craft with their ingredients consumed while nine copper crafts nothing. projects.name: Data Exporter
projects.summary: Saves what happens in your game and your statistics to files on your computer, ready to analyze.
projects.description:
Turns what happens in your game into data you own. While you play, Data Exporter saves events and statistics to files on your computer, ready to analyze with DuckDB, pandas, Spark or a spreadsheet.

Nothing is sent over the network. It only writes to the folder you choose.

**What it saves**

- Session & player: joining and leaving, dimension changes, and a sample of position, health and food every 5 seconds.
- Blocks & combat: blocks broken and placed with their coordinates, your deaths, and the mobs you kill.
- Items & progress: crafting, items picked up, and advancements.
- Statistics: every increase of the game's statistics, at the moment it happens.

By default it only saves your own data. Other players' data, typed text and keyboard input are not captured.

**How to use it**

Options > Mods > Data Exporter > Config has one switch per group and the format (JSON Lines or CSV). In a world, `/data_exporter` says what was saved and where your profile is, and `/data_exporter open` shows it in your file manager.

Files go to `data-exporter/` in your game folder, one file per kind of data, world and session.

**Your profile**

Everything is in `config/data_exporter.json`. Edit it while playing and the mod picks it up within a second. There you can turn each kind of data on or off, send one to its own folder or format, and set size limits. When the folder reaches its limit, the mod stops saving until you free space or raise the limit. It never deletes your data.

Source and full documentation: https://github.com/DylanGonzaloFerreyra/horizon-data-exporter

projects.name: Daybreak
projects.summary: Sun shadows, reflective water, waving plants, coloured light, sun rays and bloom, built to cost as little GPU time as possible.
projects.description:
Daybreak is a shader pack in Horizon's own format. It runs inside Horizon's renderer, so Horizon's culling, batching and LOD stay in charge, and it adds as little GPU time as it can.

- Sun and moon shadows with smooth edges
- Warm sunlight, blue sky light in the shade, a dim blue night
- Coloured block light: soul fire blue, redstone red, copper green, froglights
- Light from torches in your hand (turn on Horizon's Dynamic lights in Extras)
- Waving leaves, grass, flowers and crops
- Water with waves, reflections, refraction and the sun's glint
- A deeper sky with warm sunsets, sun rays, sun glare and haze
- Mobs take the sun's shadow; the Nether and the End get their own light
- Linear light and HDR on Horizon's final shader API 0.2

Every effect can be changed or turned off in the game: Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. The quality is yours to pick there too: turn shadows off for the least GPU time, or choose the shadow map's detail (1024 to 4096) and distance (48 to 160 blocks). The defaults are soft shadows over 64 blocks with screen-space water reflections; the full water mirror is one switch away.

## Which version do I take?

- **0.4.0** is for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer (the final shader API 0.2).
- **0.3.0** is for older builds that still serve shader API 0.1. The Nightly no longer loads it.
The launcher offers the one your game can run.

Original code, no Minecraft assets. Source: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders

versions.changelog:
Daybreak 0.4.1 is a water update for Horizon's shader API 0.2 (the Horizon Nightly of 2026-11-18 and newer).

- **No more checkerboard.** The waves are three swells in directions that follow neither the block grid nor each other, and the fine ripple is smooth noise instead of crossed sine waves, so wide water no longer tiles into a grid. After a pull request by ertugrulahmett.
- **Far water stays calm.** Each wave and ripple fades out where a pixel is too coarse to show it, the sun's glint widens with distance instead of sparkling, and the screen-space reflection no longer adds per-pixel noise. By Bl4ckspell7.
- **Flowing water on slopes.** Sloped water reflected and glinted as if it lay flat, which drew bright streaks on streams and at the foot of waterfalls. Its waves now ride on the slope.

Release notes: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders/releases/tag/v0.4.1

- **Watch** the gantry: a drill runs over the pit on a moving bridge, row by row. The screen says what the quarry is doing, and why when it stands still.
- **Choose** four upgrades: Area up to 17×17, Speed up to a block in 0.25 s, Fluids to plug water and lava and dig on, Chunk to keep working when you are away, in the Nether and the End too.
- **Keep** what matters: it leaves bedrock and any block with contents, and only its owner or an operator can open or break it.

English and Russian.

**Commands:** operators have `/deepbore maxsize` and `/deepbore maxsize <5|9|13|17>`, the largest area a world allows.

Native source mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, press Build there, and confirm the native-code warning. The launcher compiles it against the Horizon build it is pinned to, named in each version's changelog. It runs with your account's permissions.

No Minecraft code or assets are included. MIT licensed.

projects.name: DimStorage
projects.summary: Frequency-linked dimensional chests: a 54-slot inventory shared across dimensions, ported.
projects.description:
Two dimensional blocks in this version: a chest whose 54 slots live in a remote inventory keyed by its frequency, and a tank that holds 16,000 mB of one fluid per frequency, shares that store across every tank on the same frequency, fills and drains by bucket, and keeps its contents across a relaunch. Both persist and both are read back through the game's own capability, not a private field.

A port of [DimStorage](https://github.com/Edivad99/DimStorage) by Edivad99 for
Horizon. This is the first slice, not a full replacement.

Implemented so far

- `dimstorage:dimensional_chest` with the jar's metal block properties, carried blockstate/model/textures and loot table, plus the three component items and four recipes.
- A world-global 54-slot store keyed by frequency (public channel 1 by default); every chest on a frequency shares the same items, with a three-way slot merge once per block-entity tick.
- A vanilla 9 × 6 menu reachable from every side, so hoppers, comparators and normal click/shift-click use the vanilla menu engine.
- Persistence of all frequencies in `<world>/dimstorage/inventories.dat` (atomic write, at most once a second and on close/stop), surviving a relaunch.
- Break and explosion accounting that commits and empties a chest without spilling the shared store, and `/dimstorage channel|info|put|take` as the current fallback for the deferred frequency screen.

Not yet ported

- the dimensional tablet (remote access and autocollect), the frequency/owner/lock screens and the tank's
  comparator — the tank itself ships here and is fully readable and writable through the game's own
  capability;
- the owner/lock/frequency GUI and the item `dimstorage:frequency` component, so a broken chest re-places on the default channel;
- the custom chest renderer, lid animation and rotation display;
- auto-eject, upgrades and size tiers, and the config file;
- owner/private frequencies in normal play — this slice is public-channel only, changed with `/dimstorage channel`.

Licensed **AGPL-3.0-only**, the original's licence, with the complete corresponding source
in the port repository, so the licence obligations are met: original copyright
and licence notices are kept in its LICENSE and LICENSE-NOTICE.md. Help with
the gaps above is welcome.

versions.changelog: This version closes the last way the tank could lose a bucket. At the world's channel limit a new frequency was reported as having room, so the bucket handler accepted the transfer, the store refused to admit the channel, and the tank was then overwritten with the store's empty balance. Now a channel the store cannot admit reports no room at all, a refused write keeps the tank's own fluid and is never reported as committed, and the player is told why — which needed a third fix found in game, because a command's own answer is dropped during a block click, so the refusal had been silent. Proven on a world grown to exactly its limit: the bucket is untouched, the tank still reads its old contents, the neighbouring channel still holds what it held, and the new frequency never appears in the store, while the same click on a known channel lands as usual.

projects.name: Dis-Enchanting Table
projects.summary: Move an item's enchantments onto a book for 25 experience points at a Dis-Enchanting Table.
projects.description:
A port of [Dis-Enchanting Table](https://github.com/Mods-For-Lupin/Dis-Enchanting-Redux) by Lupin and Jason13 for Horizon. The table strips enchantments off an item and writes them onto a book.

- Place the table and right-click it: put an enchanted item in the input slot, a `minecraft:book` in the book slot, and an empty slot for the result.
- A right click moves the enchantments onto a new enchanted book and costs 25 experience points; an enchanted book needs at least two enchantments to be worth dis-enchanting. A missing book, missing experience or an occupied output leaves everything as it was.
- The cost is paid **before** the result is granted: a level cost comes off immediately, a points cost is charged at the tick's end and the book is written only once the charge succeeded (a failed write refunds it), and a second take in the same tick cannot spend the same points twice.
- The book slot is validated as an actual `minecraft:book`, including the hopper path and a save reload, so no other item is consumed for an enchanted book.
- The table keeps the jar's light 7, its 12-pixel shape, its stone-pickaxe harvest level, and hoppers may fill the input and book slots.
- `/disenchanting_table info <x> <y> <z>` prints the three slots for testing.

Unlicense — the original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/disenchanting_table/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository.

projects.name: Durability HUD

Draws a small panel with the durability left on your armour and the item in your hand, so you know what to repair before it breaks.

An original native mod for Horizon, written for this project (MIT). Source and licence: [`native/durability`](https://github.com/Jorungandr/horizon-rust-mods/tree/main/native/durability).
