projects.name: Dynamic FPS
projects.summary: Drops the frame rate while the window is in the background, so Horizon stops burning power for a screen nobody is looking at.
projects.description:
Alt-tabbing out of Horizon leaves it rendering as fast as it can into a window you cannot see. Dynamic FPS answers the game's own frame-rate hook and lowers the cap while the window is not the one in front.

- In the background: the cap you pick (1, 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 FPS), 10 by default.
- Minimised: 1, 5 or 10 FPS, 1 by default. Horizon already caps a minimised window at
  10 FPS before this mod's hook runs, so higher values would have no effect and are not
  offered.
- A lower cap you set yourself is never raised, and the game is never pushed below one
  frame, so input, ticks and the network keep running.
- Settings under Options > Mods > Dynamic FPS.

1 FPS is a power-saving trade-off, not a performance setting: at one frame per second the
client cannot keep up with a 20 TPS world. Ticks, chat and the network still run, but the
picture updates only once a second until the window is focused again; use 10 FPS if you
need the client to stay in step.

This is what Horizon's `framerate_limit` hook documents itself for, and what the game's Battery Mode uses. Nothing is drawn and nothing is sent: it only returns a number.

An independent MIT implementation that follows [Dynamic FPS](https://github.com/juliand665/Dynamic-FPS) by juliand665 (MIT) without copying its code; see the NOTICE in the source.

versions.changelog: Removes the ineffective 20 FPS minimised option (Horizon already caps minimised windows at 10 FPS before this hook) and documents the 1 FPS power-saving trade-off. Background caps are unchanged.

projects.name: Dynamic Trees
projects.summary: Dynamic Trees for Horizon, slice 1: an oak acorn grows through named stages into a full tree, and resumes after a relaunch.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Dynamic Trees 1.7.2](https://github.com/DynamicTreesTeam/DynamicTrees) by DynamicTreesTeam (**MIT**) — slice 1: the oak.

Dynamic Trees replaces vanilla tree growth with trees that grow procedurally over time. This slice carries one species: an **oak acorn** planted on soil grows through named stages — sprout, trunk, branches, canopy, mature — placing trunk, branches and leaves progressively, and resumes after a relaunch.

**Implemented so far**

- `dynamictrees:oak_seed` (the Oak Acorn) used on the top face of dirt-like soil plants `dynamictrees:oak_sapling`; stone and an occupied spot are refused and nothing is spent.
- Growth starts on the sapling's own random tick or a bone-meal click, then proceeds **over time**: one plan step per 20 server ticks, gated by upstream's `growth_rate` (seeded), with the trunk height derived from `signal_energy` and `lowest_branch_height`.
- The tree lives in a world-level record (`<save>/horizon-mod-data/dynamictrees/trees.tsv`), because a tree spans many positions and the pin reverts a block entity's writes inside its own tick; a world close flushes and forgets it, so trees cannot leak between worlds.
- `/dynamictrees info <pos>` and `/dynamictrees list` report the stage, the steps and the block counts.

**Not yet ported**

- **Every other species** (acacia, birch, cherry, dark oak, jungle, mangrove, spruce, crimson and the rest): each needs its own species numbers and shape.
- **The tree-pack API** is Java-only, so a Horizon port cannot host the add-on packs that depend on it.
- **The cell-kit solver** is not implemented — this plan honours the species' numbers, not the solver's geometry.
- **Rooty soil and fertility**, branch radius, tapering, stripping, rot and disease, fruit, voluntary seed drops, the falling-tree entity and leaf age-decay.
- **The dendro pouch, staff, potions, dirt bucket and config screens**, and worldgen replacement of vanilla trees.

Upstream's MIT notice travels inside the package. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

versions.changelog: First publication in the SDK format.

projects.name: Dyson Cube Project
projects.summary: A Dyson-sphere ray receiver: place the controller where its 3x6x3 shell fits and it writes the sixteen multiblock placeholders around itself, then pulls…
projects.description:
A Dyson-sphere ray receiver: place the controller where its 3x6x3 shell fits and it writes the sixteen multiblock placeholders around itself, then pulls up to 50,000,000 FE a tick from a sphere of solar sails into a 100,000,000 FE buffer that only gives power through its bottom face. Beams support six sails each, a sail makes 20 FE a tick, and /dysoncubeproject status, set and add read and change the sphere at a controller. This slice has the receiver, its multiblock and the beam and solar-sail components; the EM Rail Ejector (the only way to grow a sphere in game), the shared per-player sphere, the client renderers and GUIs, and the advancements are not ported yet.

**Implemented so far:** the slice in the package, as described above.

**Not yet ported**

- **EM Rail Ejector**: its multiblock, its 400,000 FE buffer, 40 FE per sent item,
- **The shared sphere**: DysonSphereProgressSavedData, subscribe/unsubscribe, one
- **The client half**: RayReceiverRender, EMRailEjectorRender, HologramRender,
- **The component items' payloads** (dysoncubeproject:solar_sail /
- **Advancements**: the root and the six sphere-percentage milestones.
- The ejector block/item/recipe/loot.

Ported to Horizon 0.2 from the upstream mod; pinned to game 26.3, Horizon SDK `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. The full corresponding source ships in this repository beside the artifact.

Based on the original project: https://github.com/InnovativeOnlineIndustries/Dyson-Cube-Project

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the shared per-player sphere. Slice 1 gave each controller its own sphere because the old pin had no level saved data; at this pin the sphere is a dimension-scoped attachment, so receivers subscribe to a sphere named by the placing player's UUID, several receivers share one reservoir, and the store survives a save, a quit and a relaunch. Proven in game: two receivers on one sphere grow it 2,000 FE a tick together rather than 4,000, roofing one moves that power to the other at the same rate, a second sphere id stays independent, the rate is flat at night and 2,000 by day, the caps hold at a billion FE a tick into a hundred million FE with nothing overflowing, and the sphere survives a relaunch. Five carried recipes craft with their ingredients consumed. The slice also fixed two of its own defects: a local enum named `Command` made `fits` against another build report the package as not fitting, and the run needed `--offscreen` for its menu legs. The sync packet stays a client gap, and the EM Rail Ejector is now possible because there is a sphere to land beams into.

projects.name: Earshot
projects.summary: Proximity voice chat for servers running Simple Voice Chat or Plasmo Voice: 3D voices, push to talk, whisper and voice groups
projects.description:
Proximity voice chat for Horizon. Talk to the players near you on servers that run **Simple Voice Chat** or **Plasmo Voice** 2.x: with Java players using either mod, and with other Horizon players using Earshot. Earshot finds which one the server has by itself.

- **Proximity voice** with 3D audio: voices come from where players stand and fade with distance.
- **Push to talk** (Mouse 4), held or toggled, or **voice activation** with an adjustable threshold and a live mic level.
- A **mic test**: hear yourself as the others would.
- **Whisper** (Mouse 5, held): only players close by hear you.
- **Voice groups**: create one (normal, open or isolated, with an optional password), join one with a click; a panel lists the members and lights up whoever is talking.
- **Noise reduction**, **per-player volume**, **mute** and **deafen**.
- A **mic icon** on the HUD, and a **speaker icon** beside other players' name tags: green while they talk, red if they turned voice chat off, grey and crossed out if they have no voice chat.
- Opus audio and the encryption each server expects (AES-128-GCM for Simple Voice Chat; RSA key exchange and AES-128-CBC for Plasmo Voice).

On Plasmo Voice servers, proximity voice, positions, push to talk, voice activation and mute work; Plasmo's own groups, broadcasts and addons aren't supported yet. Whisper and voice groups are Simple Voice Chat features.

Keys: V opens the voice menu, M mutes, N deafens; rebind them in Controls. Mods > Earshot > Config has a voice chat switch and debug info.

**Network use:** when you join a server that runs Simple Voice Chat or Plasmo Voice, Earshot asks it for a voice key over the game connection (for Plasmo Voice, by sending a public key made new for each voice connection), then sends and receives encrypted voice over UDP to the address the server names (default port 24454 for Simple Voice Chat; Plasmo Voice servers name their own). It contacts nothing else, and stays quiet on servers without either. With voice chat off, Earshot doesn't register Plasmo Voice's channel or answer the server, and switching it off drops the Plasmo Voice connection, its key and anything not yet sent. From 2.0.6, muting closes the microphone within a moment (tested on Windows), and it is only opened while voice chat is on and you're not muted, once a server's voice session or the mic test needs it. Nothing is ever sent while you're muted. 2.0.4 and older keep the microphone open while muted.

**Platforms:** tested on Windows. macOS should work but is untested. On Linux the launcher refuses it: its audio library uses ALSA there, which the game links too.

Works with Simple Voice Chat 2.6.27 (compatibility version 20), Fabric and Paper. Hosting voice on a Horizon dedicated server is off in this version, until its game patch is tested again (horizon-rust/horizon#18462 is fixed).

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/earshot

Plasmo Voice support works on Plasmo Voice 2.1 and 2.2 (tested with 2.2.0-beta.4 on Paper).

Earshot is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Simple Voice Chat, Plasmo Voice or their authors. It contains no Simple Voice Chat code or assets; its protocol support was worked out from our own network captures (PROTOCOL.md). Its Plasmo Voice support is written from the protocol in Plasmo Voice's LGPL-3.0 source, with thanks to its authors; Earshot's code is its own (PLASMO.md). Opus by opus-rs (BSD-3-Clause).

versions.changelog: Plasmo Voice support: Earshot also talks on servers running Plasmo Voice 2.x, found by itself (no whisper there: Plasmo Voice has none). With voice chat off, nothing is sent to a Plasmo Voice server; each connection uses a new key, and Simple Voice Chat and Plasmo Voice never share a connection or queued messages; when the server reconnects you, a new session with a new key starts and nothing of the old one is reused. The speaker icon beside name tags now shows. Other players' voices now come from where they stand on remote servers, and you no longer show up in your own Players list. Built for Nightly 2026-11-22 f1bb66f.

projects.name: elevatorid
projects.summary: A Horizon port of elevatorid.
projects.description:
A port of [ElevatorMod](https://github.com/VsnGamer/ElevatorMod) by Vasco (VsnGamer) for Horizon — the coloured elevators.

**Implemented so far**

- All 16 coloured elevators, on the jar's block template and with its models, textures, recipes, tags and names.
- Jump-up and sneak-down teleport the player to the nearest elevator of the same colour above or below, with the jar's search range and same-colour rule.
- The block entity and its saved state, and the carried assets in one self-loading archive.

**Not yet ported / deviations**

- **Teleport motion:** the move goes through the pin's command path at the tick, the only teleport surface the API offers, so horizontal velocity is lost and upstream's sound and particles are not sent.
- **Input:** a raw jump key edge is unavailable; the jump is inferred from the player's body, with `player_jump` as the exact edge at this pin (issue-shaped gap: give `native_player_tick` the player's input, `on_ground`/jump flag).
- **Suffocation** is approximated with a full-collision block, so glass and leaves differ at the edges.
- **Not carried:** camouflage, the options GUI, the directional model/arrow/yaw, `resetPitch`, the XP cost, mob spawning and `config/elevatorid-server.toml`.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/elevatorid/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with ElevatorMod's `Copyright (c) 2016 Vasco`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the arrival view: the `facing` and `directional` states and the landing rule. A plain elevator keeps the player's yaw and pitch; a directional one turns them to the block's face and levels the pitch, which is upstream's own rule and was previously always passed through from the jump. Proven in game on the same block with only `directional` flipped: a plain ride lands at yaw 33 and pitch 40, and a directional ride at yaw 270 and pitch 0. This version also closes the parity rule's sharpest hole in the port: 32 recipe files had shipped and not one had ever been crafted, and a new phase crafts all 16 — the shaped white and the fifteen shapeless redyes — asserting each output and that its ingredients were consumed, with eight wool and no pearl as the control. Four harness facts are recorded: `ctl click-slot`/`screen`/`ui` need `--offscreen` and hang headless, `ctl state` puts the view under `.player.yaw`/`.pitch`, `ctl block` puts the state at `.state` and needs a tick after `setblock`, and a forwarded run can overwrite a fresh log with the far box's copy.

projects.name: Ender Undertow
projects.summary: An Enderman behind an underground miner can lift them off the floor and blink them into a nearby cave.
projects.description:
In Overworld survival, mining stone or ore with an Enderman close behind you can trigger an eight-tick lift followed by a short teleport. Turning to face it or keeping a wall between you prevents the pickup.

The pack looks for solid ground, headroom and an adjacent walkable space, then checks the destination again before arrival. If the original Enderman moves away, the carry ends. Each pickup starts a two-minute cooldown. Modpack authors can tune the default one-in-eight chance with a scoreboard setting.


**Installing Ender Undertow on Horizon 26.3**

- **Ender Undertow** (this listing) — World data pack for the mining and teleport encounter. It works on its own.
- [Cinematic](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_cinematic) — Native mod for the camera turn, lowered hands and color fade. Install on the host and each participating client, then opt in with `/trigger eu.scene set 1`.
- [Resources](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_resources) — Client resource pack for the Gentleman’s voice and wardrobe and the lingering portal sound. Enable it in Resource Packs.
- [Focus](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_focus) — Optional client shader for blur and warble during the cinematic. Select it in Shader Packs.

[Download all four in one ZIP and see installation instructions](https://michado.dk/projects/ender-undertow/#install).

projects.description:
A port of [Ender IO](https://github.com/Team-EnderIO/EnderIO) (Unlicense, by Team-EnderIO) for Horizon. This first slice is the **item conduit** and its network.

**Implemented so far**

The block carries a self-drop loot table.
- Connections: a face connects to another `enderio:conduit` or to a block with an item container reachable from the touching side (the pin's `native_container_slots`, API 48). The connection state is recomputed when a neighbour changes.
- Per-side configuration (input / output / disabled), the network cycle that groups connected conduits, and item transfer along it, all through the hopper-rule helpers so a refused item stays where it is.
- `/enderio info|config` readout and configuration commands, with the carried texture, models, language and loot inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The item filters (extract and insert filter slots), the speed tiers (enhanced and vibrant item conduits), priority and dye channels.
- The conduit screen (menu, slots and toggles) and the redstone control.
- The bundle (several conduit types in one block), facades, the Yeta Wrench, and every other conduit family (energy, fluid, gas, me, redstone, dense, ender).
- The rest of Ender IO's machines and blocks.

Unlicense, like the original; the port's sources are released under the same public-domain dedication and the notice travels inside the archive.

versions.changelog: Per-side redstone control, the gap line 'the conduit screen ..., the redstone control'. The four upstream modes (never_active, active_with_signal, active_without_signal, always_active) are stored per side beside the insert/extract toggles and applied to extraction, read from the conduit's neighbour signal. A fresh conduit now extracts nothing until its control is set, which is what the jar does — slice 1 copied the toggle and ignored the gate. Proven in game: default control moves nothing for 45 ticks; active_with_signal moves a full stack only while a redstone block is above the conduit and stops when it is removed; active_without_signal is its mirror.

projects.name: enderstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of enderstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [EnderStorage](https://github.com/chicken-bones/EnderStorage) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The ender chest, keyed by its three wool colours, with the mod's own model, texture, blockstate, recipe, loot table and language.
- Upstream keeps **one inventory per frequency** in a world-global manager and every chest with that frequency opens the same container. Horizon gives a mod block entity its own slots, so the port keeps the frequency store as the truth and mirrors it into each chest once per tick.
- The mirror is a **three-way merge on counts**: an untouched slot adopts the store, and a slot a chest changed is applied to the store as a **delta**, so two chests that each withdraw from one stack subtract twice and two that each insert add twice. A stack that no longer fits stays in the chest that inserted it rather than being destroyed.
- The store persists per world and survives a relaunch.

**Not yet ported**

- **The tank does not store fluid at this pin.** The block entity can declare fluid tanks, but a bucket emptied into one does not keep the fluid: the engine's own bucket path consumes the item before any mod hook can refuse it, and a `FluidTanks::insert` over `horizon:fluids` loses the write (a 1000 mB insert leaves 0 after the tick; 500 mB is kept once and the next 500 mB refused; 250 mB is not kept at all; and cancelling the bucket event — which the mod must do so a full tank never pours into the world — takes the write back with the event's transaction). So the tank accepts the click, reads empty, and never pours into the world; the in-game leg asserts exactly that, so a pin that keeps the fluid makes it fail. The measured table and the SDK symbols are in the port's `notes.md` under *Gap: the declared tank at 0b14f8a*.
- **The pouch is deferred.** A pouch opens the same inventory from an item; a mod item has no menu route at this pin.
- Personal (owned) frequencies, the lid animation and the custom renderer are not carried.
- A slot whose *item* is replaced on two chests in the same tick is a genuine tie: one slot holds one item, so the later edit wins and the other stack remains in its own chest.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2020 covers1624, ChickenBones, Christopher R. Thompson (Ecu)`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

versions.changelog: Two inventory-loss repairs. A stack of empty buckets now drains one bucket and keeps the rest of the stack, where the old path replaced the whole held slot with a single item and seven buckets vanished. And a tank placed on a stocked frequency no longer erases the shared fluid: the merged tank and the obligation to write it are one value, so the snapshot is only ever what the entity holds. A third defect surfaced while proving the first: the click path ran a second exchange on the already-swapped hand, duplicating a bucket, so the swap now happens in the bucket item phase where it belongs.

projects.name: EnhancedVisuals
projects.summary: Feel the pain: the original's blood, hurt overlays, heartbeat, explosions and rain, with a real blur through its own shader pack.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [EnhancedVisuals](https://modrinth.com/mod/enhancedvisuals) 1.8.35 (Fabric, Minecraft 26.3), made by
[CreativeMD](https://github.com/CreativeMD) and AriaFreeze, originally by Sonicjumper. It is a reimplementation of the
original's client-side effects against Horizon's SDK, not a rewrite: every number, texture and sound was taken from the
1.8.35 jar, so the effects fire at the same strengths, counts and lifetimes as they do there.

**What it draws**

- **Blood when you are hurt.** The damage type picks the splat: slashes for a melee hit, impact for a fall, pierce for
  an arrow or cactus, the splatter for anything the original names no species or weapon for (a sting, thorns, the
  warden's boom, a mace). The count is the original's `min(5000, damage × healthScaler(health) × amount%)`, so a
  nearly dead player bleeds about three times as much for the same hit. Lifetimes of 25–75 s, placed centre-biased
  (`1 − rand²`), random size and one of eight stored rotations.
- **Elemental damage**, with the original's own counts and lifetimes: fire, freezing, drowning, wither, lightning,
  `fly_into_wall`, parasites and hyperthermia.
- **A low-health pulse and a heartbeat.** Below 6 health the red pulse follows the beat, the buffer is
  `health / max × 100 + 15` ticks, the two beats five ticks apart, and `heartbeatin.ogg` / `heartbeatout.ogg` play with
  it. The picture blurs on each beat, `min(0.7, intensity) × 50` pixels.
- **Explosions**: dust, the ringing that fades over the blast's own curve, everything else muffled, and the picture
  blurred by 50–100 px over 10–20 ticks. Blast strength is multiplied by how much of the player the blast can see (a
  3×3×3 ray sample of the player's box), as the original does, so a wall between you and the blast means no effect.
- **Splash potions**, the **sand** kicked up while sprinting on sand, the **slender** overlay when an Enderman is close,
  **hunger** desaturation as food drops, **rain** drops by look angle, and **splash blur** of 5–10 px for 10 ticks when
  the eyes go into or out of water.
- **Death-screen quips**: a line under "You died!", centred, quoted, from the original's nine.
- **Twelve settings** on the mod's page in Options > Mods: blood, hit flash, blood amount, blood duration, max
  splatters, the low-health pulse and its strength, heartbeat volume and intensity, sounds, rain, the death screen's
  quips, and the shader-pack switch.

**The blur needs its pack, and the mod installs it for you**

The original blurred the screen with its own post shaders. A Horizon mod cannot read the frame it draws on, so the blur
is a two-pass `σ = radius` Gaussian in Horizon's shader language, shipped inside this package as
`assets/enhancedvisuals/native-enhancedvisuals.hshader` and written to `shaderpacks/native-enhancedvisuals.hshader` the
first time the game starts with the mod. Pick **Enhanced Visuals** under **Options > Horizon > Shader Packs** and the
blur and desaturation come from the pack, with the original's own radii and its `Saturation` maths. Without a pack
picked the mod draws a flat haze on the same curves instead (the switch "Shader pack draws the blur" picks between the
two), so the mod is complete without it, only softer.

**Deviations and gaps**

- Splats use eight stored rotations (45° apart) instead of a random 0–360°, because HUD sprites cannot be rotated.
- A blood splat cannot take its shape from the attacker's held item: the pin has no read for another entity's
  equipment and no way to name an entity type, so a melee hit draws the slash.
- A splash potion's overlay stays white: the pin's splash event carries the item but not its potion contents.
- Textures are baked into small atlases: 96 px for the non-blood splats and 256 px for the overlays.
- The original's per-effect `opacity` and `disabled` switches are not exposed, nor its `damageBlackList` and
  `useHealthPercentage`; the effect toggles cover the enabled/disabled half.
- `/displayvisual`, `/clearvisual` and the three effect packets are not ported. In single player the world's hooks reach
  the client in the same process, and on a server with the mod installed they run there; a client-only install on
  someone else's server still draws the health-based effects, but not damage types or blast centres.
- `HealthHandler` and `UnderwaterHandler` are `enabled = false` in the original and are not ported either; the `snow`
  textures are in the jar with no handler drawing them; the `Focus` shader belongs to the thirst addons.

**Licence and provenance**

LGPL-3.0-only, as the original jar declares (`license = "LGPL-3.0-only"`), and the port keeps its notices: the
original's `LICENSE` and a `NOTICE` crediting CreativeMD, AriaFreeze and Sonicjumper travel inside the package and are
in the repository. Textures are the original's, unmodified apart from being turned into the rotation grids and, for
the overlays, downscaled; the sounds are byte for byte the original's. Built from this repository against Horizon
`0a875da91dbb0fdcb7ba8c42c11341aa229af51a` (Nightly 2026-11-20) and horizon-mixins
`e59da9094f0c2fdda6c627fe9eff22dec6a906f0`; the textures, sprites and icon are rebuilt from the jar by
`tools/gen_assets.py`, and the pack by `tools/pack_shader.py`.

projects.summary: A Horizon port of evilcraft.
projects.description:
A port of [EvilCraft](https://github.com/CyclopsMC/EvilCraft) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- `evilcraft:blood_extractor`: a container for 5,000 mB of blood that fills when the player kills a mob (jar item plus `ItemBloodExtractor`, `ItemBloodExtractorConfig`).
- `evilcraft:blood_chest_menu`: 11 slots and 2 data slots (tank, capacity), upstream's `ContainerBloodChest` (2×5 + 1).
- Every number is upstream's; `FINDINGS.md` names the file each came from. The one that reads wrong at first glance: `AnvilRepairAction` returns **25F**, which `RepairItemTickAction` *multiplies* by `mBPerDamage` (5), so an anvil step costs **125 mB** — pinned by `a_chipped_anvil_becomes_an_anvil_for_one_hundred_twenty_five_mb`.
- Blood arithmetic, the kill and inventory hooks, chest persistence and repair, the commands, the screen and tooltip, and the embedded content loader.

**Not yet ported**

- **Recipes are not carried.** `blood_chest` needs `evilcraft:blood_infusion_core` (a Blood Infuser product) and `blood_extractor` needs `dark_spike` + `dark_gem`; none of those are in this slice, so both items are creative-only for now.
- **The curse roll is not applied.** `randomBadEnchants = true` with `randomBadEnchantsChance = 10000` is recorded in `runtime.rs` (`BAD_ENCHANT_CHANCE`), but adding an enchantment component is not implemented.
- **The BER chest model is not carried.** `RenderBlockEntityBloodChest` draws a chest model with `textures/model/blood_chest.png`; a content model cannot do a block-entity renderer, so the chest is a static block model.
- The rest of the mod's blocks and items, the Blood Infuser, the Spirit Furnace, the broom and the werewolf/vampire systems are later slices.

EvilCraft for Horizon is listed under CC BY 4.0. The package includes the upstream attribution and MIT notice. Version 0.2.10 is pinned to Horizon 0a875da and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: This version audits every one of the jar's forty Blood Infuser recipes and carries the only remaining file whose input and output are both registered ids: a spider eye becomes a fermented spider eye for 1,500 mB over 500 ticks at tier two. The other twenty fail honest gates — eighteen name items this port does not carry, and the two vanilla-keyed ones are the recorded upstream defects (a shadowed tier and a 25,000 mB cost against a 10,000 mB tank). Proven in game by a readout rising to thirteen recipes, the spider eye staying inert at tier zero, and exactly one product for the declared fluid and time, with the prior ten- and twelve-recipe packages as differentials and an inverted self-test exiting one. No further infuser file qualifies at this pin.

projects.name: extended_industrialization
projects.summary: A Horizon port of extended_industrialization.
projects.description:
A port of [extended_industrialization](https://github.com/Swedz/Extended-Industrialization) by Swedz. Its generator and monitor-free recipes use vanilla ingredients; the mod is MIT.

The first port of Extended Industrialization, and it opens with the electric canning machine's water half: a block entity with a 32,000 FE buffer, two item inputs, two item outputs and two 16,000 mB tanks, running the jar's two water recipes. Proven in game both ways round: filling takes the bottle from its slot and 350 mB from tank zero in one start, spends 200 EU and produces a water bottle, while emptying takes that water bottle back and returns a glass bottle plus 350 mB into the second tank; an awkward potion starts no run and consumes nothing, a machine with no energy takes nothing, and the buffer, both tanks and both slots survive a save and relaunch. A break in survival drops the machine itself. The port also fixes a defect in the jar's own data: its loot table uses the 1.21.1 plural condition array, which evaluates false at 26.3 so the block would drop nothing at all and report no error — the port ships the singular typed condition and proves it with that break. The GUI is a recorded deferral, and honey is recorded as blocked because a mod fluid cannot live in a tank at this pin. The families that need the parent's plates and ingots are recorded as not ported with their reason.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the solar boilers: a bronze and a steel boiler that turn water into steam only in daylight with a clear view of the sky, and that calcify as they work, losing efficiency until a wrench scrapes them clean. The steam question was the point of this slice and it is answered by measurement rather than assumption: the campaign's own parent port models steam as energy and registers no steam fluid, and a package may only declare a fluid in its own namespace, but the engine does offer a tank-only fluid declaration, so the boiler declares its own steam, fills a real tank with it, and a pipe drains it. That also corrects an earlier claim in this port that distilled water was blocked for want of a fluid registry. Proven in game with the ratio and the sky rule: sixteen millibuckets of steam per millibucket of water, four a tick at noon, three hundred and twenty drained back out by a pipe, the tank frozen for forty ticks when a block is placed above and running again when it is removed, and calcification at fifty percent halving the rate until an iron axe resets it. Two defects only the game found are recorded: one part type attached as both the block and the block-entity part makes the engine refuse the package, and this data set spells the axe tag differently from the loader's convention, so both spellings are accepted.

projects.name: extradisks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of extradisks.
projects.description:
A port of [Extra Disks](https://github.com/ChaoticTrials/ExtraDisks) by MelanX for Horizon — slice 1, the **1024k item storage**.

**Implemented so far**

- `extradisks:1024k_item_storage_block`, a block entity holding 1,048,576 items in up to 256 resources, and `extradisks:1024k_item_storage_disk`, the same storage in the `extradisks:storage` item component, so a disk carries its contents when moved.
- One engine for both: capacity 1024 × 1024 = 1,048,576, an insert of `min(amount, free)`, an extract of `min(available, amount)`, a resource being the item **plus its components** (two named diamonds are two resources), and the saved `"<amount>|<id>|<component key>"` form trimmed to capacity when loaded.
- The block's interface: right-click with a stack to insert, empty-handed to take one stack out; `/extradisks info|insert|extract` and `/extradisks disk …` (the commands move items without an inventory, which is how the exact capacity is checked).
- Breaking the block returns its contents to the breaker. When the inventory cannot hold them all the break is refused and the block keeps the remainder, so a filled block is never lost to a plain block item.

**Not yet ported**

- **No network.** The block is standalone storage, not a Refined Storage network node, so the parent's Grid cannot browse it (each port is its own crate and there is no cross-mod API).
- **No energy.** Upstream the 1024k block draws 14 FE/t; nothing is modelled here.
- **No GUI.** Upstream's storage menu (insert slots, a search box, a sorting/priority panel) is not built; the right-click and the commands are the interface.
- **No recipes.** Every recipe in the jar needs `refinedstorage:` ingredients and tags that only the parent mod can declare, so the block and the disk come from the creative tab.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/extradisks/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. Apache-2.0. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the block's own loot table, proven in game: a broken storage block now drops both itself and its contents' block item, where the carried table was in the 1.21.1 dialect and it dropped nothing. The pool is now the 26.3 shape — a singular `"condition": {"type": "minecraft:survives_explosion"}`, `"rolls": 1`, no `bonus_rolls` — matching vanilla's own block tables. The port also gains a data-shape check and closes a gap that had never run: readiness now reads `wait-ready`'s snapshot because `ctl screen` is null in `--headless` and `ctl state` carries no server block. Proven in game: a barrel beside the storage drops one and so does the storage, the inventory readout holds 1,048,640 of 1,048,576, and the unmodded game does not know the block. One tooling caveat is recorded with proof in the port: `fits` against another build reports this package as not fitting because the usage scanner records the `item` command argument's match arm as building the SDK `Item` field by field — the type is byte-identical in both builds' surfaces and the argument works in game. An aliased import does not help; the scanner resolves through the `use`. The same false positive will appear on any port with an `item` argument.

projects.name: fluxnetworks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of fluxnetworks.
projects.description:
A port of [Flux Networks](https://github.com/SonarSonic/Flux-Networks) (MIT, by Sonar Sonic and BloCamLimb) for Horizon. This first slice is the network core: one network, five blocks and one readout.

**Implemented so far**

- `fluxnetworks:flux_plug` pulls FE from the blocks beside it (up to its transfer limit and what the network asked for last cycle), buffers it, and gives it to the network.
- `fluxnetworks:flux_point` takes FE from the network's plugs and storages by priority, up to what the blocks beside it can accept, and pushes it there.
- `fluxnetworks:basic_flux_storage`, `herculean_flux_storage` and `gargantuan_flux_storage`: network buffers of 2,000,000 / 16,000,000 / 128,000,000 FE with transfer limits of 20,000 / 120,000 / 720,000 FE per tick.
- Every device declares its FE buffer as the block's energy capability (API 142), so a cable or machine from another mod can read and fill it, and the network runs its pass after each level tick.
- `/fluxnetworks info|energy|network|priority` readout and configuration commands, plus the carried models, textures, language and recipes inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported, and one deliberate deviation**

- A device of **another network is treated as an outside energy block**. Upstream refuses every `IFluxDevice` as an outside block; a one-bundle world has no other block with an FE buffer, so this slice draws the boundary at the network id: a plug or point ignores the devices of its *own* network and treats a device of another network as an ordinary FE block. Two networks placed side by side therefore exchange FE through their plugs and points. `FINDINGS.md` and the support module record it; the e2e's source and receiver are devices on networks 10 and 20.
- The controller and its GUI, the wireless transmitter, the flux controller and its screen, surge mode, chunk loading, the storage colour layer, the security levels and the config file are later slices.
- The device blocks' own GUIs and their upgrade items are not carried; configuration goes through the commands.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/fluxnetworks/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the flux-dust source. Every one of the seven carried recipes — flux_core, flux_block, plug, point, controller, storage and configurator — required `fluxnetworks:flux_dust`, and nothing produced it, so the mod's entire content was unreachable in survival. The mechanic is now carried from the jar's own handler: click obsidian with redstone in the gap, over bedrock or a flux block two below, and each redstone becomes a dust (capped at 512), with the upstream chance deciding cobblestone versus the obsidian sliding down. Proven in game: all seven recipes craft with their declared id and count, their ingredients consumed, and two wrong patterns left empty; eight redstone make eight dust and the obsidian is consumed; a stone base refuses and keeps the redstone; 576 redstone leave 512 dust and one 64 stack; and flux_core consumes four of the dust the mechanic had just made.

projects.name: FPV Horizon
projects.summary: Fly real FPV drones in Horizon with quadcopter physics, Betaflight rates, an OSD and gamepad support. Beta.
projects.description:
**Beta.** Fly FPV drones in Minecraft as in a drone sim.

Press **H** (L1 + R1 on a gamepad) to put your drone down and switch to its camera. Your body stays where it stood. Arm with **R** (Triangle), fly, and press **H** again to return to your own eyes.

**Features**

- Quadcopter physics: 6-DoF flight, blade element propeller lift and drag, motor back-EMF and heating, battery voltage sag, and block collisions with bouncing.
- Real drone presets: 5" freestyle and race quads, a 3.5" cinewhoop, a 75mm whoop and a 7.5" long-range build, or your own custom build.
- Betaflight rates (RC Rate, Super Rate, Expo per axis), a configurable deadzone and an optional 3D mode.
- FPV camera that rolls with the drone, with an adjustable field of view, an OSD and stick gimbal overlays.
- Gamepad (Mode 2) or mouse and keyboard.
- Motor and wind sound.

**What it does and doesn't do**

Client-side only. While a drone is out, the mod reads the gamepad and the player's position, moves the camera, and stops pad buttons from also triggering game actions. It makes no network connections and reads or writes no files beyond its own settings.

**Credits**

The flight physics, drone build model, rates and controller logic are based on code from [Minecraft FPV](https://github.com/minecraft-fpv/mfpv-client) by its authors, used under GPL-3.0.

versions.changelog: 1.2. Flies through a simulated flight controller, and adds the setup screen (J) for drones, rates and camera. Built for Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da).

projects.name: framedblocks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of framedblocks.
projects.description:
A port of [Framed Blocks](https://github.com/XFactHD/FramedBlocks) (LGPL-3.0-only, by XFactHD) for Horizon. This first slice is the **full-cube frame** and its camouflage.

**Implemented so far**

- `framedblocks:framed_cube`, the full-cube frame, with upstream's frame properties: wood map colour, `strength(2F)`, wooden sounds, ignitable by lava, and occlusion once a solid camo is set. Its default state is `alt=false`, `reinforced=false`, `solid_bg=false`, and those three flags are outside this slice.
- Camouflage from `handleInteraction`: right-clicking an empty frame with a block item applies that block as the camo (consuming the item unless creative), and an empty-hand click on a framed block removes the camo and returns the block item.
- The camo is stored as a block id on the frame's block entity and drawn as that block's default state, with the carried frame block, model, texture, language, recipe and loot inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/framedblocks` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

- One frame shape only (the full cube). Slopes, panels, pillars, doors, the double blocks, waterlogging, `alt`/`reinforced`/`solid_bg`, glowstone frames, intangibility, overlays, the camo applicator, wrench rotation, camo rotation, state cycling and the item's camo preview are not ported.
- **Default-state block camos only.** Upstream stores the placed `BlockState`; a block item gives its block's default state, and this port stores the block id and draws that default state. A state-specific camo (a stair's facing, a log's axis) is not expressible from an item at this pin.
- The frame's own renderer layer and the camo's tint/overlay passes.

LGPL-3.0-only, like the original; the full licence and the original copyright notice travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the camo is a block state. The block entity now stores the full state — block id plus properties — where slice 1 stored only an id and drew that block's default; `/framedblocks camo <x> <y> <z> [state]` sets and reads it and refuses anything that is not a block state. The render differential is the proof: with `minecraft:grass_block[snowy=false]` the screenshot holds 153 snow pixels and with `[snowy=true]` 20,870, so the state is what is drawn, not just what is saved. Breaking a frame drops both the frame and its camo block. This version also closes a parity hole the port had since slice 1: both carried recipes now craft in game, the frame giving four with the grid consumed and the hammer one. A local `Held::Block` variant is renamed `Held::BlockItem` because the fit scanner read it as the SDK's non-exhaustive `Block` and reported a false failure — the rules and tests are untouched. Three command-parser facts are recorded: a literal may not follow arguments at this pin, `word` cannot carry a state (`Expected whitespace to end one argument`), and a greedy optional `text` last node works.

versions.changelog: Slice 2: the faithful left-click take, and the locked drawer's kind. The 0.1.0 ruling — that a block-entity write from `left_click_block` was reverted, so a take would duplicate — was re-checked at the new pin, as the campaign requires for a blocked item, and it no longer holds: the write persists. So upstream's take is back: one item, a whole stack while sneaking, the front panel only, inside a three-tick window; and a locked drawer keeps its kind when it is emptied, then takes its own kind back. Proven in game: a left click moves the drawer 68 to 67 with one stone in hand; a sneaking click takes the locked drawer's ten; the emptied locked drawer still reads its kind; and all ten drawer recipes craft, consume their ingredients and refuse a wrong shape.

projects.name: Hipped´s Galaxie Shader
projects.summary: A galaxy night sky with turning planets, volumetric clouds, sun shafts, rainbows, puddles, water waves and glowing Nether and End skies.
projects.description:
A shader pack for Horizon (shader API 0.2) that turns the sky into a galaxy and brings weather, light and water to life.

**Sky**
- Night: a painted galaxy with glowing nebulae, a blue gas giant with four turning moons, twinkling stars, rare shooting stars and an aurora in cold biomes.
- The moon: a round, cratered moon with dark seas and real phases (full, half, crescent, new) instead of Minecraft's square one, with a soft terminator and earthshine.
- Now and then a great comet that stays for several nights: a bright head in a green coma, a broad curved dust tail with striations and a faint blue ion tail.
- Day: a deep blue scattered-light sky with volumetric clouds. Some days are clear, some overcast; clouds cast shadows and let sun shafts through their gaps.
- After rain: rainbows (sometimes a double one), fog bows on damp mornings, rare solar and lunar eclipses with a corona.

**World**
- Sun and moon shadows; torches and other light sources fill the shadows around them.
- Coloured block light (lava orange, soul fire blue, redstone red) and light from held torches with Horizon's Dynamic lights.
- Leaves, grass and flowers sway in the wind; sunlight shines through leaves.
- Rain darkens the ground and leaves reflecting puddles that dry over a few minutes; rain rings and sheet lightning in storms.
- Water with waves, refraction, depth colour, foam, caustics and a mirror; light shafts and floating specks under water.
- Bloom, biome-tinted haze, auto exposure and a filmic tone curve; optional depth of field, motion blur and chromatic aberration.

**Nether and End**
- The Nether glows in each biome's colour, lit from below by the lava sea, with heat shimmer, rising embers and an animated portal.
- The End gets a black hole with a glowing accretion disc over a drifting violet nebula.

Every effect has its own option on the pack's options page. Needs a Horizon build that serves shader API 0.2; it is made for a strong GPU (tested on an RTX 4060 Ti).

All textures are painted by the pack's own generator (skygen, in the source repository); nothing comes from Minecraft.

versions.changelog:
- A round, cratered moon with real phases instead of Minecraft's square moon, with a soft terminator and earthshine.
- A fuller comet: a broad, curved dust tail with striations, a green coma and a faint blue ion tail.

projects.name: Gateways to Eternity
projects.summary: A port of Gateways to Eternity for Horizon: a gate pearl opens a gateway, the gateway runs its wave list, and each wave pays out when its mobs die. The…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Gateways to Eternity 1.21.1-5.1.0: a gate pearl opens a gateway, the gateway runs its wave list, and each wave pays out when its mobs die. This slice carries one gateway, `gateways:emerald_grove`, with the jar's complete four-wave list, its rewards and its timing rules. Upstream: https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/GatewaysToEternity — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The item `gateways:gate_pearl` is made by the emerald-grove recipe (eight flowers around an ender eye) and carries its gateway in `minecraft:custom_data`; it ships as a vanilla shaped recipe with a result component, because a content mod cannot declare the jar's own recipe type.
- Using a pearl on a block opens the gateway there with upstream's placement lift from the clicked block's top, and a second gateway in the same box is refused.
- The gateway runs the jar's four waves in order — zombies, spiders, a mixed wave, and a named zombie villager — each after its setup time and within its maximum wave time, with the 200-tick no-player grace period, dead-mob accounting and out-of-leash re-placement.
- Wave rewards are split into stacks of four and spawned as item drops at the gateway, the completion reward summons six of each animal, and each is paid once.
- Gate state is bound to the world it was opened in and cleared when that world closes, so a gate can never resume or teleport an entity from a save loaded in the same process.
- `/gateways list` and `/gateways open <x> <y> <z> <id>` work at permission level 2, standing in for upstream's `/open_gateway` and accepting a namespaced id.
- The port was proven in game at 0.2.1: the launcher-built package passes, a game without it fails at the first step, and a selftest inverts the reward assertion.

**Not yet ported**

- The gateway entity itself is absent, so there is no visible portal, boss bar, particles or sound; the gateway is a server-side record and the wave mobs are what a player sees.
- An open gateway does not survive a world reload, because upstream saves it as an entity and this port keeps it in memory only.
- Wave attribute, effect and gear modifiers and `entity_loot` rewards are not applied, because the pin has no attribute API and no per-mob loot roll, and the failure explosion and lives system are not carried either.
- The other seven gateway definitions (basic blaze, slime and enderman, overworldian nights, hellish fortress, the endless pair) and their recipes are not carried.
- The pearl's tooltip lines and its size-driven model are missing, since the size models need a custom item property the content API does not offer.
- JEI and Jade integration, the `gates_defeated` statistic and the advancement trigger are not implemented.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: glassential
projects.summary: A Horizon port of glassential.
projects.description:
A port of [Glassential Renewed](https://github.com/bigenergy/glassential-renewed) by bigenergy (Big_Energy) for Horizon — the glass set plus its two behaviours.

**Implemented so far**

- The 24 carried glasses as content: blockstates, block and item models, textures, recipes, loot tables, tags, the creative tab and the language files. Every item model's sprite is namespaced to `glassential:`, so the carried textures resolve.
- **Redstone glass** reports its neighbour signal and lights while powered.
- **Smart glass** joins its connected panel and turns `powered` on when any member is powered. A panel is capped at **1024 blocks** (upstream's limit) and one level tick rebuilds at most 32 panels, so a huge connected mass cannot stall a tick.
- The jar's glass sounds, hardness and light levels.

**Not yet ported**

- Per-entity collision (ethereal, ghostly and the reversed glasses), gravity glass, the colour-able painter, the clear-fluid face occlusion, the lava-lamp step damage and the one-way glasses: they need hooks or a block-entity renderer the pin does not have.
- The panel updates after the level tick rather than inside vanilla's neighbour update, so a comparator sees a powered change one tick later.
- Panes, doors, trapdoors and the other non-cube shapes.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/glassential/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the clear-fluid glass's face connections: its six up/down/east/west/north/south booleans are now derived at placement and on every neighbour change, where before all 128 of those states were dead data reachable only by `/setblock`. A face links only to the same block, which is upstream's own rule, and the block owns the state like the smart glass owns its powered flag. Proven in game: an isolated pane connects to nothing; a second pane links both ways; a middle pane links on both sides; a stacked pane links up and down; breaking one clears the end face again; and the differential — a clear *fake* glass beside it — links neither way. The second half of the gap line stays blocked and is recorded as such: fluid-face occlusion needs an occlusion shape that content 0.2 cannot declare, and the hook gives no direction or position. No upstream defect was fixed: the jar's placement sets NORTH twice, but the redundancy changes no behaviour, so it is documented rather than corrected.

projects.name: Gleaming Ores
projects.summary: Animated, glowing ores: a shine sweeps across every ore, so you spot them in the dark. No mods needed
projects.description:
Ores that shine. Every ore gets new, animated specks that glow in their own colours, so they stand out in a dark cave: cyan diamonds, green emeralds, gold nuggets, red redstone and more.

- **Every ore**: coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, emerald, lapis and diamond (stone and deepslate), Nether gold and Nether quartz.
- **Animated shine**: every few seconds a band of light sweeps across each ore, each block at its own moment, so a vein shimmers in waves.
- **Glow**: the specks are drawn at full brightness in the dark. They don't light up the cave around them.
- **Variety**: two layouts per ore, turned at random, so veins don't repeat.
- **Your stone stays yours**: the stone, deepslate and netherrack under the specks are your game's own (or your texture pack's), so ores always match the blocks around them.
- **No mods needed**: it works in Horizon as it is.

**Fair play:** only ores you can already see gleam; nothing shows through stone, so it's not an X-ray pack. Some servers have their own rules about ore-highlighting packs: check them before you play there.

All the speck art and the icon are Gleaming Ores' own: the pack contains no Minecraft textures.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/gleaming-ores

projects.name: gmut
projects.summary: A Horizon port of gmut.
projects.description:
A port of [Gravitational Modulating Additional Unit](https://github.com/gisellevonbingen-Minecraft/GravitationalModulatingAdditionalUnit) by gisellevonbingen for Horizon — slice 1, the item and its stored modes.

**Implemented so far**

- `gmut:module_gravitational_modulating_additional_unit` on the paper template (stack size 1, rarity rare), with one of five steps kept **per stack** in the item's own `gmut:vertical_speed` component.
- The five steps (`off` 1.0x, `low` 1.5x, `medium` 2.0x, `high` 2.5x, `ultra` 3.0x), cycled by right-click (back while sneaking) or by `/gmut mode|next|prev`, each change printing upstream's `Vertical Speed Modifier: <step> (<mult>x)` line.
- `/gmut info` reports where the unit is (`held` / `off_hand` / `carried(N)` / `absent`), the stored step, four rule defaults and the gate; the tooltip shows the stored step and the gate line.
- The carried model, texture, creative tab and English names.

**Not yet ported / deviations**

- **It does not change velocity.** The stored step is a label and a number: this port applies no vertical-speed multiplier, no gravity change, no flight, and no FOV or sound change. Upstream gates those on a worn MekaSuit carrying a working unit; Mekanism is not ported at this pin, so the gate is permanently `needs_gravitational_modulating_unit` and is reported honestly.
- **No Mekanism recipe content.** The jar's shaped recipe and its advancement are not carried: every ingredient (`mekanism:module_base`, `mekanism:alloys/reinforced`, `c:circuits/ultimate`, `c:pellets/polonium`) does not exist at this pin, so the recipe could never match and the game rejected it at load. The item is reachable by `give` and from its creative tab only.
- The HUD indicator, suit installation, the module GUI and the remaining config options.

MIT: the original copyright and licence notices ship inside the package (`LICENSE` and `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` at its root) and are also in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Review repair: the licence keeps upstream's full copyright line (`Copyright (c) 2022 gisellevonbingen`) and the notice names only files that exist at the package root; the listing text now says what the item actually does — it stores a step and changes no velocity, and no Mekanism recipe content is carried, because the 0.2.0 recipe files were dead data the game rejected at load and are dropped. The five steps, the readout, the tooltip and the gate are unchanged.

projects.name: gtceu
projects.summary: The steam chain: a solid boiler, a steam turbine and an electric macerator.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [GregTech CEu Modern](https://github.com/GregTechCEu/GregTech-Modern) (LGPL-3.0, by **KilaBash**, **screret**, **Mikerooni**, **serenibyss**, **Tech22**, **YoungOnion** and **Ghostipedia**) for Horizon. This first slice is **the steam chain**: a boiler, a steam turbine and an electric macerator.

**Implemented so far**

- **The solid boiler** burns a fuel for the mod's `burnTime × 12` ticks (coal: 19,200), heats at +1 °C per 24 ticks up to 500, and from 100 °C makes `120 × temp / 500 / 2` mB of steam per 10 ticks while draining 1 mB of water. It cools at −1 per 45 ticks, vents 4 buckets when full, and **explodes if water returns after a dry spell**, exactly as upstream does.
- **The steam turbine** takes 640 mB of steam and returns 4 mB of distilled water, generating 32 EU/t for 10 ticks.
- **The LV macerator** spends 2 EU/t for 400 ticks (800 EU) to turn one ore into **two crushed ore**, on the mod's own recipe logic.
- **Measured in game:** a watered boiler reaches 428 °C with 211 mB water and 280 mB steam; the turbine banks 2048 EU from 16,000 mB; the macerator sits at progress 290/400 with `recipe_logic_status=working` and holds `gtceu:crushed_iron_ore:2`; an unpowered macerator keeps its ore; `minecraft:gold_ore` is refused; a dry boiler is gone once the water returns.
- **The blocks connect by adjacency** (this jar carries no cable blocks), and `/gtceu status|take|fill` inspects and feeds the machines, with `fill` standing in for pipes because the solid boiler accepts no bucket.

**Not yet ported**

- GUIs and screens (the commands above are the surface for now), ash output and the weather-explosion behaviour;
- pipes, cables, covers and the multiblock machines;
- the material system and everything it generates — the mod's other ~1,555 blockstates and ~2,700 items.

**Licence.** LGPL-3.0: the port ships the LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts and a notice naming the authors, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256; it is a derivative under the same licence and its complete source is published, with no further restriction added.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

projects.name: Guard Villagers
projects.summary: Villages raise iron-armored guards who defend the town and rally when one of their own is hit.
projects.description:
Your villages can fight back. Guard Villagers adds armed guards on top of the villagers a town already has: two for every three residents. Farmers, librarians and toolsmiths keep their trades while patrols form around them.

Guards wear iron armour and carry a sword, a sword and shield, or a crossbow. They hunt hostile mobs, and striking one brings the rest of that village running. Villages share spare guards when one has lost residents, and babies born near a garrison can become guards when it is short-handed.

This release is a sandboxed WebAssembly mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page with nothing to build. It runs on both the client and the server; host and guests need it installed for the same village rules to apply. Built on the pinned Horizon `0b14f8a` SDK.

*WebAssembly mods are sandboxed and cannot touch your files or the network.*

Source and build guide: https://github.com/CGRLabs/guard-villagers/tree/v0.8.0-hmod/hmod

versions.changelog: First WebAssembly `.hmod` release after the `.hnmod` format was retired. Full village grouping, guard hiring, iron gear, combat goals, baby promotion and surplus rebalancing ported to the mod API. Combat goals are now installed once per live entity rather than on every server tick, so a loaded village no longer grows its goal selectors without bound, and village reassignment clears every coordinate tag so a guard can no longer read back a mixed village key. 15 unit tests, source check and signed package check pass.

projects.name: Do a Barrel Roll
projects.summary: Fly an elytra like an aircraft, with banked turns and adjustable camera roll.
projects.description:
Fly an elytra like an aircraft. Do a Barrel Roll swaps Horizon's locked horizon for six-degree-of-freedom control: bank into a roll, pull through it to carve a turn, push the nose past vertical and loop.

An independent implementation for Horizon, named after the Java Edition mod that popularised elytra aerobatics. It is not that mod and shares no code, assets or data with it: this is written from scratch against Horizon's native hook points, with its own flight model.

| While gliding | What it does |
|---|---|
| Mouse left / right | Roll, with no snap-back |
| Mouse up / down | Pitch through your current bank, so a wing-down pull carves a turn |
| `A` / `D` | Rudder yaw for fine heading corrections |

In third person your avatar, elytra and held item stay pinned to the camera while the world rolls around you. When you stop gliding, the view eases back to level and the mouse is an ordinary camera again.

**Options > Mods > Do a Barrel Roll > Config** now has real settings: Invert Y, Bank strength and Max bank. The old fake keybind rows are gone. Invert Y negates only the pitch input, so it works with the banked flight model instead of fighting it.

This is a native `.hmod` pinned to Horizon `0b14f8acfd97fa2c750e42795249dcc981178ca4` and horizon-mixins `e59da9094f0c2fdda6c627fe9eff22dec6a906f0`. Native mods are unsandboxed code running with your account's permissions; install only from authors you trust.

Source and build guide: https://github.com/CGRLabs/gyro/tree/v1.9.0-hmod/hmod

Replaces fake keybind rows with real settings, adds an Invert Y toggle, corrects the mixin paths for the current `.game-area` layout, and pins the exact SDK and mixins revisions. The invert-Y mixin now negates all three `yo` reads of `turn_player` (studio freecam, look rotation, held-lead history) instead of declaring one and failing the access count. The package ships the MIT licence notice. 6/6 unit tests, source check and signed package check pass.

projects.name: Horizonmatica
projects.summary: Litematica for Horizon: schematics as ghost blocks, a verifier, material lists and a printer that builds the missing blocks for you.
projects.description:
Horizonmatica is a re-creation of **Litematica** (with its **printer**) for Horizon. Load a schematic, see it as ghost blocks in your world, check your build against it, get a material list, and let the printer place the missing blocks.

## Features
- **Formats:** `.litematic` (versions 1–7, several regions), `.schem` (Sponge v1–v3: WorldEdit, FAWE, Amulet, Axiom), `.schematic` (MCEdit / WorldEdit up to 1.12) and vanilla structure `.nbt`. Older files are upgraded with Horizon's data fixer, the same way old worlds are.
- **Overlay:** missing blocks as translucent real block models (chests, banners, heads and other block entities included), optionally visible through walls.
- **Verifier:** wrong block (red), wrong state (orange), extra block (pink), plus a progress HUD.
- **Layers:** all / one layer / above / below / range.
- **Placements:** several at once; move, rotate, mirror, show or hide each; a move mode for mouse wheel and arrow keys. The placements are remembered per world and dimension and restored when you join again.
- **Save your own:** select an area with the selection tool (a stick: left and right click set the corners, the wheel grows and moves the box) and save it as a `.litematic` (blocks and their states), chunk by chunk as in Litematica: chunks not loaded yet show as frames to fly to.
- **Material list:** missing, total and carried, with item icons, in the HUD or in the menu, and copied to the clipboard as a table for spreadsheets.
- **Menu (M):** a screen of its own, drawn with the game's widgets. Every action is a key mapping of the game, bound in Options › Controls; the settings are on the mod's page in Options › Mods too.
- **Pick block:** middle-click a ghost block to take that block in hand, for building by hand.
- **Easy place:** look at a ghost block and its block is taken in hand; hold the right mouse button to place it, facing the right way. While it is on, only the schematic's blocks can be placed. Its own *air place* option (off by default) places ghost blocks without a neighbour.
- **Highlights:** mark missing and wrong blocks through everything, however far away, for all items or just one you pick in the material list.
- **Printer:** places one missing block within reach every few ticks, from the bottom up. It only clicks when Horizon's own placement logic says the click produces exactly the wanted state (stairs, slabs, logs, furnaces…). Redstone-aware order, repeater, comparator and note block setup after placing, double slabs and stacks, chests, falling blocks. The camera never moves.

Usage: put schematics into `schematics/` next to `options.txt` of your instance (`/hm folder` shows the path), then `/hm load <name>` or press **M**. All commands and keys are in the [README](https://github.com/keksi2k/horizonmatica#usage).

## What it does and doesn't do
- **Reads** only files in the instance's `schematics/` folder, and creates that folder if it's missing.
- **Writes** only the `.litematic` files you save (`/hm save`), into that folder. Settings go through Horizon's mod settings, remembered placements into the mod's own data folder that Horizon gives it.
- **Network:** no connections of its own. The only thing sent to a server is what the printer and easy place do: the same block-placing clicks a player would make (with the matching look direction), and hotbar slot changes.
- **"Open folder"** in the menu (and `/hm folder`) starts the system's file manager on the schematics folder (`explorer`, `open` or `xdg-open`); nothing else is ever started.
- No telemetry, no downloads, no code run from schematic files. Schematics are parsed as data only.

⚠️ On other people's servers, automatic placing may break the rules or trip anti-cheat. The printer is off until you turn it on (`K` or `/hm printer on`). The *air place* options of the printer and easy place (off by default) are noticed by anti-cheat plugins such as Grim.

**Version:** Horizonmatica is a `.hmod` on Horizon's mod API. The overlay, the printer and easy place also use game internals, so it is pinned to one Horizon build (currently Nightly 2026-11-20, `0a875da`). A new Nightly needs a new release.

## Credits
The idea, the way it's used, the file format and the behaviour come from **[Litematica](https://github.com/maruohon/litematica)** by masa (maruohon), maintained by **[Sakura-Ryoko](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/litematica)**, and from **[Litematica Printer](https://github.com/aleksilassila/litematica-printer)** by aleksilassila. Horizonmatica is not an official project of these authors, isn't made or endorsed by them, and contains none of their code. Only the file format and the behaviour are re-created. If you like it, go and support the originals.

MIT licensed.

versions.changelog:
### Added
- The whole mod speaks the game's language: the menu, the HUD, the chat messages, the printer's notes, the settings (Options › Mods) and the keys (Options › Controls) are in English, French, German and Spanish (Spain and Mexico), and follow Options › Language at once.
- Material lists, the HUD and the printer use the game's own item and block names in your language.

### Changed
- Horizonmatica is now a `.hmod` built on Horizon's mod API (`horizon-mod.toml`). Launchers from 0.2.70 on load only `.hmod` packages, so 0.3.x (`.hnmod`) no longer installs there.
- Commands, chat output and completions, the HUD, settings, keys, mouse input and the menu go through the mod API. Game internals are used only where the API has nothing for it: the overlay (the game's renderer and full block models), the printer and easy place (clicking a chosen face, the game's placement prediction) and the data fixer for older schematics.
- Keys are now the game's key mappings: bind them in Options › Controls. The menu's Keys tab is gone, and keys bound there in 0.3 are not carried over (the defaults are the same).
- The menu (M) is a mod screen of its own instead of borrowing the Debug Options screen; **1–7** switch its tabs. Tabs take the width their names need, long button labels are cut with "..." and shown whole as a tooltip, and the Display tab and the credits scroll on small windows.
- Settings are registered with Horizon and also shown on the mod's page in Options › Mods. Settings and remembered placements from 0.3 are carried over.
- The package carries the MIT license text and names its license, home page and issue tracker.
- Old MCEdit `.schematic` files: 1.12's numeric block ids are mapped by the game's own data fixer; the mod no longer bundles a copy of that table.

### Fixed
- Opened a second time, the menu's origin and corner fields were empty until the placement moved.

Thanks to Fenrur, whose port brought up the scrolling Display tab and the French page.

Built for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da).

projects.name: hostilenetworks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of hostilenetworks.
projects.description:
A port of [Hostile Neural Networks](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Hostile-Neural-Networks) by Shadows_of_Fire for Horizon — the Simulation Chamber and the Loot Fabricator.

**Implemented so far**

- **Simulation Chamber** (`hostilenetworks:sim_chamber`): a model plus one input and one output slot, a 2,000,000 FE buffer, the jar's runtime/prediction arithmetic and its failure states; a finished run yields the model's predicted drop.
- **Loot Fabricator** (`hostilenetworks:loot_fabricator`): a model in one slot and 16 output slots, a 1,000,000 FE buffer, the jar's per-model selection and its 60-tick × 256 FE cost per drop.
- Both machines' block entities, fill-only energy capability on all faces, menus, screens, persistence, six data slots for the chamber and five for the fabricator (runtime, selection, model index, both halves of the FE count).
- The carried models/drops/tags/lang and the creative tab, plus `/hostilenetworks info` and the administrative commands.

**Not yet ported**

- Kill/break model upgrades (`data_gained`, the `living_death` hook, the Deep Learner scan), blank-model attunement and the Model Framework's use.
- The other 58 entity and 10 block models, their optional drops and the silk-touch upgrade conditions.
- The Deep Learner (curio, menu, HUD), the Fabrication Directive, the Data Center multiblock with queue and redstone modes, training mode's model-data upgrades, the generalized predictions and the `living_matter` recipes.
- The chamber/fabricator GUI textures and the model-rendering item.

All commands that change a machine or grant a model are **operator-only**; only `/hostilenetworks info` is open to players.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/hostilenetworks/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with the upstream MIT notice) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, training mode's model-data upgrades. A finished training run now upgrades the model by one data point, produces no base drop and no prediction, and costs the jar's 300 ticks at 1.2x — measured in game as an energy fall of exactly 299 ticks times 154 FE with the finishing tick free, `fail input`, and the model reading 20 to 21. A self-aware model refuses to start (`fail cannot_train`, runtime 0, input not consumed, energy unchanged), which is upstream's own rule. The slice also fixes a real defect: 0.2.1's training run produced the inference loot and left the model's data untouched. A flaw in the unpublished 0.2.2 is corrected too — it stamped an explicit `data: 0` on a model after an inference run, and the data write is now gated on a gain. Two gaps were checked against the artefact and deliberately left: the kill/break data path needs the Deep Learner's item container, and attunement is blocked because the entity-interact hooks carry no player at this pin. Proven in game: all three carried recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and two negative controls stay empty, every carried item gives and reads back with an unknown id refused, and both machines drop to a survival pickaxe beside a vanilla stone-to-cobblestone differential.

projects.name: iceandfire
projects.summary: A fire dragon end to end: its egg hatches in flame and the dragon takes flight.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Ice and Fire Community Edition](https://github.com/IAFEnvoy/IceAndFire-CE) (LGPL-3.0, by **IAFEnvoy**, **xiaowu** and **uoay**) for Horizon. This first slice is **one fire dragon, end to end**: its egg, its hatching and its flight.

**Implemented so far**

- **The fire dragon egg** (`iceandfire:dragonegg_red` places `iceandfire:dragon_egg`) ages only while the egg's block is on fire, exactly as the mod's `DragonEggEntity` does: one step per 100 ticks, 72 steps, and the progress is stored in the block state so it survives a reload.
- **Hatching** at the mod's own `eggBornTime` of 7200 ticks turns the cell to air and summons one **tamed, owned and homed** `iceandfire:fire_dragon`, with the mod's health (500 × 0.04 = 20).
- **Flight:** the dragon hovers at the mod's +0.08 blocks/tick, and a wild dragon pursues the nearest player within 128 blocks at 0.78 blocks/tick, holding at the 2-block tackle reach.

**Not yet ported**

- fire breath and biting: mobs cannot damage or mount at this pin, so combat and riding are out of reach for now, and the port supplies the AI itself because the goal registry is still a draft API;
- the other 21 entity types (ice and lightning dragons, hippogryphs, cyclops, sea serpents, pixies and the rest) and the other 11 egg colours;
- dragon growth, hunger, loot, sounds and the mod's own model (the dragon draws with the wandering trader's until the mob-submit hook exists);
- dragon roosts and the mod's ore and gear families.

**Licence.** LGPL-3.0: the port ships the LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts and a notice naming the authors, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256; it is a derivative under the same licence and its complete source is published, with no further restriction added.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the dragon's bite: a wild dragon that reaches the target it hunts starts the jar's 35-tick bite animation and lands one hit for its attack damage (1.0 at age 0); a tamed dragon never does. The whole slice is rules the existing entity tick already runs, with the numbers read from upstream at this version. The port's first in-game leg rides with it and proves each family: four bites take the player from 20.0 to 16.0 one point at a time while a tamed dragon at three blocks leaves health unchanged; a killed dragon is removed; the egg item, block and an unknown id refused; the flame differential; the 7,200-tick hatch with its tamed flag and owner; and the egg's loot table beside a vanilla barrel. Two engine facts are recorded with their evidence: `EntityRef::tick_count` reads 0 inside the entity tick hook, so the animation counts its own ticks, and the SNBT parser refuses an unquoted namespaced key (`{iceandfire:Tamed:1b}`), so a harness must quote it. A port defect is fixed too: a killed dragon stayed in the world at 0 health because the port cancels the template's tick and the death tick is what removes a mob.

projects.name: I'm Fast

projects.description:
A port of [I'm Fast](https://github.com/Gabriel-Hiss/Im-Fast) by Gabriel Hiss for
Horizon: it lifts the server-side movement checks that pull a player back for
"moved too quickly".

**Implemented so far**

- `player_movement_check` and `elytra_movement_check` are switched off once per

- Verified with a real LAN guest: a 200-block move is kept while the rules are
  off and refused when they are back on.

**Not yet ported**

- The two "moved wrongly" thresholds (player and vehicle) and the vehicle speed
  limit: Horizon has no rule for them, and the hooks that could patch them are
  not stamped yet.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to
Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining thresholds
is welcome.
