projects.name: InControl!
projects.summary: Spawn and loot control driven by two JSON rule files a pack author edits by hand: config/incontrol/spawn.json denies a fresh mob by id, mod, dimension,…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of InControl 1.21-10.3.0, the server-side rule engine a pack author drives with two hand-edited JSON files: `config/incontrol/spawn.json` cancels mob spawns and `config/incontrol/loot.json` rewrites the drops of a mob or a block. The package carries no blocks, items or assets, only the rules engine and the hooks that drive it. Upstream: https://github.com/McJtyMods/InControl — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The spawn engine reads `spawn.json` top to bottom, matches a rule only when every condition in it matches, and lets the first match decide unless the rule says `"continue": true`.
- Spawn conditions cover `when` (`position` for natural attempts, `onjoin` for every fresh mob), `mob` and `mod`, `dimension`, `minheight` and `maxheight`, and block and sky light through `minlight`, `maxlight`, `minlight_sky` and `maxlight_sky`.
- The results `deny`, `deny_with_actions`, `allow` and `default` are honoured, and any other word denies as upstream does.
- The loot engine reads `loot.json` and denies, replaces or adds the drops of a mob or a broken block, with `drops`, `add`, `replace`, `remove` and `result`, the `item` and `removeall` aliases, looting-scaled `itemcount` tiers, and a per-drop `nbt` object applied as `minecraft:custom_data`.
- A rule that uses a key this port cannot evaluate is inert and reported by `/incontrol reload`, so a rule it cannot read in full never denies more than its author asked.
- A broken rule file is refused and the rules already in force stay, so a typo cannot silently un-deny every spawn.
- `/incontrol reload` and `/incontrol status` work at permission level 1, and the JSON parser is bounded to 32 levels so a deeply nested imported file is refused instead of overflowing the stack.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control run that fails at the first rule assertion.

**Not yet ported**

- `minlight_full`, `maxlight_full` and the `light` expression stay inert, because they subtract the sky darkening value and the pin has no probe for it.
- `biome` and `biometags` are unavailable, because the pin exposes no biome read outside client-side colour refresh, and `mob: "#tag"` cannot match, because entity-type tags do not exist at the pin.
- `finalize` rules for equipment, health, AI and NBT are absent, because the entity-write APIs they need are not exposed, and `despawn` rules are absent because there is no despawn hook.
- Phases, random rolls, counts, distance, difficulty, weather, cave and slime checks, structure and area tests, block tests and scoreboard conditions are outside this slice.
- The other rule files are not read: summon-aid `spawner.json`, events, experience, effects, break, place and click rules.
- The pre-join veto redesign is not implemented, which is also why a denied natural spawn can still leave a jockey behind.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: First publication in the SDK format.

projects.name: industrialforegoing
projects.summary: A Horizon port of industrialforegoing.
projects.description:
A port of [Industrial Foregoing](https://github.com/Buuz135/Industrial-Foregoing) by Buuz135 for Horizon — slice 1, the Water Condensator.

**Implemented so far**

- `industrialforegoing:water_condensator` on the iron-block template (hardness 5.0, blast 6.0, iron sounds) with Titanium's four-way `subfacing` state and the jar's own four-variant blockstate; placement turns it toward the placer.
- A 10,000 FE buffer through the block energy capability (any side may fill or drain it) and a 16,000 mB **drain-only** water tank through the fluid capability, both saved in the block entity.
- The condensation rule from the jar: with fewer than 2 water sources on the six sides nothing happens; with 2 or more and at least 1,000 FE it makes `sources × 100` mB for 1,000 FE on a 10-tick cooldown; with 2 or more and under 1,000 FE it makes `sources × 50` mB for free on a 50-tick cooldown. A full tank clamps the water and the operation still spends its FE, as upstream's `fillForced` does.
- The carried blockstate, both block models, the item model, five textures, the lang strings, the loot table, the advancement and its recipe. The recipe accepts the jar's ingredient **tags** alongside vanilla fallbacks (`#c:gears/iron` or an iron block, `#c:plastics` or a slime ball, `#industrialforegoing:machine_frame/pity` or an iron block), so the machine is craftable standalone while other mods' gears and plastics still count.

**Not yet ported**

- **No GUI:** the jar's Titanium bars are not carried; the buffer, tank and rule are read through commands.
- **The rest of the mod:** the other generators and processors, the laser drill and lenses, the mob duplicator/slaughterhouse, plant and interaction machines, conveyors, the ore-washer/fermentation chain, the infinity tools, the enchantment applicator and the guide book.
- No fluid inputs (nothing in this slice consumes a fluid) and no config file.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/industrialforegoing/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 5, the dissolution chamber: the machine that gives the mod's whole item set a source, including the three higher machine frames and all sixteen lenses that until now could only be given as items. It has its own recipe type read as data, eleven slots, two fluid tanks and its own timing, and the fluids it needs are declared and written the way a mod fluid has to be at this pin, then proved through the declared capability rather than by reading the block entity. Proven in game end to end: twenty-three recipes load and the readout says so; two thousand millibuckets of latex enter the tank and answer through the capability; a white lens takes exactly a hundred ticks, spends exactly a hundred times ninety FE and two hundred and fifty millibuckets, and produces one lens from five consumed inputs; an empty tank leaves the recipe unstarted with its energy untouched, and filling it starts the run; a hopper empties the output into a barrel; the simple frame's three hundred ticks spend ninety FE a tick; and the advanced frame is made from the plastics tag, a crafted diamond gear and the simple frame, which is exactly the chain an add-on was waiting on. Two harness facts cost runs and are recorded: a container command writes the window's copy and never reaches a machine's server slots, and the End's mobs will kill the player mid-scenario unless difficulty is peaceful.

projects.name: industrialforegoingsouls
projects.summary: A Horizon port of industrialforegoingsouls.
projects.description:
A port of [Industrial Foregoing Souls](https://github.com/InnovativeOnlineIndustries/Industrial-Foregoing-Souls) by Buuz135 and Rid. Requires [industrialforegoing](https://github.com/AdLf0208/industrialforegoing) 0.2.7 or later, which provides the blue laser lens and the laser drill ore recipe type it registers against.

The first port of Industrial Foregoing Souls, and the three blocks are one mechanic: a laser base that turns a warden in range into souls, pipes that move them, and a surge that spends them to accelerate a block. The gate is the parent's own: the base produces nothing until a blue laser lens sits in its catalyst slot, which is exactly how the jar gates it. Proven in game with that differential in one run: sixty ticks with no lens leaves the bar at zero and the warden at full health, seating the lens makes four operations land sixteen damage and eight souls, and pulling the lens freezes the tank for the next sixty ticks. The pipes move four and then eight souls at one transfer a tick, and the surge takes a wheat crop from age zero to age four with random ticks disabled while its own counter falls from two hundred and ninety-three to two hundred and merely waits while it has no signal. Three recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and each block drops itself. Two of the agent's own expectations were wrong against upstream and were corrected in the test rather than in the code, which is the right way round: a nearly full tank still fires and clamps, and a surge facing nothing still spends its ticks.

versions.changelog: This version fixes a join the port had been drawing wrong: a soul pipe beside the laser base showed no arm, because the tag the package generates named only the pipe and the surge, and at this pin a join is decided by that tag rather than by code. The reference joins a pipe to a soul handler, so the base belongs in the tag, and one line of generated data is the whole fix. Proven in game by reading the pipe's own block state with each neighbour: a pipe beside a pipe joins to the east, a pipe beside stone shows nothing on that side, and the same cell reads joined once the laser base replaces the stone, in both placement orders, and beside a surge as well. The base itself carries no pipe property, so the join belongs to the pipe. The negative run asserts the joined side reads false and fails, which is what makes the positive reading evidence.

projects.name: industrialization_overdrive
projects.summary: A Horizon port of industrialization_overdrive.
projects.description:
Requires [Modern Industrialization](https://github.com/AdLf0208/modern_industrialization) 0.2.3 or later: the pyrolyse oven's multiblock is built from that mod's casings, coils and hatches, and the package declares it as a required dependency, so the game refuses this mod by name when the parent is absent.

A port of [industrialization_overdrive](https://github.com/WhitePhant0m/Industrialization-Overdrive).

The first port of Industrialization Overdrive, and it opens with the machine the mod is named around: the pyrolyse oven, a thirty-three member multiblock of seventeen bronze plated bricks and sixteen coil blocks with item, fluid and energy hatches, which turns four logs into five charcoal and proxies the parent's own coke recipes. The parent surface it binds to went from nothing to complete across three slices of its own: the shell blocks, the hatches, the energy aggregation and a coke recipe kind another package can read, which is why this slice needed no hard-coded recipe table. Proven in game with the numbers that matter: the shell forms with three hatches and nothing missing, four logs and exactly twelve thousand eight hundred FE through the hatches make five charcoal with the controller and hatch both emptied, and twelve thousand seven hundred and eighty makes nothing and stalls at nine hundred and ninety-eight of a thousand, so the energy is coming from the hatch rather than from nowhere. Breaking one coil freezes the run and a brick where the coil belongs stays unformed, and restoring it finishes. A second coil tier reads its own batch size and multiplier and pays its own coke run. The creosote by-product, the oven's own craft recipe and the other four families are recorded with their exact missing symbols rather than approximated.

versions.changelog: This version answers a review with three fixes, and the first one is the interesting kind: the hatch moved items by the registered stack limit rather than the stack's own, and it ignored whether either write succeeded. Now a read that fails is never taken for an empty slot, the limit comes from the stack's own component when it has one, and a move only counts when both writes report a change, so a refused write rolls the whole tick back instead of leaving one side changed. Proven in game both ways: twelve of a sixteen-limited stack beside eight of the same moves exactly four and keeps four, and a state the boundary refuses consumes nothing on either side. The second fix validates the whole craft result before anything is spent, including a recipe with two distinct results, which this oven's shipped data never produces but a data pack can declare over either the machine's own type or the proxied one, so the guard is proved against an installed pack rather than against a hypothetical. The third removes the inventory diagnostic outright rather than gating it, because operator commands cannot be shown to refuse in this harness, and the vanilla data command prints the same items with their components.

projects.name: Integrated Crafting
projects.summary: A port of Integrated Crafting for Horizon: a Crafting Interface block that accepts crafting jobs, resolves each against the game's own crafting recipes,…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Integrated Crafting 1.8.1, the autocrafting add-on for Integrated Dynamics. This slice is the crafting-job engine and its Crafting Interface: a request for N of an item is resolved against the game's own crafting recipes, the ingredients are held in the interface's slots, and one recipe is crafted at a time. Upstream: https://github.com/CyclopsMC/IntegratedCrafting — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The block `integratedcrafting:part_interface_crafting` is a part-shaped plate with a 13-slot container: nine ingredient slots laid out as a crafting grid and four result slots, with hoppers above and beside it as the ordinary route.
- The job engine resolves a request to a `minecraft:crafting` recipe, computes `ceil(requested / output)`, and reserves the whole job's ingredients at submission, refusing with the exact deficit when the slots cannot pay.
- A craft takes 20 ticks, and ingredients are consumed and the result inserted only on the tick it completes, so a craft that cannot finish costs nothing.
- A job that cannot continue blocks with a reason (`missing` with the deficit, or `output full`) and retries every tick, a finished job leaves the queue, and the queue is capped at eight jobs.
- An idle interface answers `Unchanged` from its tick, so it does not dirty its chunk or notify comparators.
- `/integratedcrafting status <x> <y> <z>` reads the queue, the running craft and the blocked reason, and `/integratedcrafting request|cancel|feed` work within six blocks of the interface, where `feed` moves the player's own items rather than creating any.
- The carried content is the interface texture and model geometry, a blockstate, an item model, the block declaration, a loot table, a creative tab and a recipe in 26.3's ingredient form.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control run that fails without it and a selftest that inverts the craft count.

**Not yet ported**

- The network half is `blocked(no-parent-network-attachment-api)`: a part on the Integrated Dynamics cable, the network's recipe list and its item storage, because the parent exports no API and its cable's face properties are a closed enum.
- The variable-card layer and the Crafting Writer part are `blocked(no-variable-card-layer)`, and so are the attuned and enumerated interface variants.
- The five part screens are not carried, since this slice has the container and the commands but no GUI.
- The job dependency graph is missing, so a request whose ingredient is itself craftable is refused as missing ingredients; this is the largest remaining piece of the engine.
- Priorities, distributed jobs over several interfaces, several crafting CPUs, blocking modes, reusable ingredients, fluids and energy are not implemented, and neither is inserting the inputs into the machine the interface faces.
- Recipe types other than `minecraft:crafting` are unsupported, because stonecutting, smelting and smithing recipes expose no ingredient and result lists this engine can read.
- Advancements, the info book and the gametests are not carried, and stack components are not preserved through a job, since the slots keep an item id and a count.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the job dependency graph: a request that needs a crafted intermediate now plans the intermediate first instead of refusing with missing ingredients. A request for four sticks from one log plans planks, then sticks, and the log's surplus feeds back into the simulation; a dependency failure aborts with the pieces it lacked, and a recursive chain is refused. The rewrite follows the jar's semantics — dependencies resolved before the parent exists — with the deviations stated rather than hidden: a chain is the steps of one job, there is no network across interfaces, and the depth bound is eight. This version also fixes a real duplication bug the exact-count assertions exposed: the mirror held the pre-write container state and the result slots were never merged back, so a hopper under the interface refilled and drained the same stack every tick, and an eight-plank job reported twelve planks. Both halves now merge against the written state and the counts are pinned at eight, four and one. Proven in game: the plan is accepted, the sticks are crafted from the planned planks, the chest holds exactly one of the requested item, and the same run with the parent item present crafts the carried interface recipe from its tag ingredients.

projects.name: integrateddynamics
projects.summary: A Horizon port of integrateddynamics.
projects.description:
A port of [Integrated Dynamics](https://github.com/CyclopsMC/IntegratedDynamics) (MIT, by rubensworks / kroeser) for Horizon. This first slice is the **logic cable** with a redstone reader and a redstone writer part — upstream's `redstone_transmission` without the variable-card layer.

**Implemented so far**

- `integrateddynamics:cable`, a non-occluding 4 px core (`CableModel.MIN..MAX`, hardness 3.0) with six `part_<face>` enum properties (`none|reader|writer`), a `status` property (`inactive|active`), a block entity holding the network channel, and the carried model, texture, language and recipe inside the one `.hnmod`.
- The **redstone reader** part and the **redstone writer** part: right-click a cable face with the part item to place one (a face already holding a part refuses), and `/integrateddynamics part <pos> <face> none` removes it. Every writer on a connected cable network emits the network's channel value on its own face; the network's channel is the strongest reading any reader on it produced.
- The network walk: a bounded flood fill over connected cables (the safety cap counts **cables**, as it should — a long sparse line keeps its whole 1024-cable budget), recomputed after the level tick for the cables whose block entity ticked.
- Placement rotation for the parts, the carried `part_redstone_reader`/`part_redstone_writer` items, and `/integrateddynamics` readout commands for the harness.

**Known limitation (an API gap, disclosed rather than faked)**

- The reader samples the **strongest redstone signal around the cable**, not the block on the reader's own face: `native_neighbor_signal(dimension, pos)` is the only signal reader at this pin (API 96), and nothing returns "the signal block X gives on face F". A reader next to a lever and a wire therefore reads the strongest of the six neighbours rather than its own face. Directional sampling needs a per-face signal helper; it is recorded in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 as a gap, and the entry claimed face-specific behaviour before this slice was corrected.

**Not yet ported**

- The **variable system**: variable store, logic programmer, materializer, proxy, delay, variable cards and transformers — the whole typed value layer.
- Every other part (inventory, fluid, energy, entity, machine, world, audio, network, effect, panel, connector), the facade and fake-cable placement, and the display panel.
- The screens (part settings, writer aspect card slot, display panel).
- Energy consumption of parts and the network's power (upstream's `getConsumptionRate`).
- The menril resource chain (log, wood, chunk smelting, squeezer, basin) beyond the carried blocks.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/integrateddynamics/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the World Reader (`integrateddynamics:part_world_reader`). It is the same cable-block-entity-holds-parts shape slice 1 established, and it reads world state only the server can answer: light, weather and the day cycle. Six of the mod's 14 World aspects are carried — the ones whose value fits a redstone channel exactly (a boolean becomes 15/0, light 0..15); the other eight need the typed value layer and stay not ported. A placed part defaults to `light`, and the operator command `/integrateddynamics aspect <pos> <face> <aspect>` selects another. This version also repairs the fit gate: the local `Parts` type was renamed `PartSlots`, so `fits` no longer records an SDK literal at a local site and `0b14f8a fits` is true again. Proven in game: a cable carrying a world reader answers with its aspect's redstone level, and the control game without the package refuses the block.

projects.name: integratedtunnels
projects.summary: A Horizon port of integratedtunnels.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Integrated Tunnels 1.13.0, the item, fluid and energy transport add-on for Integrated Dynamics. This slice is the item tunnel: an Item Importer pulls items out of the inventory behind a cable face into the network's store, an Item Exporter hands them out again, and `/integratedtunnels info` reads the cable back. Upstream: https://github.com/CyclopsMC/IntegratedTunnels — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The package adds the carrier block `integratedtunnels:tunnel_cable`, a 4 px non-occluding core with six `part_<face>` properties and a block entity holding the network's item store.
- Two part items, `integratedtunnels:part_importer_item` and `part_exporter_item`, are placed on a clicked cable face and consumed outside creative, and `/integratedtunnels part` covers a face that is not clickable.
- An importer moves up to 64 items a tick into the store and an exporter hands up to 64 a tick into the inventory behind its own face, while whatever the destination refuses stays in the store.
- The network is the connected cable set (six-way adjacency, bounded to 1,024 cables), its store lives on the network's root cable, and importers run before exporters so items can leave the tick they arrive.
- A stack that carries components or damage is left in its container rather than flattened to an id and a count, so a filled shulker is never silently rebuilt.
- The launcher-built package was proven in game: import runs at the jar's rate, export loses nothing, and removing either part stops its half of the loop.

**Not yet ported**

- The variable and aspect layer is not ported — variable cards, the aspect screen and the other six item aspects — because it needs the parent's variable system, which the Integrated Dynamics port does not carry.
- The fluid and energy parts and their channels are absent, since the parent has neither a fluid nor an energy network.
- The world parts and the block break and place handlers are absent, because they need a fake player the pin does not expose.
- The interface parts, the player simulator, the part screens, the part-removal path and the jar's `error` state are not carried.
- Network energy is not modelled, and neither is NBT fidelity in the store, which keeps an id and a count per entry.
- Cable interop with the sibling Integrated Dynamics port is impossible, because two packages cannot share a namespace and that port's cable enumerates only its own part kinds.
- The two part recipes, advancements, the info book and the multipart renderer are not carried.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the fluid tunnel: a fluid importer and a fluid exporter on a tunnel cable face, plus a slotless fluid channel beside the item store. It is the jar's own face-mounted protocol — the same carrier and the same once-per-part tick move — with the rate defaulting to 1,000 mB. The energy half is deliberately not taken: the pin has no vanilla FE block to feed or drain, so a transfer could not be given a fail-capable in-game assertion, and an untestable transfer is worse than a stated gap. Proven in game: a full water cauldron behind a fluid importer drains into the channel as 1,000 mB and the source becomes an empty cauldron; a fluid exporter fills an empty cauldron to level 3 with the channel back to zero and the thousand millibuckets conserved; removing the exporter leaves the channel full and the sink empty while removing the importer leaves a refilled source full; both fluid part ids give and read back; and the carried loot table rolls the cable. The readout had to become marker-based because the chat history caps at a hundred lines and the old count-based wait saturated once the fluid phases ran.

projects.name: inventory_blur
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Inventory Blur.
projects.description:
A Rust port of [Inventory Blur](https://github.com/Enchanted-Games/inventory-blur)
(Enchanted_Games / ioblackshaw, CC BY-NC 4.0): applies the 1.20.5+ menu
background blur to in-world inventories (chests, the player inventory and
other Screen-extended menus) instead of the vanilla dark gradient.

The 1:1 core (ModConstants, the Logging wrapper, ModEntry, the loader
entrypoints and ScreenMixin's renderTransparentBackground replacement:
skip the vanilla dark gradient entirely, apply the blur once per frame
when the render state's first stratum after blur is still unset, then
tile the bundled inworld_inventory_background.png over the menu) runs
inside the mod API wiring (Horizon f00125f61f, mixins e59da909, api 0.2).
Upstream holds no config file, so there are no settings to register.

The draw itself waits on horizon-rust/horizon#19349, the screen-render
hook the port needs (first filed as #10131, closed 2026-11-06 without
the surface landing in the SDK). Until it lands the screens draw
vanilla's gradient.

Source-only .hmod with the full port source and the texture asset.

Licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-inventory-blur

projects.name: ironjetpacks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of ironjetpacks.
projects.description:
A port of [Iron Jetpacks](https://github.com/BlakeBr0/IronJetpacks) by BlakeBr0 for Horizon — slice 2, the iron tier with an item-backed tank.

**Implemented so far**

- `ironjetpacks:jetpack`, the 26.1 single jetpack item fixed to the iron tier: a chest item (right-click equips it), unbreakable, stack size 1, armor 3, with the upstream item model and texture.
- **Flight:** while the jetpack is in the chest slot and the jump key is held the player rises, at `min(motionY + accel, speedVert) × throttle × sprint` with the upstream acceleration, cap, water and sprint rules; thrust ticks also zero the fall distance.
- **Engine switch and tank:** an 800,000 FE item-backed tank in the stack's own `minecraft:custom_data`, the engine component (off by default, as upstream), and `/ironjetpacks fuel|engine` — `fuel` is operator-only, `engine` is open to the wearer (the pin has no key-to-server action path, so the command is the switch).
- A pure 29-test flight model, the content (item, model, texture, recipes, tags, creative tab), and one `.hnmod` that carries both halves.

**Not yet ported**

- **One item, one tier:** 26.1 uses one `jetpack` item with a `jetpack_id` component and a registry of 14 tiers; the pin's content format cannot register that component, so the item id itself is the tier and only iron-tier components are listed.
- **No HUD/item bar** for the item-backed tank: the charge shows through `/ironjetpacks fuel` only, and the tank has no GUI.
- **Hover is not toggled:** the runtime and its tests cover the branches, but the pin has no keybind or component plumbing to toggle it.
- **Guest input** comes from `player_input` flags; there is still no server-side velocity write for a guest, so guest thrust is one-sided.
- **Horizontal flight** (`moveRelative` with `speedSide`/`sprintSpeed`) is not implemented; sprint's vertical and fuel multipliers are.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/ironjetpacks/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with BlakeBr0's MIT notice) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

projects.name: Item Scroller
projects.summary: Move items with the mouse wheel, sort inventories, refill saved crafting recipes, and repeat villager trades with configurable shortcuts.
projects.description:
## Item Scroller for Horizon

Item Scroller is a client-side inventory utility for Horizon. It adds mouse and keyboard shortcuts for transferring items, sorting inventories, reusing crafting recipes, and repeating villager trades.

### Features

- **Inventory transfers.** Hover over a slot and scroll up to send one item to the other inventory, or scroll down to pull one back. Hold **Shift** to move a stack or **Ctrl** to move matching stacks. Drag across slots to transfer several stacks in one gesture.
- **Inventory sorting.** Press **R** over a supported inventory to merge matching stacks and sort its contents. Choose a sorting method and set custom item priorities.
- **Recipe memory.** Save up to **18 crafting recipes** per Horizon profile. Middle-click a crafting result to save its ingredient layout, then hold **S** and select a saved recipe to refill the grid from your inventory. Additional shortcuts support repeated crafting and moving or dropping the results.
- **Villager trading.** Right-click a trade result to repeat the selected offer with the payment items you have. Middle-click a payable result to save or remove a profile-wide favorite. A star identifies matching favorite trades across villagers.

### Configuration

Gameplay shortcuts start disabled. To use them, turn on **Enable gameplay shortcuts** in **Mods → Item Scroller → Config**. Some multiplayer servers may disallow these shortcuts or flag them with anticheat. Check the server rules before enabling them.

In single-player, pause with **Esc**, then press **Ctrl + Alt + I** to open the keybind editor. On multiplayer servers, use the shortcut while playing. Click a binding to capture a key combination, or open **Options** to select a key and modifiers from a list.

Use **Mods → Item Scroller → Config** to adjust scroll direction, sorting, and individual gameplay features. The shortcuts above are the defaults.

### Requirements and languages

Requires **Horizon mod API 0.2**. Item Scroller runs on the client as a WebAssembly mod.

Available in English, Russian, Spanish, Korean, Dutch, Ukrainian, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

### Credits

The Horizon port is maintained by **caskh**. It is based on **Sakura-Ryoko’s** Java 26.3 branch of the original Item Scroller by **masa**. [Horizon port](https://github.com/caskh/item-scroller) · [Java 26.3 branch](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/itemscroller/tree/26.3) · [Original Java project](https://github.com/maruohon/itemscroller)

versions.changelog: Gameplay shortcuts start disabled and require explicit opt-in. Configuration remains available while shortcuts are off. This update also adds a dedicated keybind editor, bulk villager trades, global trade favorites, and six new translations.

projects.name: Jade for Horizon
projects.summary: Shows what you are looking at: the block or entity under the crosshair, its mod, and details like growth, health and contents.
projects.description:
An unofficial Horizon port of [Jade](https://github.com/Snownee/Jade) by Snownee. Jade is a Java NeoForge mod that can't run in Horizon: this port rewrites its main features in Rust, as a WebAssembly mod on the mod SDK.

A tooltip at the top of the screen shows what the crosshair is on:

- **Blocks**: icon, name, originating mod; crop growth; beehive honey and bees, composter level, respawn anchor charges, farmland moisture, egg hatching, cake slices; redstone power, repeater delay, comparator mode, lever state; note block, jukebox disc, spawner mob; container contents (merged by item, up to 18 icons); furnace and brewing stand progress; whether your held item can harvest the block; a mining progress bar.
- **Entities**: name, health, originating mod; animal growth, breeding cooldown and love mode, time to the next egg; tamed animal owner; horse speed and jump height, llama strength; villager profession and level, zombie villager cure time; active effects; item frame contents; primed TNT fuse.

Numpad 0 shows or hides the tooltip (rebindable in Options > Controls). Theme (Vanilla, Dark, Light, Waila), position, size and one toggle per kind of information are in Options > Mods > Jade for Horizon > Config.

**What it does and doesn't do.** On the client it only reads what the player is looking at and draws on the HUD. Health, animal, villager and horse data, effects, container contents and furnace/brewing progress are only known to the server: when the mod is also installed on the server, the client asks for them a few times per second over the mod's own payloads (`jade_horizon:peek_entity` and `jade_horizon:peek_block`, answered with `jade_horizon:entity_info` and `jade_horizon:block_info`), only for a target within 24 blocks, and the server answers with that target's data. A locked container (vanilla `lock`, on it or on the other half of a double chest) has its contents left out, for every player. Nothing else is sent, and it makes no other network access. Without the mod on the server, the tooltip still works without those lines. It doesn't change the world or any block, item or entity.

Not ported from Jade: its hundreds of integrations with other Java mods (Create, Mekanism…), which have no Horizon counterpart.

Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, like Jade. Jade is the work of Snownee and contributors; the original licence and credits are in the package's LICENSE and NOTICE files. Not affiliated with Snownee.

versions.changelog: First release, for Horizon Nightly 0a875da. A locked container's contents are never sent.

**Implemented so far**

**Not yet ported**

- **No GUI/menu:** upstream opens `GeneratorT1Screen`; this slice has no menu type, so right-click does nothing and the fields are read by command.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the generator's redstone control: the four upstream modes (ignore, low, high, pulse) on `RedstoneControlledBE`, the base-class behaviour every later Just Dire Things machine inherits. Three saved keys, one tick gate, and the payload carries the recorded edge so a pulse fires once per edge. A defect found in the in-game leg and fixed: the tick replied `Unchanged` when nothing burnt, which discarded the recorded falling edge, so the second pulse bought no burn — the reply now persists when anything burnt, a fuel item was pulled, or the redstone control changed. Two of the port's own gap claims were corrected from the jar rather than copied: upstream has no comparator output in 1.5.7, and the mode set is four, not "beyond ignored". Proven in game: high runs only while powered, low freezes while powered, pulse buys 1,500 FE per edge with the stick count falling 4 to 3 to 2 while a held signal buys nothing, and a guest 40 blocks away is refused both commands while one a block away is allowed.

projects.name: Kid Mode
projects.summary: A gentler world: friendly and invulnerable mobs, an invulnerable player, sunny days, nights that pass by themselves, and mobs to tame for their loot.
projects.description:
Kid Mode takes the fear out of the game without taking the game away. Monsters still roam the world, but
they leave you alone. You can't get hurt, animals can't be hurt, and the mobs you'd normally fight can be
befriended instead, tamed and kept as pets that bring you useful things.

It's meant for children who want to build, explore and play with the creatures of the world, and for
parents who'd like them to do that without the scary parts.

## What it does

- **You can't get hurt.** No damage from mobs, falls, fire, lava, drowning or explosions, and no starving.
- **Monsters are friendly.** Zombies, skeletons, creepers, spiders and the rest, even the bosses, never
  chase or attack you. Endermen don't mind being looked at, and wolves, bees and other neutral mobs stay calm.
- **Animals can't be hurt.** Cows, pigs, sheep, horses, fish and the other animals are safe from everything.
- **Tame monsters and animals.** Feed a creature the food it likes (raw meat for a zombie, a flower for a
  creeper, a golden carrot for a cow) and it may become yours. A tamed creature stays where it is, never
  disappears, sparkles now and then, and every few minutes drops something useful: string, bones,
  gunpowder, leather and more.
- **Taming hints.** Look at a creature and a little thought bubble shows what food it likes, or a heart once
  it's tamed. A creature someone else tamed shows that player's face, so everyone can tell whose pet it is.
- **Optional extras**, off unless you turn them on: sunny weather all the time, nights that pass by
  themselves, monsters that can't be hurt either, and an Ender Dragon that can't be hurt.

Every feature can be turned on or off on the mod's settings page in the game (**Options > Mods > Kid Mode**).
The mod speaks English and Polish. The full list of features and their settings is in
[docs/features.md](https://github.com/veinmine/kidmode/blob/main/docs/features.md).

## What works today

Kid Mode 0.11 runs on the newest Horizon. Everything in the list above works, in single player and when
friends join your world. Some smaller touches from earlier versions aren't possible on the new Horizon yet:

- Leads can't be put on monsters, only on the animals the game normally allows.
- Undead monsters still catch fire in daylight (it doesn't hurt them).
- The Elder Guardian's curse still reaches you, and the Ender Dragon still swoops and breathes at you,
  although nothing it does can hurt you.
- The thought bubble grows in and out instead of fading.

## Licence

Copyright © 2026 veinmine. Kid Mode is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or
(at your option) any later version.

projects.summary: A Horizon port of laserbridges.
projects.description:
A port of [Laser Bridges & Doors](https://github.com/Mars-The-Planet/Laser-Bridges-And-Doors) (MIT, by Mars) for Horizon. This first slice is the **laser sources and the beams they project**.

**Implemented so far**

- In scope: the four sources `laser_source_block`, `laser_source_fullblock`, `laser_fence_source_block` and `laser_fence_source_fullblock`, with the upstream state set (`face` × `facing` × `powered` × `color`) and their upstream outlines and powered outlines.
- The two beams `laser_block_powered` and `laser_fence_powered` (unbreakable, light 10, thin collidable plates) that the sources write and clear.
- Placement: the clicked face becomes `face` and the placer's direction `facing`, with the attached variants' sturdy-support requirement.
- The bridge generator: the beam's length, the blocks it cuts through, where an obstruction stops it, and shrinking back when a source is switched off or removed.
- Redstone-driven switching, the carried models, textures, sounds metadata, recipes, loot and language, and the source and beam blocks declared as one content pack inside the `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The two receivers (`laser_attached_receiver`, `laser_attached_receiver_fence`): their blocks, models, textures, lang and recipes, and their redstone output (the colour copy from the laser in front).
- Dyeing a source with a dye or from a dispenser.
- The `laserbridges:on`/`off` playback sounds.
- The `config/laserbridges.json` options (`max_length`, `blocks_cut_through_by_lasers`): the port uses upstream's defaults.
- A colour change mid-line strands the far cells — upstream's exact-state test, kept deliberately.
- Beam blocks are unbreakable like upstream (the bedrock template), so a beam has no drop and no break sound.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/laserbridges/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two receivers: the attached receiver and its fence variant now power on a laser and copy its colour, where slice 1 carried only the sources. A receiver lights the lamp above it and leaves the one behind it dark — upstream's signal-face rule — clears both when the beam goes, stays off when it faces away, does not power from an unpowered source in front, and reports light 0 or a per state like the attached sources do. The fence variant refuses the side a plain stone accepts. Proven in game: all twelve carried recipes craft with their ingredients consumed, both receivers and sources drop themselves on a survival break, and 168 declared states are accepted. One upstream defect is recorded and not reproduced: `IReceiverBlock.updateState` computes "is it looking into me?" from its own state, so its guard can never fire, and the port implements the effective rule instead. The colour tint stays a recorded client-side gap — the state and the signal are asserted, never a visual.

projects.name: laserio
projects.summary: A Horizon port of laserio.
projects.description:
A port of [LaserIO](https://github.com/Direwolf20-MC/LaserIO) by Direwolf20-MC for Horizon — the nodes, the connectors and the item cards.

**Implemented so far**

- `laserio:laser_node` and `laserio:laser_connector`, the network they form through their faces, and one card per side saved in the node's block entity.
- The item card: `insert` (upstream's default) or `extract`, with its channel and amount, placed by right-clicking the node (consumed outside creative).
- After the level tick, each extract card whose 20-tick operation falls on this tick takes the first item type the source side offers — skipping empty earlier slots, so they cannot stall a network — and moves up to its amount into the network's inventories. No destination means no extraction, and a refused item stays in the target's remainder.
- `/laserio info` readout, and the carried blockstates, models, textures, recipes, loot, tags, langs and creative tab.
- The mutation commands (`card`, `remove`, `mode`, `rate`, `face`) are **operator-only** (level 2): the node screen is a gap, so they are an administrative surface rather than something every player may use on any node.

**Not yet ported**

- The node screen (card settings UI), so players cannot yet configure cards by hand.
- Fluid, energy and gas cards, the advanced/wireless connectors, the lasers' rendering, filters and the round-robin/channel modes beyond a single channel.
- The full recipe chain and the guide book.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/laserio/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, channels as routing: a card's channel now decides where its stacks go. Upstream hands a stack only to inserter cards on the same channel and takes nothing when none answers, so until now the port's channel was decorative — every insert endpoint in a network was a destination, and the mod's central routing rule was missing. The service and destination order now carry the channel, the card stores it, and `/laserio channel` sets it. Five carried recipes were dead and are fixed, with their second half: all five used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` ingredient form the pin rejects, and the `c:` tags they name exist in no target data, so even the right shape could not match — the port now declares the seven tags it needs. Proven in game: the five recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and a wrong pattern crafts nothing; a channel-3 extract card fills the channel-3 card 20/20 and leaves the channel-0 card at 0; moving that card to channel 5 makes the extract card take nothing while the source keeps 20; and returning it receives all 20.

projects.name: Learn or Die (Horizon port)
projects.summary: Learn German as you play: a teacher narrates what you do and quizzes you on it, with rewards and penalties.
projects.description:
Learn or Die, ported to Horizon: a German teacher narrates what you do and quizzes you on it.

## What it does

- The teacher says out loud, in German, what you do: mining, building, picking up and dropping items, moving, fighting, eating, the weather and more. The sentence shows on screen with a translation, and his portrait talks along.
- Questions come up as you play: pick the German for the word or sentence shown, or for the phrase you hear, with keys 1 to 4 or the mouse, or type it. The game pauses in single player while a question is open.
- Right answers bring buffs or friendly mobs. Wrong ones bring debuffs, five monsters, lost hearts or death, as you choose, and always death in a Hardcore world. After several wrong answers in a row the angry teacher drops your inventory.
- Every 20 minutes of play an exam asks up to 20 phrases you have met and shows your score.
- The dictionary lists the phrases you know, word by word, with grammar notes and other forms, and plays them normal or slow. Item tooltips show the German noun, and "what is this" names the block or mob you look at.
- Your answers are saved per world. A phrase you know is not asked or said again in that world.

Riding and fishing are said, and rewards and penalties given, in single player and for the host of a LAN world. A short guide opens in your first world. Not ported yet: voice answers, and the HUD's score counter, learned-phrase banner and jingle.

## Install

The port reads the German pack, the voices and the portrait from the official Learn or Die German 0.6.2 jar for Minecraft 26.3, `learn-or-die-german-0.6.2+mc26.3.jar`, from the [official release](https://github.com/Larenlearn/learn-or-die/releases/tag/v0.6.2). It contains none of them itself.

1. Install the mod. It is a native mod, so the launcher compiles it for your instance first.
2. Start the instance. Without the jar, the launcher stops and names the path it expects. Copy the unmodified jar to that path, then start again.

## Keys

N turns the teacher on or off, M mutes the voice, K switches between normal and slow speech, I opens the settings, J the dictionary, U the guide, and V says what you are looking at. 1 to 4 answer a question and Enter checks a typed answer. All but 1 to 4, Enter and Esc can be changed in Controls, Key Binds.

## Settings

Press I in a world: question type and frequency, penalties and rewards, the angry teacher, the exam, speech speed and volume, tooltips, and which actions the teacher talks about. They are saved to `config/learnordie.json` in the instance folder, with the original's setting names and defaults.

## Credits and support

Learn or Die is made by Laren. Website: [learnordie.me](https://learnordie.me). Official mod: [github.com/Larenlearn/learn-or-die](https://github.com/Larenlearn/learn-or-die). This port is made with Laren's [permission](https://github.com/Larenlearn/learn-or-die/issues/17), and like the original it is All Rights Reserved.

For problems with the port, open an issue in [its repository](https://github.com/y0sif/learn-or-die-horizon/issues). For everything else, see the official mod.

versions.changelog: First release: the teacher's narration, quizzes, rewards and penalties, the angry teacher, exams, the dictionary, tooltips, naming what you look at, the guide and the settings screen, with the German pack. Built for Horizon 8f83e5c (nightly 2026-11-21).

projects.name: little_big_redstone
projects.summary: A microchip block that runs redstone logic on its circuit board.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Little Big Redstone](https://github.com/Swedz/Little-Big-Redstone) (MIT, by **Swedz**) for Horizon. This first slice is **one microchip** with the mod's own AND scene — two input ports, a 2-input AND gate, one output port and three wires.

**Implemented so far**

- **The microchip block.** The jar makes the microchip the *block* and the logic components *items on its circuit board*, so the slice is a placed microchip that holds a circuit: two input ports, a 2-input AND gate, one output port and three wires, saved in the block entity.
- **The guide's own scene runs in game:** inputs `0,0`, `0,1` and `1,0` leave the lamp dark and `1,1` lights it, with the per-face redstone properties tracking the ports.
- **Analog input:** A=15 with B=5 (a wire line decaying to `power=5`) still lights it, and the saved `microchip.power` reads 15.
- **State survives a quit and relaunch**, the circuit is inspectable and resettable with `/lbr circuit <x> <y> <z> status|clear|and`, and a signal arriving on a wire strongly powers what sits beside it.
- **Crafting** follows the jar's shaped recipes (circuit board plus the mod's tags), and the block drops itself to a pickaxe.

**Not yet ported**

- the other 15 microchip components and the guide's remaining scenes;
- the in-game guide book and the microchip's GUI (this slice configures with a command instead);
- the mod's own wire-rendering template (the slice uses a vanilla wire model).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the six-gate logic family: OR, XOR, NAND, NOR and NOT beside the existing AND. Each gate carries its own rule from the jar's own guide — OR and XOR are analog with XOR's odd parity, NOT/NAND/NOR are boolean, every gate takes 2 to 10 inputs clamped and NOT exactly 1 — and each has its saved compound type with `input_count`. A `/lbr circuit` action drives an output port so the guide's analog rule is observable in game. Proven in game: the truth tables per gate, analog 3+5 reading 5, XOR four-input parity (2 then 4 then 3 then 2 then 1 inputs), NAND `15,0` reading 1, NOR `0,0` reading 1, the `status` readout naming a gate and its input count, and refusals that leave the circuit unchanged.

projects.name: Living Camera
projects.summary: A camera that moves with you: it leans into strafes, sways on turns, dips on landing and bobs with your steps
projects.description:
A camera that moves with you. It leans into strafes, tips as you jump and fall, sways on fast turns, dips when you land, bobs with your steps and breathes while you stand still. Everything runs on springs, so the camera eases into each motion and settles back with a little weight instead of snapping.

- **Strafe and forward lean**: the camera rolls into sideways movement and tips slightly while running.
- **Turn sway**: fast mouse turns tilt the view.
- **Jump and fall tilt**: the view lifts going up and dips coming down.
- **Landing dip**: a hard landing bumps the camera down, then it springs back.
- **Step bob**: a soft bounce in step with your walking, on top of vanilla's.
- **Idle breathing** and **Speed FOV** (off by default).

projects.name: Living Hands
projects.summary: Your first-person hands come alive, and your own arm holds what you carry
projects.description:
Your first-person hands come alive. Held items bob with your steps, drop into a sprint, dip when you land and lift when you jump, and breathe while you stand still. Everything moves on springs, so it eases in and settles back instead of snapping.

- **Your own arm holds the item**, with your skin, as the game shows it only for an empty hand (not for maps, which already show arms, or while invisible).
- **Per-item swings**: a fist jabs, a sword cuts across, a trident or spear thrusts, tools chop down, a mace lifts and slams, a shield bashes.
- **Walking bob, sprint pose, jump and landing**, and slow breathing while standing still.
- **Actions**: food and drink are chewed, a drawn bow trembles, a raised shield is pushed out.
- **Movement**: a breaststroke in water, hand over hand on ladders and vines, arms trailing on an elytra.
- **Hurt flinch**, a little flip on **item switch**, and an optional **turning sway** (off by default, since Living Camera already sways the hand).

Every effect has its own strength, plus overall intensity, in Mods > Living Hands > Config.

Client side only: it works in single player and on any server. No network, file or process access beyond its own settings.

The mod API can draw in the hand but doesn't say which texture is your skin, so besides the mod API this mod patches the start of Horizon's own hand_geometry to read your skin, whether your model is slim, your main hand and whether you're invisible; it changes nothing the game does. It works on the Horizon build it is made for. An API for this is requested in horizon#19904.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/living-hands

projects.name: Lumina
projects.summary: High performance with real-time shadows, physical water, roof overhang occlusion, volumetric 3D clouds, and sharp anti-aliasing
projects.description:
Native shaders designed for high frame rates and clean, balanced visuals without post-processing blur. All options are fully configurable directly in the shader settings menu.

**Lighting & Overhang Shading**
- Balanced daytime lighting with warm sun and clean azure shadows.
- Directional sky dome occlusion: accurate contrast between ground, walls, and ceilings.
- Non-linear ambient occlusion under house roofs, eaves, porches, and balconies.
- Selective midtone vibrance on grass and foliage without clipping bright highlights.
- Foliage subsurface scattering and sun-facing rim lighting.

**Shadows**
- Real-time sun and moon shadow maps with distortion-aware filtering.
- Acne-free shadows on terrain, blocks, and thin grass at any distance.
- Selectable shadow map resolution: 512, 1024, 1536, or 2048.

**Clarity Anti-Aliasing (FXAA)**
- Edge-selective geometric smoothing on block silhouettes, roofs, and stairs.
- Flat surfaces, textures, wood, stone, and UI remain 100% sharp with zero blurring.
- Modes: Sharp, Smooth, or Off.

**Water & Underwater**
- High-speed Screen Space Reflections (SSR) combined with planar mirror reflections.
- Physics-based Beer-Lambert light absorption with depth-dependent color transition.
- Snell's window when looking up from underwater with total internal reflection.
- Animated seabed caustics, wave refraction, and underwater depth fog.

**Clouds & Atmosphere**
- Raymarched procedural 3D cumulus clouds with Fast, Balanced, and Cinematic presets.
- Volumetric god rays through terrain and trees.
- Procedural rain puddles on grass and dirt with raindrop impact ripples.
- Custom weather rendering for rain and snow particles.
- Native block emission and dynamic colored lighting support.

**Setup Note:**
Set Clouds to OFF in your video settings to let the custom 3D clouds render properly.

projects.name: Macro Keys
projects.summary: Keys that send your chat messages and commands, set up in an in-game editor
projects.description:
Keys that send your chat messages and commands.

- **12 macros**, each with up to **5 lines**: commands (`/home`) or chat messages.
- **Three modes**: **send all** (in order, with a delay you choose between lines), **type in chat** (opens the chat with line 1 typed, like `/msg Steve `, for you to finish and send), or **one per press** (the next line each press, then back to the first).
- **An in-game editor**: press **K** (rebind it in Controls). Bind each macro's key in Options > Controls > Macro Keys; Ctrl, Shift and Alt combinations work.
- **Paced** to stay under the server's chat spam kick: messages wait rather than get you kicked, and anything still waiting is dropped when you leave a server or the world changes (another server behind a proxy, or another dimension).
- The macros are kept in `config/macro_keys.txt`, which you can also edit by hand.

Client side only: it works in single player and on any server. **Network use:** it sends only what you put in your macros, as chat messages or commands to the server you are playing on, when you press their keys; it contacts nothing else. It reads and writes only its own file in `config/`.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/macro-keys

Inspired by CommandKeys by TerminalMC (Apache-2.0). Written anew for Horizon: it contains none of its code and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CommandKeys or its authors.

projects.name: measurements
projects.summary: A Horizon port of measurements.
projects.description:
A port of [Measurements](https://github.com/Mrbysco/Measurements) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The item `measurements:tape_measure`: right-click a block to place point A, right-click again to place point B and finish the measurement. The action bar shows `Distance: <d> blocks (X: <dx>, Y: <dy>, Z: <dz>)`.
- The distance is Euclidean over the coordinate differences, printed with one decimal (`5.0`, `7.1`, `0.0`), with the deltas as integers.
- The next click starts a new point A; shift-right-click removes the latest measurement (`Measurement undone (N left)`, or `Measurement cleared`).
- The same block twice reports `Distance: 0.0 blocks (X: 0, Y: 0, Z: 0)`.
- A session is dropped when the tape leaves the main hand, when the player changes dimension, and one tick after a player leaves.

**Not yet ported**

- **Delivery is the action bar, not an in-world box.** Upstream is a client-only renderer (`MeasurementBox` draws an AABB and three axis labels); it has no chat/action-bar readout and no Euclidean distance. The pin has no client render hook usable in the headless harness, so the port reports through `native_action_bar`. Deferred: the drawn box, its colours, text size, line width and the live crosshair preview.
- **The port prints the Euclidean distance (one decimal) and coordinate differences**, where upstream's labels are inclusive block counts (`|Δ|+1`): the same 0→5 measurement reads 5 here and 6 in upstream's label.
- One process-wide client list upstream becomes per-player sessions here, pruned one tick after a player leaves (the pin has no quit hook).
- The "still holding" reset checks the main hand only; an off-hand-only tape can start a measurement and is cleared on the next player tick.
- The recipe is accepted by `horizon-mod check` with the supplied `#c:ingots/iron` tag, but the harness did not craft it in game.

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

projects.name: Mekanism

projects.description:
A port of [Mekanism](https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism) by Aidan C. Brady and the Mekanism contributors for Horizon. These first slices bring four pieces of the ore-processing chain:

- **Energized Smelter** — 50 FE/t, 200 ticks per smelt, a 20,000 FE buffer.
- **Enrichment Chamber** — the jar's recipes: one ore becomes two dusts, raw ore 3 becomes 4, a raw block 1 becomes 12.
- **Basic Energy Cube** — a 4,000,000 FE buffer.
- **Basic Universal Cable** — moves 8,000 FE/t between them.

Feed items and FE through their sides and right-click a machine to open its menu.

**Not yet ported**

- **The Energy Cube has no menu and no side configuration.** The container hook returns for the cube and all six of its faces are both inputs and outputs; the side configuration the mod is known for is not implemented.
- **The four block recipes are this slice's own**, using vanilla stand-ins (iron, redstone, glass, copper) for the steel casing, the basic alloy, the circuits and the energy tablet that this slice does not register; upstream's recipes depend on the steel chain, which is a later slice.
- The rest of Mekanism — the other machines, the multiblocks, the tools and the deep-tier content — is a planned gap list.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2017-2025 Aidan C. Brady`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: This version completes the four metals: each gets a storage block, a nugget and the four recipes that connect them to its ingot, so nine ingots make a block and a block gives nine back, and an ingot makes nine nuggets. The shapes are the jar's own and they are not symmetric in the way the obvious version would be: the block is a ring of eight tag members around one of the metal, which looks redundant until you notice it lets the recipe accept any ingot the tag names, and there is no nugget-from-block recipe at all because the jar has none — so none is carried. Proven in game: all sixteen recipes craft with their grids emptied and their ingredients consumed, eight ingots and a dirt in the centre make nothing, all nineteen blocks place and read back and drop themselves, and no ingredient fails to resolve, which is the check that the tag-keyed cells actually read their tags. One thing deliberately not carried is the tool-tier tag: this build implements no tool tiers, so shipping it would be data claiming a behaviour the port does not have.

projects.name: mekanismcovers
projects.summary: A Horizon port of mekanismcovers.
projects.description:
A port of [Mekanism Covers](https://github.com/lucaargolo/mekanism-covers) by D4rkness_King, built on [Mekanism](https://github.com/AdLf0208/mekanism) 0.2.2 or later, which it declares as a required dependency.

The first port of Mekanism Covers, two items and a component that let a transmitter wear a block. Right-click a universal cable with a cover to make it look like stone, glass or anything else you can craft a cover from, and the choice is written into the cable's own saved data, so it survives a save and reload and can be replaced by a second cover or stripped back off. Proven in game on a game carrying both this package and the parent, since the cable's block entity is the parent's code: the shaped recipe crafts four empty covers and consumes all nine cells, the special recipe fills one and the held stack's components name the block, the cable has no such key before the click and names the block afterwards while still holding it forty ticks later, a second cover replaces the first, sneaking with an empty cover strips it and returns both the cover and the block, and a plain stone block or a torch is refused by name. The tests count the cover consumed in survival and untouched in creative, which is the difference between the two hands. The appearance half is recorded as blocked with its symbols: the cover is carried but not yet drawn, because the API has no per-position appearance, shape or dynamic-light hook.

versions.changelog: This version applies the same rule to the other path a cover can be consumed by. A cover renamed in an anvil carries a component besides its block, and clicking it onto a transmitter used to store only the block, so the name was gone when the cover came back off. The click now refuses such a cover exactly as the crafting grid refuses a stack with components, through the same predicate, and the cover stays in hand with nothing written. Proven in game beside the plain case: a named cover clicked on a cable leaves the transmitter wearing nothing and the cover in the inventory, while a plain cover in the same session writes its block. Three harness faults the legs forced are fixed and recorded: an item given lands in the first free hotbar slot rather than the first, a spawned drop can miss its first sample, and the game's folder is the launching command's working directory, which had been writing worlds into the campaign root instead of the run's scratch directory.

projects.name: Mekanism: Generators
projects.summary: Heat generator and the graphite/lava energy chain from Mekanism: Generators, with the jar's burn times and FE rates.
projects.description:
A port of [Mekanism: Generators](https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism) (MIT, by Aidan C. Brady and the Mekanism contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **heat generator** and the graphite/lava energy chain behind it.

**Implemented so far**

- `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator`, a fuel slot (container slot 0) that takes any item with a furnace burn time and turns one item a tick into `burnTime / 20` mB of lava: coal 80 mB, a lava bucket 1,000 mB, and a crafting remainder replaces the stack.
- A 24,000 mB lava tank (this port's saved int `lava`; upstream's fluid capability is not declared in this slice, so only the fuel slot fills it).
- A heat capacitor of 10 units, fed by 200 heat/t while lava burns, 30 per lava side and 100 in the Nether, cooled by the 0.5 thermal-efficiency factor, so the capacitor settles at its stable temperature and the generator reports 100 % efficiency.
- The generator's FE buffer (160,000 FE, output only at up to 1,020 FE/t) declared as the block's energy capability, so another mod's cable can read and drain it.
- `/mekanismgenerators info|energy` readout, plus the carried block model, texture and language entries, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- No FE *output* into a neighbour: the generator fills its buffer and declares the capability, but nothing pushes it outward. The API-142 transfer helpers exist at this pin, so a cable slice can add it.
- No fluid capability: the tank is a saved int, so a pipe cannot fill it and nothing reads it as lava.
- No GUI: fuel goes in through the container, and state is read with the command.
- No `active` block state, so the `heat_generator_active` model, the sound that goes with it and the block's animation are not carried.
- The other generators (gas-burning, bio, solar, wind, advanced solar, laser, fusion, turbine), the generator upgrades and the boiler are later slices.

MIT; the upstream copyright line (2017-2025 Aidan C. Brady) and the full permission notice travel inside the archive at `mixins/mekanismgenerators/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, energy output: the heat generator now pushes its buffer into the block on the face its state names, which is the half of the tick that was missing — it filled its own buffer and nothing ever left. Upstream's rule is the one carried: emit to the front face only, up to twice the production rate, taking only what that neighbour accepts, inside one transaction. Proven in game on a two-mod game with our own mekanism parent: the generator held 56,432 FE and the cube on its facing face went 15,300 to 71,888 while the generator fell to zero, the cube on the opposite face stayed at zero, the steady rate measured 12,096 FE over about a hundred ticks, and with the front cube removed the generator stored 11,984 itself. The red leg is the same scenario with the emit call removed: the buffered FE did not reach the front cube, plus nothing. One thing is recorded rather than claimed: the carried recipe stays `blocked(no c:ingots/osmium provider)` because the game rejects its tag, so it is not counted as crafted. The slice also fixed its own repin properly — the manifest bump alone leaves the old SDK in `.horizon/sdk`, which is now a documented trap.

projects.name: Mekanism: Tools

projects.name: mekmm
projects.summary: A Horizon port of mekmm.
projects.description:

**Not yet ported**

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the recycling factory at every tier the jar registers: advanced, elite and ultimate beside the basic one, each with its own process count, energy buffer and container. The buffer is the jar's own formula — half the machine's storage or its usage, whichever is larger, times the tier's processes — giving 30,000, 50,000, 70,000 and 90,000 FE, which corrects slice 1's figure of 20,000 for the basic factory: that was a single machine's storage, not a factory's. The five extra tiers the mod names are recorded `blocked(evolvedmekanism-not-ported)` rather than faked, because the jar appends them only when Evolved Mekanism is loaded and it is not in the registry. Proven in game: each tier stalls at its own process count on 10,000 FE — advanced at forty units five times, elite at twenty-nine three times and twenty-eight four times, ultimate at twenty-three twice and twenty-two seven times — then finishes every process on exactly the energy it had left with one scrap each and a zero buffer; the four containers open nine, eighteen, eighteen and twenty-seven slots; and a survival break drops the ultimate factory beside a vanilla stone break as the differential. The tier roll measured the real seventeen percent, which the scenario had only pinned for the basic tier.

projects.name: mifa
projects.summary: A Horizon port of mifa.
projects.description:
Requires [Industrial Foregoing](https://github.com/AdLf0208/industrialforegoing) 0.2.5 or later: every item here carries that mod's augment component, and every carried recipe is its dissolution chamber's type. The package declares it, so the launcher installs the parent and the game refuses this add-on by name when the parent is absent.

A port of [mifa](https://github.com/Christofmeg/MoreIndustrialForegoingAddons) by Christofmeg. The tag's LICENSE credits the original author; this package now carries that MIT notice inside the archive too.

The third attempt at this mod, and the first to ship: the two blockers that stopped the earlier passes now exist in the parent, so nineteen addon items with their augment payloads, ten machine recipes and the smithing recipe are carried as content. The measurement that says it is real: of the sixty-one external symbols the jar names, fifty-six now resolve, and the five that do not are named individually as missing parent fluids, a fluid tag with no member, and a processing addon the parent does not ship at all. Proven in game on a two-mod game with the parent: all nineteen items and names, every tier from three to eight seating its own speed and efficiency values where the efficiency bar reads thirty-nine and nineteen rather than forty and twenty, because those are the jar's own literals; a rate that falls fifty-eight to twenty-six over eight ticks; a crafted addon seating at nine; the smithing recipe producing netherite gear with its inputs consumed; and all ten carried recipes running to product with their fluid and inputs consumed while a wrong grid matches nothing. Two harness facts are recorded with it, both of which had silently corrupted earlier reads: the message list is newest first, so tailing it reads the oldest reply, and the console command returns success even when it refuses.

versions.changelog: This version answers a review with one declaration: the package now names the parent it binds to, so the launcher installs that parent and the game refuses this one rather than loading add-ons whose component and recipe type do not exist. The floor is the later of the two surfaces used, and it was measured rather than copied: the augment component arrived in one parent release and the dissolution chamber with its recipe type in another, so the requirement is the second. The refusal is proved by launching without the parent, where the loader names both mods and repeats the declaration's own reason and link, and by launching with it, where the parent compiles and the carried recipes read 33 of 33 against the chamber. Nothing in the content changed, which is the point of the version, and the test harness that produced the earlier evidence is kept as a script.

projects.name: minecolonies
projects.summary: A town hall founds a colony, a citizen joins and farms it — with generated art.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [MineColonies](https://github.com/ldtteam/minecolonies) (GPL-3.0 code; the mod's own art is All Rights Reserved, so **every asset here is generated by this port**) for Horizon. This first slice is **a town hall, a colony, one citizen and one job**.

**Implemented so far**

- **Founding:** placing a `minecolonies:blockhuttownhall` founds a colony with a default name (`<owner>'s Colony`), its owner, centre, a **64-block (4-chunk) radius**, the founding tick and its records of citizens and harvests. Legality is decided before the block appears, so an illegal hall never exists.
- **Refusals that matter:** a second hall too close is refused, a hall **120 blocks across and 120 up** is refused (founding distance is horizontal — the colony is a 2D claim), and a second colony for the same owner is refused.
- **A citizen and a job:** `/minecolonies citizen hire|list`, `/minecolonies job assign <citizen> farmer|info` and `/minecolonies colony info|rename|radius`. The farmer needs a `minecolonies:blockhutfarmer` in the colony, walks to a mature wheat every 40 ticks, harvests it, replants at age 0 and counts it; a citizen with no colony does nothing.
- **Everything survives a quit and relaunch** — name, roster, radius and harvest count are in the town hall's saved data.
- **The art is generated**, never copied: `tools/gen_assets.py` builds all 15 asset files from a named 10-colour palette and three model templates, and regenerating gives byte-identical files.

**Not yet ported**

- the other ~40 jobs, the builder and its schematics, the research tree, and the colony/citizen UI (the commands above are the surface);
- happiness, saturation, requests, raids, building-driven growth and worldgen colonies;
- the citizen's own renderer (its texture is generated but not yet bound), and the proper hut and scythe shapes.

**Licence.** MineColonies' code is **GPL-3.0**; its art is **All Rights Reserved**, so this port ships **regenerated art only** and contains no upstream texture, model or language file. The GPL-3.0 text and a notice naming the authors, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256 travel inside the archive; the port is a derivative of the code under the same licence with its complete source published.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 9f42064 and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 5, the food request: a citizen spends one point of saturation per work tick, stops working when it reaches zero, and the colony records a request for bread that one loaf from the chest settles. This is the request system's second family, and it uses the same machinery the tool request built: one saved field on the roster row, one request kind, one more branch of the delivery queue. Proven in game on the same tree: saturation falls from forty-six to forty-one over two hundred ticks while the tree still stands, then reaches zero and the citizen is hungry with one request naming the bread, and once the loaf leaves the chest the citizen reads fed, the request clears and the tree falls. The asset half is measured rather than asserted: a new provenance tool hashes every one of the jar's twenty-two thousand seven hundred and forty-seven files and every one of the port's twenty-five asset files, and reports zero matches, so the licence's no-copying requirement is checked by the same command every slice.
