projects.name: Minimap, Worldmap and waypoints reworked
projects.summary: An adaptive minimap and world map with named waypoints, portals, world borders and a biome readout.
projects.description:
An adaptive minimap and a full world map for Horizon, with a persistent per-world terrain cache.

- Minimap in four corners, square or round, 64–256 GUI pixels, 0.1–4 blocks per pixel, and optional player rotation.
- Player arrow on both maps shows the viewing direction and accounts for minimap rotation.
- English, Russian, French, Spanish and German interfaces follow the game language, including regional variants.
- World map opened by a rebindable key (M by default); drag to pan and scroll to zoom under the cursor, with eased camera motion.
- Independent dimension selection for the minimap and the world map (Player / Overworld / Nether / End), without teleporting the player.
- Hover shows the pointed-at coordinates, the localised biome and waypoint names; the hovered block is outlined.
- Right-click menu: copy coordinates, create a named waypoint, or teleport when the client knows the player has game-master permission.
- Configurable two-letter initials distinguish waypoints sharing their first letter: similar colours (default), any colours, or a single letter; the same labels appear on maps, in the list and in 3D.
- Separate waypoint manager (N by default) for creating, renaming and deleting waypoints; waypoints are drawn as first-letter markers on the HUD through walls and on both maps.
- 3D-world waypoint markers in the waypoint's colour (or a skull for deaths), through walls; the label can be letter + distance, letter only, or name + distance, and can be shown only while the crosshair is on the marker. Each point can hide its own 3D marker.
- Death waypoints are placed automatically as numbered black skulls and can be removed on approach or switched off in the settings.
- Eight compass direction letters (localised) or the game's axis names at the inner edge of both maps, tracking true north.
- Water and glass-family blocks are semi-transparent, water tint thickens with depth, grass-like ground cover is skipped, and flowers/crops use their real colours.
- Portals (Nether, End and End gateways) are marked and show their destination; Nether destinations prefer the nearest known portal, otherwise coordinate conversion.
- Overworld and Nether world borders are drawn on both maps (the Nether border is scaled to the same physical area).
- Relief shading crosses chunk borders; unknown terrain is transparent; the minimap renders at high resolution for smooth movement.
- Settings and named waypoints persist asynchronously in the mod data folder. Waypoints are isolated by save/server identity and dimension, with 64 points per world/server. Legacy unscoped points are deleted on upgrade; preferences are retained.
- Both maps stream reusable GPU tile pages. Persistent world-space overview tiles accelerate distant views; camera and zoom targets are prefetched, retaining coarse coverage until finer tiles are ready. Detailed terrain preserves original block texels when zoomed in. Detailed and LOD terrain, sampled heights, biome names and portals persist across reconnects and restarts in one `.mwwr` container per single-player save/server address. A **Map RAM** slider (16–512 MiB, default 64 MiB) budgets retained terrain; no network requests are made by the mod.
- Each of the 67 vanilla biomes has an individual 16×16 icon. Waypoint colours can be edited, and Show on map centres the world map on a selected waypoint.
- World, actual-render/LOD and chunk-render borders have hover labels; right-click outlines the selected chunk and region.

- Map caches lists world/server names and available local icons, file sizes and compatibility. View saved terrain and player position, switch saved layers, manage waypoints or move to coordinates from the main menu. Confirm deletion of idle caches or rebuild derived images while retaining saved terrain.
- Distant terrain uses snow-aware climate/height approximation, fixed world-space biome blending and shared water opacity: snowy taiga and mangrove water retain their expected appearance. Detailed terrain remains authoritative; fresh LOD samples gradually refresh legacy colours.
- Version 0.7.9 is a flat source .hmod for the signed native SDK, pinned to Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da), Minecraft 26.3 and SDK Rust 1.99.1. Existing scoped waypoints, settings and terrain containers remain in use.

Created by daniliammo and continued by Gurov08ruS after the original account was removed from GitHub.

The runtime uses only portable standard-library APIs and is intended for Linux, macOS and Windows. The 0.7.0 SDK port was built and tested in a live Linux game; macOS and Windows runs remain unverified.

versions.changelog: Offline cache maps with progressive terrain loading, saved Nether layers and waypoint editing. Safe cache deletion, retry after a busy lease, release on disconnect, and title Options and controller routing. Adds coloured icons and precise waypoint teleport. Requires Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da).

projects.name: Mining Gadgets
projects.summary: A laser mining gadget that clears a plane of blocks for FE, with its upgrade data model.
projects.description:
A port of [Mining Gadgets](https://github.com/Direwolf20-MC/MiningGadgets) by
Direwolf20 and ErrorMikey for Horizon. This slice is the gadget itself: the
right-click laser and the plane of blocks it clears.

- Right-click a block, or the air in front of you, with a gadget: it mines the
  aimed face's plane (wider ranges are the square on that plane, oriented by the
  face) and nothing it is not allowed to break — no block entities, doors or
  fluids other than waterlogged blocks.
- Each broken block costs FE: 200 base plus the active upgrades' cost per block.
  A shot needs `cost × range × range` in the buffer before it starts. The gadget
  holds 1,000,000 FE and its damage bar is the charge.
- The three tiers (MK1–MK3) are carried as items, and the upgrade list
  (`{name, active}`) is read and written as data.

The held-use trigger, the ghost preview, the client beam, particles and sounds,
the settings and filter screens, the Modification Table and the remaining
upgrade effects are later slices. MIT — original copyright and licence notices
are kept in the port repository; see LICENSE and LICENSE-NOTICE.md there.

projects.name: modern_industrialization
projects.summary: A Horizon port of modern_industrialization.
projects.description:
A port of [Modern Industrialization](https://github.com/AztechMC/Modern-Industrialization) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- `modern_industrialization:electric_macerator`, one block: a **32,000 FE buffer** that any face may fill and nothing may drain (upstream's `EnergyComponent.buildInsertable` is insert-only). The mod's own default is 1 EU = 10 FE, so 3,200 EU = 32,000 FE.
- One item input slot and four item output slots: hoppers insert into slot 0 and pull from slots 1..=4.
- `CrafterComponent`'s tick in the pure runtime: a run starts when the buffer covers the recipe, is consumed at the machine's EU rate, and overclocks by the mod's own divisor.
- The jar's macerator recipes that only need vanilla materials, with tag inputs resolved to the vanilla items the tags hold.
- `/modern_industrialization info|energy|efficiency` (upstream has no commands).

**Not yet ported**

- **No crafting recipe** for the machine or the dusts: the creative tab is the entry point, and the four block recipes are the port's own, using vanilla stand-ins (iron, redstone, glass) until the steel chain, the basic alloy and the circuits this slice does not carry arrive.
- **34 of the jar's 324 macerator recipes** are carried. The other 290-odd need MI's own ingots, plates, gears, rods and wires, which this slice does not register.
- **No data-driven recipe type**: the pin offers no machine-recipe registry for a native mod, so the table is a `const` in `runtime.rs`; adding a recipe is a code change.
- No menu: `ModContainer` has no per-slot rule for a player's menu at this pin, so the machine is driven by hoppers.
- The energy and efficiency commands refuse any block entity that is not this macerator, and the energy hook leaves another mod's declaration for the same block alone.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2020 Azercoco & Technici4n`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, the energy hatches: ten blocks, five tiers each way, an input and an output, so a multiblock can finally be fed electricity through its shell instead of only through its controller. The tiers are the jar's own, thirty-two EU up to a hundred and twenty-eight million, and their buffers follow; the superconductor tier's real buffer exceeds what this pin can hold, so it is declared at the largest value a thirty-two-bit buffer can express and the difference is stated rather than hidden. Proven in game in the way that matters for a hatch: five thousand FE put into the hatch appears in the controller's buffer and leaves the hatch, a run of exactly twelve thousand makes one coke with both ending at zero, and a run of eleven thousand nine hundred and eighty stalls at nine hundred and ninety-eight of a thousand with the same recipe and no product, which is the differential that shows the energy came from the hatch rather than from nowhere. Each tier clamps at its own capacity when filled twice over, and an output hatch drains the controller back out. The shell accepts the hatch in place of a brick and refuses it in the middle ring. The item and fluid hatches from the last slice still pass, and the coke oven's own recipe list is unchanged as a regression.

projects.name: Modern Dynamics
projects.summary: The item pipe and extractor attachment: 4 items every 40 ticks between inventories, ported.
projects.description:
A port of [Modern Dynamics](https://github.com/Technici4n/Modern-Dynamics) by Technici4n for
Horizon. This is the first slice, not a full replacement.

Implemented so far

- `moderndynamics:item_pipe` with six boolean connection states and the carried multipart core/arm models and textures; it connects to another pipe or to an inventory reachable from the touching side.
- `moderndynamics:extractor`, placed on a pipe side by right-clicking with the item (consumed outside creative) or by `/moderndynamics attach`; the side is saved with the block entity.
- Upstream's default transfer: every 40 ticks each extractor moves up to 4 items from the inventory on its side into the network's other inventories, nearest first; a refused item stays in its slot.
- The jar's recipes and carried content, the `/moderndynamics info` readout, and persistence across a relaunch.

Not yet ported

- the fluid pipe, the five energy cables (LV/MV/HV/EV/superconductor) and the machine extender;
- the attractor, filter and inhibitor attachments, the wrench, the attachment screen and the upgrade data;
- routing modes other than CLOSEST, priorities, and the stuffed-item retry path;
- item-travel rendering, waterlogging and the per-type arm textures;
- the JEI/EMI/REI/Jade plugins, the debug tool and the config file.

Licensed **LGPL-3.0-only**, the original's licence, with the complete corresponding source
in the port repository, so the licence obligations are met: original copyright
and licence notices travel with it, inside the bundle (`mixins/moderndynamics/LICENSE`
and `data/moderndynamics/license/`) as well as in its LICENSE and LICENSE-NOTICE.md. Help with
the gaps above is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the attractor: upstream's reverse of the extractor, pulling out of the pipe network into the inventory on its own side, four items per operation, nearest first, and never from another attractor. That is the half that lets a pipe feed a machine, which nothing else in the port did. The design is upstream's own and the proof is a direction differential: the same geometry with an extractor moves four items the other way, and two attractors move nothing. Proven in game: every carried recipe crafts with its ingredients consumed and a wrong pattern crafts nothing, right-click places both kinds, the attractor fills its own chest in four operations, a pipe broken in survival drops itself, the admin attach costs one item and a detach clears the side, and a missing item or an unknown kind is refused by name. The port also had a dead loot table in the 1.21.1 array form, so a broken pipe dropped nothing; it is rewritten to 26.3's typed condition and proved by that survival break.

projects.name: modularrouters
projects.summary: A Horizon port of modularrouters.
projects.description:
A port of [Modular Routers](https://github.com/desht/ModularRouters) by Des Herriott (desht) for Horizon — the Router, the Puller Mk1 and the Sender Mk1.

**Implemented so far**

- `modularrouters:modular_router`: nine module slots and five upgrade slots saved in the block entity, its facing, the `active` block state while a module works, and its one-slot buffer exposed as the block's item container on all six faces.
- Two modules: the **Puller Mk1** takes from the container beside the router into the buffer, topping up a buffer stack of the same resource first and never more than the Stack Upgrade count or the room left; the **Sender Mk1** pushes from the buffer into the first container in range and leaves a refused remainder in the buffer.
- A resource is the item **plus its components**: a named or enchanted stack never merges with a plain one, and a pull never replaces the buffer's components with a namesake's.
- The tick rate (`max(2, 20 − 2 × speed)`), items per operation (`1 << min(6, stacks)`), phase-spread across routers by position, and the module/filter settings in the block entity.

**Not yet ported**

- **The other modules:** Puller Mk2, Sender Mk2/3, vacuum, dropper, flinger, placer, breaker, extruder 1/2, detector, distributor, energy distributor/output, fluid 1/2, player, activator, void and creative, with their settings screens.
- **Upgrades and augments:** the 10 upgrade items and their insert rules, the 11 augments and the 5 smart filters (this slice's filter is a whitelist/blacklist over item ids).
- **The GUI** (module/upgrade/buffer slots, redstone and eco modes) and the recipe/advancement chain for the carried items.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/modularrouters/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: This version adds the first extruder module, and the artefact corrected the brief's premise outright: it is not a pass-through that moves an item from one block to another, but a redstone-driven extending and retracting arm along one face. While the router is powered it places buffered blocks outward one at a time up to a saved distance; when the signal is gone it retracts them back into the buffer, breaking with the module's pickaxe and testing drops against its filter. The range is sixteen to thirty-two, read from the reference configuration rather than the stale book value, and the pickaxe is copied from the breaker at crafting time. Proven in game on both directions: a powered module places stone and empties its buffer, an unpowered one pulls cobble back, and no signal, a dirt whitelist or no direction leave the arm still.

projects.name: Montarc
projects.summary: Bright, colorful shader pack: soft shadows, colored light, living water, wind, and own look for the Nether and the End.
projects.description:
Bright, colorful shader pack for Horizon. Horizon had no shaders on the registry, so I made one. Style is close to Complementary Reimagined, but the code is mine, written from scratch in WGSL.

## What you get

- **Soft shadows.** Sun and moon cast them. Water and stained glass tint the light that goes through.
- **Sky and fog match.** Blue day, orange sunsets, dark blue night. Far terrain fades into the sky, no hard line at the horizon.
- **Colored light.** Torches are warm, soul fire is blue, redstone is red, sea lanterns are cyan, amethyst is purple.
- **Water that looks like water.** Waves, depth color, reflections, sun glitter and foam on the shore.
- **Wind.** Grass, flowers, crops and leaves move. Rain makes it stronger.
- **Nether and End look different.** Nether is hot and hazy, with heat shimmer. End is cold and purple.
- **29 options.** Everything can be tuned or turned off in game.

## Which version do I take?

- **1.7.1** is for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer (the final shader API 0.2).
- **1.6.1** is for older builds that still serve shader API 0.1. The Nightly no longer loads it.
The launcher offers the one your game can run.

## Slow? Try this

- Shadow quality: Low
- Shadow map size: 1024 or 512
- Shadow distance: 64
- Water reflections: off
- Bloom: off
- Shadows: off. Biggest gain.

## Known problems

- Horizon's shader API is experimental and can change.
- Entities, block entities and particles are not shaded yet. There is no stage for them.
- Nether and End sky is vanilla. The sky stage only draws in the Overworld.
- Shadow bias may need tuning on some GPUs. If you see stripes on surfaces, change `Shadow bias`.

versions.changelog:
- Final shader API 0.2 (Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer). It reads the terrain's shaded_tint, fogs with [frame] fog = "pack" and uses fog_environment and fog_render. The look is the same as 1.6.1, with the clearer underwater fog.
- Needs no extra switch in the game. Shader API 0.1 is retired, so 1.6.1 no longer loads in the Nightly.
- Everything from 1.6.1: portals with coloured light, shadow size and distance options, own rain and snow, puddles, optional sunbeams, seabed light patterns.
- Screenshots added. Release v1.7.1 of the repository.

projects.name: Chat Memory and History

projects.name: morered
projects.summary: A Horizon port of morered.
projects.description:
A port of [More Red](https://github.com/Commoble/morered) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The **logic gate plate** family (diode, NOT, AND/OR/NAND/NOR, XOR/XNOR, multiplexer, 2-input AND/NAND, latch, pulse gate): a plate attaches to a face, rotates, reads its input sides, and emits 15 from its output face when its logic function passes.
- The pure model (`runtime.rs`) has upstream's function table, the 24-entry output-direction table, the clockwise input mapping, the latch's hold/reset rule and the pulse gate's edge/2-tick rule (18 tests).
- Content: eleven gate blocks plus the `stone_plate` recipe dependency, on an `end_rod` template with the real `facing`/`rotation`/`input_*`/`powered` state properties.
- The red-alloy wire posts and the spool (select, link, cut), the six bitwise plates and their wires.
- The gates are proved in game with `ctl`: a placed plate reads its inputs and drives a lamp, a 2-tick pulse arms and clears a latch, and a stone control stays dark.

**Not yet ported**

- Placement orientation: **resolved** — a plate placed through vanilla placement takes its attachment from the clicked face and its rotation from the clicked quadrant (`state_for_placement` plus `use_item_on` rod rotation).
- The coloured network cables, the bundled cable posts/spools, soldering and the wire spool's remaining modes are deferred.
- The carried `end_rod` template gives the plates their 2-px shape and collision, but there is **no lit/unlit tint** (the models' tint indices need a block-colour provider); the wire model is simplified to six 2-px plates.
- A comparator's strength collapses to a boolean (the gates are binary), and inputs are sampled once per tick: a rise and fall of one input inside a single tick collapses to no edge.
- Loot drops one wire rather than the subwire count (the pin has no equivalent of `WireCountLootFunction`).

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Carry-dialect repair: 46 data files were still in the 1.21.1 dialect. Four recipes used the `{"item": …}` / `{"tag": …}` ingredient form 26.3 rejects, so they never crafted, and 42 loot tables carried the array `"conditions"`, `bonus_rolls` and `1.0` rolls, so their blocks dropped nothing. All converted to the 26.3 shapes. Proven in game: `redwire_post` crafts with its red alloy consumed and the grid emptied, and `redwire_post` drops itself beside a vanilla control that drops one too.

projects.name: mysticalagradditions
projects.summary: A Horizon port of mysticalagradditions.
projects.description:
A port of [Mystical Agradditions](https://github.com/BlakeBr0/MysticalAgradditions) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The six tier-6 crops `mysticalagradditions:<name>_crop` (`nether_star`, `dragon_egg`, `gaia_spirit`, `awakened_draconium`, `neutronium`, `nitro_crystal`) on the `minecraft:wheat` template: `age` 0..7, the jar's 4-pixel outline with an empty collision, and vanilla crop random tick.
- Their seeds (`<name>_seeds`, a plain item with `place_block`, as the parent port does) and essences (`<name>_essence`).
- The six cruxes `<name>_crux` on the `minecraft:stone` template: hardness 5.0, blast resistance 10.0, `requires_tool`, and the jar's `mineable/pickaxe` + `needs_stone_tool` membership.
- `insanium_farmland` on the `minecraft:farmland` template, in `#minecraft:supports_crops`, `#minecraft:grows_crops` and `#minecraft:mineable/shovel`.
- The growth gate: a crop only grows while its own crux is two blocks below it. The parent's `requiresEffectiveFarmland` default is false; when true the block below must be insanium farmland.
- Bone meal only targets a crop that can grow and is under age 7, and never advances it (the jar's `isValidBonemealTarget`/`isBonemealSuccess`).
- 26.3 loot tables: a ripe crop gives 1 essence + 1 seed, a young one 1 seed (tier 6's `secondarySeedDrop` is false, so there is no second roll); the farmland gives itself with silk touch, else dirt + a 25% insanium essence.
- The jar's `MEM/ESE/MEM` seed recipe for `nether_star` and `dragon_egg`, the nether-star and dragon-egg crux recipes, and insanium farmland (essence + farmland), with `#c:storage_blocks/diamond` supplied as a tag.
- One tier-6 line is proved end to end in game (awakened draconium): planted, held at `random_tick_speed 0`, grown to age 7, and a survival break drops exactly 1 essence + 1 seed.

**Not yet ported**

- **Fertilized essence** is not carried (`runtime.rs` explicitly leaves it out), so no crop can be fertilized by it.
- **Four integration recipe families are missing**: the seed/crux recipes that depend on other mods' materials (`tools/carry_content.py` records which ones were dropped), so those tiers cannot be reached from survival yet.
- The remaining tiers' crops are content only where the jar defines them; the awakened-draconium line is the one proved in game.
- **This is an add-on**: it requires the parent mod **Mystical Agriculture**, whose Horizon port (`mysticalagriculture`) supplies the essence, farmland and growth rules this port builds on.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the Wither drop: the mod's last remaining server-event behaviour, and the acquisition path for two carried recipes that were dead in survival. A Wither now leaves a withering soul at the jar's own 0.35 chance (strict `<`, tested at 0.3499 against 0.35), and `mob_drops` off adds nothing. Two measured facts are recorded rather than worked around: this pin's gamerule is `mob_drops`, not `do_mob_loot`, and `living_drops` does fire for `/kill` deaths with the dying mob resolving through the host — thirty withers left nine souls. The Ender Dragon half is `blocked(living_drops-ender-dragon)`: a probe that pushed eight scales from the hook's first line, with no host read, left nothing for a dragon killed four blocks away over 400 ticks, so the dragon's death never reaches this hook; `mob_killed` is melee-only and cannot add to a drop list, and `entity_leave_level` also fires on chunk unload. The e2e asserts that gap, so it will fail the day the pin gains the hook. Proven in game: 30 kills leave 9 souls, a zombie leaves neither drop, and the gamerule gate works.

projects.name: Mystical Agriculture
projects.summary: The inferium crop and essence loop: grow crops on farmland, harvest essence, craft seeds and ingots.
projects.description:
A port of [Mystical Agriculture](https://github.com/BlakeBr0/MysticalAgriculture) by BlakeBr0 for Horizon. This first slice is the inferium crop/essence loop:

- Craft inferium seeds (8 essence plus 1 wheat seed) and plant them on farmland; the crop grows through vanilla wheat's eight ages on random ticks and needs light 9 to survive.
- Harvest a mature crop for essence and seeds; the drop depends on whether the farmland is still there, as upstream. Bone meal is refused.
- Craft an inferium ingot from a prosperity ingot and 2 essence.

The machines, the other crops, the armour and the essences above inferium are later slices. MIT — the original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/mysticalagriculture/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the carried crop loot table in 26.3's dialect, the port's first SDK-format in-game leg — and a measurement that corrects an assumption the campaign was working from. The table is converted to 26.3's singular `condition` with `match_block`, matching vanilla's own `wheat.json`. But running the published 0.2.0 package's own bytes at this pin shows the old array form **still rolled correctly** — age 7 gave 1 essence and 1 seed, age 0 gave 0 essence and 1 seed — so this is dialect parity, not a behaviour repair, and `notes.md` records the measurement instead of the claim it was briefed with. The leg is the port's first SDK-format run: the crop drops its essence and seeds through the native hook, a content-only copy proves the table on its own, and both legs carry a selftest that inverts the expectation.

projects.name: Mythic Upgrades
projects.summary: Eight gems and necoium with their ores and crystal geodes, and armour sets and tools that each have their own effect.
projects.description:
Eight gems (sapphire, ametrine, topaz, ruby, peridot, aquamarine, citrine, jade) and necoium, with their ores, crystal geodes in the Overworld, the Nether and the End, budding crystals that grow buds and clusters, bricks, schists and cave patches of crystal blocks. A smithing template from end city chests upgrades netherite gear into each gem's tools and armour. A full armour set gives its gem's effect: Damage Deflection, Arcane Aura, Topaz Reaction, Blood Thirst, Miasma, Ice Shield, Static Field or Jade Aura, and each tool has its own on-hit effect: percentage damage, levitation and teleport, shocks, life steal, poison bursts, freezing, chain lightning. The gem shards are armour trim materials, and the necoium carrot shares effects between nearby holders.

**Differences from the original:** Armour trims made of the mod's gems are applied and saved but not drawn, on worn armour or on item icons, because the game's client doesn't load trim materials from mods ([horizon#19695](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/19695)); vanilla trim materials draw on the mod's armour. There are no potions or brewing recipes for the mod's effects (the effects themselves come from the armour, the tools and the necoium carrot). The Mythic Caves, Rifts and Barrens biomes don't generate: their crystals and ores appear as patches inside the existing biomes, without the biomes' own music, fog or colours. The ruby and jade tools' right-click effects are left out, the particles are plain dust rings and puffs, and on this Horizon build the mod's damage types fall back to magic or generic damage, so death messages say so. There is no config file: the original's default numbers are used.

A port of [Mythic Upgrades](https://github.com/TriQue06/mythic-upgrades-multiloader/tree/1.20.1) 5.1.1 by TriQue, published under its licence, MIT. The original copyright and licence notices are kept in the file (LICENSE, NOTICE).

Its textures, models, sounds and data come from the original mod. No Minecraft code is included.

versions.changelog: First registry release. Built with the exact-build SDK dd67b76 on the mod API only, with LICENSE and NOTICE in the package.

projects.name: naturesaura
projects.summary: A Horizon port of naturesaura.
projects.description:
A port of [Nature's Aura](https://github.com/Ellpeck/NaturesAura) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The chunk aura: drain spots (base 1,000,000 + spots) and the aura bloom (150,000 aura once, when it appears).
- The Nature's Altar's 9×4×9 multiblock and its **500,000-aura container** (300 aura a tick from the area, only in the Overworld and the Nether).
- The ritual for the three catalyst-free recipes, the right-click insert/take, and the materials that make the multiblock buildable in game.
- Why this is the smallest honest loop: the altar's only inputs are aura and one item, its only output one item, so the loop closes with no GUI, no energy, no fluid and no multiblock-machine API, yet every piece of it is the mod's own core behaviour.

**Not yet ported**

| Gap | Shape | What the slice does instead |
|---|---|---|
| `IAuraType` per dimension | the pin has no aura-type registry | the altar pulls in the Overworld and the Nether and not in the End — upstream's rule, no type objects |
| Aura spot storage | NeoForge attaches to `LevelChunk`; the pin has `Holder::Chunk` attachments | a `ChunkAura` codec compound `{spots: [...]}`; same arithmetic |
| The client aura overlay | no client HUD in the slice | `sync: false`; the readouts are commands, and a later slice adds the overlay |
| The altar's waterlogging | the slice's templates have no waterlogged state | not carried |
| The bloom's ground set | `minecraft:poppy` allows mycelium, moss, mud and rooted dirt too | upstream's five grounds plus four extra template grounds |
| Aura-container items | the altar's "fill the held item's aura" branch | not in the slice; the tick goes straight to the recipe |

A saved altar whose recipe index is no longer in the table drops the run instead of panicking. MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two carried crafting recipes — and the 1.21.1 dialect they shipped in. `gold_brick` is a shapeless recipe, and the port's carry script upgraded a shaped recipe's `key` for both tag and item forms but left a shapeless `ingredients` list in the old `{"item": …}` form, so 26.3 rejected it at load and the recipe returned nothing. The shaped `gold_fiber` beside it crafted perfectly, which is why slice 1 never noticed the dead one. The script now upgrades both shapes through one helper, and regenerating the carry from the kept jar changes exactly one file of fifty-two. The port also gains the checks that would have caught it: a dialect check over the built package, a real-table craft check for both recipes with two wrong-ingredient controls, item and block read-backs, and the four carried loot tables proved by breaking them. Proven in game: both recipes craft with their ingredients consumed, two wrong patterns return nothing, the load log has zero `invalid ingredient` lines against six in the red run, and all four blocks drop themselves.

projects.name: neovitae
projects.summary: A Horizon port of neovitae.
projects.description:
A port of [Neo Vitae](https://github.com/breakinblocks/NeoVitae) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The altar `neovitae:ara_vitae`: a horizontal `facing` block with no menu, so a right click reaches the use hooks (hardness 2, blast 5, stone sounds, collision 16×12×16). It has a block entity, a server tick and one slot.
- Structure → tier, data-driven from the jar's two layouts: `weak` (the altar alone, tier 0) and `apprentice` (altar + 8 runes at `y-1`, tier 1), revalidated every 100 ticks; only the layout's four orthogonal `upgrade` positions are scanned for runes.
- The LP tank: `10,000 × capacityMod` mB main, `1,000 × mod` I/O and a reserve `× 20`. A Capacity Rune adds 0.2, an Augmented Capacity Rune multiplies by 1.075.
- Clicks: a right click with an item puts one item in the slot (carrying that stack's own components); an empty-hand right click takes the stack back.
- The weak orb: within 5 blocks of an altar it trades health for LP — creative fills the altar's room (verified at exactly 18,000), survival pays 2 health for 200 LP.
- Harness commands `/neovitae altar|lp|insert` (upstream has none).

**Not yet ported**

- **Altar tiers `mage`/`master`/`archmage`/`transcendent`** (pillars, t3–t6 capstones, tier effects) and the 21-rune family beyond Capacity.
- The altar's fluid I/O (input/output/charging tanks), the reserve auto-move, the tier-0 bootstrap leech, redstone/comparator output, particles, sounds and the block-entity renderer.
- **The crafting tree above the altar** (vitae stone, tabula rasa/robur/animata and the rest) is not carried, so every recipe it would unlock is missing.
- The slot move is applied by the altar's tick, one tick after the click (a block-entity slot written inside a use hook is not kept at this pin); upstream moves it inline.
- A take is ignored for 500 ms after an insert on the same altar, so the engine's other-hand retry cannot take back what the first hand inserted.
- The layouts are Rust constants transcribed from the jar's data, not a datapack registry (the pin has no consumer for the mod's own registry).

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Carry-dialect repair: four loot tables were in the 1.21.1 dialect — the array `"conditions"`, `bonus_rolls` and `1.0` rolls — so those blocks dropped nothing. Converted to 26.3's singular `"condition"` and integral rolls, and `rune_blank` now drops itself beside a vanilla control that drops one. The port carries no crafting recipe (its altar crafting is its own path), so the in-game proof here is the drop family.

projects.name: Aurora Lights

projects.description:
Aurora Lights is a native Horizon mod that makes torches, lanterns, glowstone and other luminous items glow while you hold them, while they lie on the ground and while they sit in item frames. It also gives enchanted gear a faint violet halo.

Everything is optional: the mod menu has switches for other players, dropped items, item frames, light colors and the enchanted glow. All of them are on by default except light colors. The hue palette is shared with Aurora Bloom, the companion shader pack that turns this colored light into a sheen on water, blocks and entities.

Install only one shader pack: Aurora Bloom. Turn off Horizon Extras > Dynamic Lights, or both systems will emit duplicate lights. The mod is client-side and needs the launcher to trust its Rust source, which is compiled for the exact pinned game build.

Repo: https://github.com/netfeez/aura-lights-mod
Companion shader: https://github.com/netfeez/aura-bloom-shader

versions.changelog: Reads the local player's entity id once per frame instead of resolving every cached mob, removing a quadratic mob-list scan in crowded multiplayer scenes. Otherwise identical to 0.1.3: overlapping lights are balanced towards the brightest source, the enchanted halo fades beside brighter frames and drops, and weak halos cannot take a slot at the eight-light cap. Same Nov 21 Nightly pin (Horizon f037744).

projects.name: Nocturne
projects.summary: Dark fantasy & gothic horror shader pack with Blood Moon skies, thick rolling mist, eerie lantern halation, wet reflections, and AgX filmic grading.
projects.description:
**Nocturne** transforms Minecraft `26.3` into a brooding dark fantasy and gothic horror world built natively from scratch on **Horizon Shader API `0.2`**. Inspired by classic atmospheric horror shaders, every daytime sky becomes an overcast, mist-shrouded vale while nightfall awakens a towering **Crimson Blood Moon** with abyssal starfields and creeping dread fog.

### Key Features
- **Overcast Gothic Daylight & Crimson Blood Moon**: Veiled pale sun, ominous storm-lit horizons, blood-tinted lunar corona, and subtle horror sky pulse.
- **Rolling Multi-Layer Dread Mist & Volumetric Shafts**: Swirling noise-driven valley mist, claustrophobic distance fog, and shadowed crepuscular rays.
- **Flickering Sanctuary Lanterns & Spectral Soul-Fire**: Warm 1950K torch/lantern flicker contrasted against cold cyan soul-fire and glowing cursed ores/eyes.
- **Dark Mirror Water & Rain-Slicked Reflections**: Deep obsidian-teal water with Gerstner waves, Fresnel sky/SSR reflections, and storm rain ripples.
- **Gothic Cinema Lens & AgX Tonemapping**: Soft eerie halation bloom, gothic SSAO, subtle chromatic fringe, organic 35mm film grain, FXAA, and bleach-bypass AgX color grading.
- **39 In-Game Options**: Customize Blood Moon intensity, fog density, lantern warmth, water darkness, film grain, vignette, and horror effects live in Horizon's shader settings.

A port of [Occultism](https://github.com/klikli-dev/occultism) (MIT, by klikli-dev) for Horizon. This first slice is **spirit fire**: the block, its ignition, and the chalk colours it takes.

**Implemented so far**

- Ignition: flint and steel or a fire charge struck on a block with a `#occultism:start_spiritfire` item entity (datura) inside upstream's `AABB(-1,-1,-1,1,1,1)` around the clicked block's centre lights one spirit fire on the target and consumes **every** datura in that box, as upstream does. With no datura in range nothing happens and the lighter's own use runs.
- Chalk: right-clicking a spirit fire with any of the jar's chalks (16 colours, pure and impure) sets the block's `color` property.
- The datura item, the 33 chalk items, the spirit fire's own recipe, loot and language, carried inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/occultism` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

| Declared upstream library | What it would have provided | What this slice does |
|---|---|---|
| Modonomicon (required) | the guide book and its 260 pages, ritual and recipe pages | nothing: there is no guide-book reader at this pin |
| Curios (required) | accessory slots (familiar ring, spirit lamp) | nothing: there is no accessory-slot API |
| GeckoLib | the 21 animated spirit models | nothing: no spirits in this slice |
| SmartBrainLib | the spirits' job AI | nothing: no spirits in this slice |

- The remaining machines (crusher, smelter, sacrificial bowl, pentacles and rituals), every spirit and their jobs, the storage system and the dimensional mineshaft are later slices.
- The ritual and chalk recipes beyond the ones carried, and the sapling models the carried sapling item references.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices (klikli-dev, 2020) ship inside the package: `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` at its root, with the same texts in the source repository.

versions.changelog: This version carries the six sacrificial bowls, the family's first block entity, and it holds one item at a time and gives it back. The reference is precise here and the port follows it: one slot with a limit of one, so five dirt put one in and leave four in the hand; a right-click with an empty hand returns the stored stack with its components intact, damage included; breaking a full bowl drops the bowl and spills what it held; and a plain bowl converts its stored item over spirit fire while a golden one deliberately does not. Proven in game on all of those plus the tool pair, which was measured rather than inherited — these blocks do not require a tool, so a hand break drops them and the template's own requirement had to be overridden. The game leg also found a port defect the unit tests could not: a click is dispatched once per hand, so the main hand stored the sword and the off hand's empty turn took it straight back, which is now a rule that only the main hand fills a bowl. The ritual itself stays blocked and is named, not approximated.

projects.name: Occultism
projects.summary: Occultism by KliKli, ported to Horizon: ritual circles, spirits and their jobs, possessed creatures, the guide book, dimensional storage and the mineshaft.
projects.description:
An unofficial, alpha port to Horizon of [Occultism](https://github.com/klikli-dev/occultism), the mod by KliKli ([klikli-dev](https://github.com/klikli-dev)), made with their permission. It isn't made or supported by KliKli, so please report problems [to this port](https://github.com/Dawnforger/occultism-horizon/issues), not to them. Occultism's code is MIT and some of its art is CC BY 3.0, both credited in the package's NOTICE.

**What's in this alpha**

- **Ritual circles.** All sixteen chalks, crafted as in Occultism, with glyphs that wear down as you use them, sacrificial bowls and a golden bowl, and Occultism's rituals and pentacles, with their sacrifices and item uses.
- **The Dictionary of Spirits.** Occultism's guide book, with its ritual pages, pentacle previews placed in the world, and the ritual satchels that build a previewed circle for you.
- **Spirit names.** Books of binding carry their spirit's name, and what is made from them passes it on.
- **Working foliots.** Summoned with a job and bound to a book of calling: the janitor gathers dropped items, the transporter moves stacks between containers, the lumberjack fells and replants trees, and the farmer harvests and replants crops, each bringing what it gathers to a container.
- **Soul gems.** Capture a creature whole and let it out elsewhere.
- **Crusher, smelter and crystallizer spirits** in all four ranks, as Occultism's, at their rank's speed.
- **Possessed creatures.** Occultism's sixteen possession rituals and the creatures they make.
- **Unbound spirits.** Summon a hostile Afrit or Marid, drawn from Occultism's own models and animations, with its stats, immunities and helpers.
- **Spirit fire and Demon's Dream.** Datura, otherstone, books of binding, inks, pastes, cursed honey and more.
- **The otherworld tree.** An oak sapling in spirit fire grows into it, with its logs and fruit.
- **The Third Eye and otherworld goggles.** Raw iesnium in silver ore, otherworld logs among the oaks you chop.
- **Dimensional storage.** The Storage Actuator in Occultism's terminal look with its crafting grid, stabilizer plates, stable wormholes, the Storage Accessor, and hoppers that pull from it.
- **The dimensional mineshaft.** Miner spirits dig ores into it.
- **Weather and time magic, and traders.** Djinni and afrit rituals that bring day, night, clear skies, rain or thunder, and spirits that trade stone for otherstone and otherrock, or gamble gems.
- **Wild rituals.** The wild hordes, the Wild Hunt, the illager invasion and the trial breezes, whose followers shield their leader; random-animal possessions, and resurrections into allays and undead mounts.
- **Equipment.** Silver and infused tools and armour, made infused in Occultism's upgrade rituals, the butcher knives and their extra drops, flaming paste, and silver and infused horse and nautilus armour.
- **Furnishings and blocks.** Large candles, copper, silver and dark bowls, the iesnium bowls that run a ritual four times as fast, silver and otherrock building blocks, the spirit lantern and torch, and Occultism's ritual particles.

**Different from Occultism for now:** the book of calling has no screen (its mode and work area change when you use it, and its tooltip shows them); spirits take no item filters; the transporter doesn't open doors.

**Not in yet:** familiars, the higher spirits' other jobs, satchels and tablets, and the dark storage blocks.

This is a native mod: the launcher builds it after asking you to trust its code, and it runs with your account's permissions. It contains no Minecraft code or assets. Pinned to game 26.3, Horizon SDK `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`, and fits the Nightly of 2026-11-21 (`8f83e5c`); the full corresponding source is the linked repository.

versions.changelog: Much more of Occultism. Added: weather and time magic; otherstone, otherrock and gambler traders; the wild hordes, Wild Hunt, illager invasion and trial breezes; random-animal possessions and resurrections; flaming paste; silver and infused tools and armour, the butcher knives and their drops; large candles, golden pitayas, otherglass, the otherflower, otherrock and silver building blocks; copper, silver, dark and iesnium bowls (iesnium runs rituals four times as fast); the spirit lantern and torch; ritual particles and chalk-coloured spirit fire. Security, from the registry review: flaming paste no longer sets fire or pours lava beside the block it is used on, throws fireballs or primes TNT, and the spirit torch isn't put on walls, as none of these could go through the server's own checks (spawn protection, the world border, TNT's priming) at this SDK pin. Same id, namespace and saved worlds as 0.11.2-alpha.1.

projects.name: oritech
projects.summary: A Horizon port of oritech.
projects.description:
A port of [Oritech](https://github.com/Rearth/Oritech) by Rearth for Horizon — slice 1, the **Basic Generator and the Pulverizer**.

**Implemented so far**

- The Basic Generator: a 50,000 FE buffer (insert 0, extract 256 FE/call through the block energy capability), 32 FE per burning tick, fuel from the engine's `minecraft:cooking_fuel` so modded fuels work, the jar's buffer-full rule (at 49,984 FE the burn pauses and keeps its progress) and output to the six neighbours at `level_tick_post`.
- The Pulverizer: a 25,000 FE buffer, 32 FE/t while working, the jar's custom recipe type read from the pin's recipe table, progress saved with the recipe id (upstream resets after a reload; this port continues) and the jar's output-room rule.
- An operation whose result does not fit its output slot (empty or partial) **waits** instead of clamping the result, so no recipe consumes its input for a partial output.
- The seven carried pulverizer recipes, the two machine textures, the loot entries, the block entities and the English names.

**Not yet ported / deviations**

- The buffer's key is the API's int `energy` rather than upstream's long `oritech.machine_energy`; every value here fits and the buffer is a real block energy capability other mods can use.
- **The rest of Oritech:** the other generators, the accelerator ring, the reactor, the GeckoLib deep-tier models, the machines beyond these two, the ore/ingot sets and the rest of the crafting chain.

Oritech 0.2.13 includes the upstream CC0-1.0 licence in `LICENSE` and credits in `LICENSE-NOTICE.md`. The [release receipt](https://github.com/AdLf0208/oritech/blob/1a230cb0f29429e1ba8d97a931b51820ed6d05f9/RECEIPT.md) records the exact build pins.

versions.changelog: This version answers a review, and the honest answer is that the delivered version already validated its output before consuming anything — so the work was to make the wrong order inexpressible rather than to fix a bug. The whole decision now lives in one pure rule that answers either a work item or nothing, and the tick only applies what it returns, so a path that takes the input and the fluid before learning the output cannot fit no longer exists. Proven in game on the review's own case and its twin: a full output slot leaves the input, the buffer and the progress untouched for an item recipe, and a full output tank does the same for a fluid recipe, while the same machines with room finish for their exact costs and let the fluid fall by exactly the recipe's amount. The counterfactual removes the fit check and watches exactly those two tests fail. A harness command had to be added, because a machine's output slot has no player route at all — the right click fills inputs and the container reader cannot see a mod block entity.

projects.name: Petalveil
projects.summary: Vanilla's light kept whole: shadows only shade the sky's, so caves, torches and night stay vanilla. Pastel sky, waves, caustics, wind in the leaves, glow.
projects.description:
Petalveil is a shader pack in Horizon's own format, and its rule is that vanilla's light stays whole: a surface is lit by `albedo * tint * lightmap` first, and the pack only adds to it. The sun and the moon add light, and the shadow map takes back a bounded share of what comes from the sky, so a cave, a cellar, torchlight and the night keep the brightness and the colours vanilla gives them.

What it adds:
- Sun and moon shadows, soft to very soft, 1024 to 4096 texels over 64 to 160 blocks.
- A pastel sky veil that fades into vanilla's fog colour at the horizon, a rainbow while the rain dries, and a cooler night with its brightness kept.
- Broad cloud shadows drifting over the land, on their own pattern.
- Water of its own: a swell and a fine chop on the surface, rain rings, the world mirrored by fresnel, its own refraction so the bed bends with the wave, sun glitter, and caustics on the blocks under the water.
- Leaves, grass and flowers waving in a gust, the same in the shadow pass so their shadows move with them.
- Sun rays and moon rays, a soft glow, cloud edge softening, and a gentle colour grade.

Every effect can be turned off or brought to a neutral value: 59 options on five pages (Lighting, Water, Nature, Sky, Camera) in Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. Shadows off is the cheapest setting; the water's own surface detail has a switch for each part.

The pack costs about 3.8 ms of GPU time at 2560x1440 with the default settings (budget 3.0 ms). No Minecraft assets, original code.

Source: https://github.com/Givemegitpls/Petalveil — built for shader API 0.2, so it needs a Horizon Nightly from 2026-11-16 or newer.

versions.changelog:
Ported to shader API 0.2. The look is the same as 1.29.0: every stage converts at its doors (the engine's own `horizon_encode`/`horizon_decode` powers), so the values the pack's maths was tuned at are untouched, and the options keep their meaning and their defaults.

- Needs a Horizon Nightly from 2026-11-16 or newer (it reads `MaterialInput.shaded_tint`, which arrived that day).
- Nothing moved on the options pages; all 59 options keep their ids, so saved settings carry over.
- Full-bright blocks follow the new `emission`: the block's light level over 15 rather than a brightness class, so lamps in the dark are a touch dimmer than in 1.x.
- No change to the pack's cost on the GPU.

projects.name: pneumaticcraft
projects.summary: A Horizon port of pneumaticcraft.
projects.description:
A port of [PneumaticCraft: Repressurized](https://github.com/TeamPneumatic/pnc-repressurized) (GPL-3.0-only, by desht, MineMaarten and the PNC:R contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Flux Compressor**, the machine that turns FE into compressed air.

**Implemented so far**

- `pneumaticcraft:flux_compressor` with a **100,000 FE buffer**. It spends FE a tick to make **16 mL of air a tick** at 100 % heat efficiency (`40 × eff/100 × fluxCompressorEfficiency/100`, the config default 40 air per 100 FE).
- A 10,000 mL air handler with `PressureTier.TIER_TWO` (danger 20 bar, critical 25 bar), and the heat exchanger: capacity 100, `addHeat(air/20)` a tick, ambient 300 K and `(T − 300)/101` lost a tick — so it settles at about 300.8 K and stays at 100 % efficiency.
- With nothing connected the compressor **leaks** `(int)(pressure × 40) + 20` mL a tick, as upstream does, so a lone compressor never accumulates air (measured: 16 mL after 118 ticks).
- Every 5 ticks the compressor refreshes its rates; `/pneumaticcraft` readout commands expose the buffer, the air and the temperature for the harness, and the carried model, texture, language and recipe ride inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The **pressure tubes** (`pressure_tube`, `advanced_pressure_tube`, `reinforced_pressure_tube`, `tube_junction`) and tube modules — the network proper: the six-sided connection state, tube volume aggregation, network leaks, modules and camouflage. This is the next slice and the block most of the mod stands on.
- The upgrades (speed, volume, security, dispenser) and their items.
- The menus and screens, the pressure gauge and manometer items, and the GUI redstone modes.
- The overpressure explosion (`doOverpressureChecks`): nothing in this slice reaches the critical pressure without the harness, and the harness clamps at 25 bar.

GPL-3.0-only, like the original; the full licence and the original copyright notices travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, pressure tubes and the network between them: the three tubes, their six-sided connection state, per-tube volumes and tiers, network dispersion by volume, and the dead-end leak. Deferred within the same gap line: the pneumatic wrench and closed sides, tube modules, camouflage, waterlogging and the junction. One trap is recorded for every future cable-like port: a block-entity write made **during** a tick is overwritten by that entity's own write-back — a four-handler network at 25 bar lost about 200,000 mL in 40 ticks that way — so the port now applies writes in `level_tick_post` as deltas on the target's current value. Proven in game: a pair moves 2,216 mL for 5,560 FE in 139 ticks; a chain at 24.90 bar feeds a dynamo from 3,648 to 9,490 FE; a ring of four splits 4,000 mL into four 1,000 mL tubes; a dead end vents to 16 mL over 221 ticks; and each tube tier keeps upstream's volume when it is alone.

projects.name: pocketstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of pocketstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [Pocket Storage](https://github.com/Flanks255/PocketStorage) (MIT, by Flanks255) for Horizon. This first slice is the **tier-1 storage unit**: a pocket-sized container whose contents ride the item stack itself.

**Implemented so far**

- `pocketstorage:psu_1`, one of the four tiers the jar ships, built on the `minecraft:iron_ingot` template with `max_stack_size: 1`, with the jar's own model and texture.
- **8 slots of 255**: upstream's `PSUTier.TIER1` (`slots = 8`, `capacity = 0xFF = 255`), repeated in its `README.MD` and in the jar's language file ("Holds %s different items, up to %s of each"). Insert tops up the slot holding the same item, else takes the first empty slot, else refuses the stack.
- The contents ride the stack's own component (`pocketstorage:contents`, one compound per filled slot), so a unit that is saved, thrown or picked up keeps what it holds; an empty unit carries no component at all and stacks like a new one.
- Sneak + right-click a container **deposits** all but one of each kind into it (upstream's `giveItems` rule); sneak + left-click **withdraws** the kinds the unit already holds (upstream's `takeItems` rule). A withdraw takes only plain stacks: a damaged, renamed or enchanted container stack is refused rather than rebuilt from its id, because a saved slot is one `{id, count}` entry and flattening it would destroy the components.
- `/psu put|list|help` stands in for upstream's screen, which this slice does not carry.

**Not yet ported**

- Tiers 2 to 4 (`psu_2` 16 × 4,095, `psu_3` 32 × 65,535, `psu_4` 64 × 1,048,575): only the tier-1 item is carried. The runtime already holds all four tiers' numbers, but the items, models, tabs and the upgrade path are not shipped.
- The `pocketstorage:upgrade` recipe type: a shaped recipe whose `D` is the previous unit, needing a `ShapedRecipe.pattern` access transformer. The pin has no custom recipe type a port can register, so a tier 2–4 recipe cannot be authored yet; the three upgrade recipes are a named gap.
- The storage unit screen, its item handler and the keybind that opens it.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/pocketstorage/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, tiers 2 to 4 and the three upgrade recipes. Tiers 2, 3 and 4 are now carried — 16 by 4,095, 32 by 65,535 and 64 by 1,048,575 — and the upgrade path is authored as data, with `pocketstorage:upgrade` copying the old unit's contents onto the next tier so nothing is lost. The port's own gap note said the pin had no custom recipe type a port could register; that was stale — at this pin a mod registers a crafting kind (`CraftingRecipeKind` plus `register_crafting_recipe_serializer`) and the engine loads it into the crafting table, so the recipes are real data rather than a code special case. Proven in game: tier 1 crafts; gold around it makes a tier 2 that carries the 30 diamonds the old unit held; the same step reaches tier 3 and tier 4, whose readout is one of 64 kinds with 30 items and 1,048,575 each at most; a fourth step produces nothing; and every craft consumes its ingredients. The counterfactual flips the "the upgraded unit kept its 30 diamonds" assertion and exits 1.

versions.changelog: This version finishes the side config, the last half of the machine control gap: each face now stores its own transfer type rather than a boolean, with the four types and their order read from the reference. The defaults are not uniform and are carried as the jar has them — cells, hoppers, transmitters and ender machines start at all on every face, while furnators, solar panels and dischargers start at extract, and the orb and cable have no side config at all. Proven on a cell whose north face was set to none: the sink stayed at zero across twenty ticks while the south face delivered exactly five hundred energy a tick, the two stores conserved to a round million, and flipping the face back resumed charging. The full replay reached this slice with every earlier phase green, then false-failed on a harness regex that demanded a space before the comma-separated fields; that run was discarded and the verdict came from bounded legs.

projects.name: pvp_music
projects.summary: A Horizon port of PvP Music.
projects.description:
A 1:1 Rust port of [PvP Music](https://modrinth.com/mod/pvp-music) (CC0-1.0),
which plays battle music when you engage a player or (if enabled) a mob.
Upstream publishes no source repository, so the port follows the documented
behavior. The package is the .hmod source: a native mod built against the
pinned Horizon SDK (api 0.2, game 26.3).

## Behavior (the original's, kept)

- Mutual-combat detection: attacks on and by players and mobs are remembered
  for 5 s; a landed hit on a player opens the 500 ms target confirm, and a
  mob fight starts when both sides have recently attacked each other.
- The wither and explosion triggers, with their own radii.
- The fading battle track: per-tick volume, death fades when you die or the
  target dies, and the short and long end sounds queued when a battle of
  30 s or more ends.
- The phased two-half battle music, switched at low health on a beat.
- Settings through /pvpmusic (short form /pvm): volume, fades, the mob
  rules, the phase lengths, the beat, the end thresholds and the disabled
  mob list, exactly the original's config fields.

## Wiring

- music (client): the state machine runs once a tick and answers the track
  and its volume, replacing vanilla's situational music while a battle
  plays, and leaves vanilla's when idle.
- client_attack_target (client): records our attack clicks as combat
  candidates.
- client_tick_pre (client): refreshes the max-health read, detects a health
  drop as a hurt, and plays the queued end sound once the battle stopped.
- command + register_client_commands: /pvpmusic, answered locally, shown as
  a chat line, and consumed so the game does not run it.
- The battle tracks and end sounds ship as assets/pvp_music/sounds/.

## Horizon seams

Where the client cannot see what the original read, the port degrades the
same way the original's own fallbacks do: a click on a player opens the
target confirm (the API's client attack hook fires before the server
confirms the hit), and a health drop records a hurt with an unknown source
so the machine's own mob fallbacks apply. Both are the client-side combat
facts the port needs; the ask is filed on horizon-rust/horizon as issue
#10064 and tracked until patched, at which point the wiring switches to it
directly.

Licence: CC0-1.0. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-pvp-music

versions.changelog: Rebuilt on the f00125f native-mod API: hooks wired (music, client_attack_target, client_tick_pre, command); the sounds.json index sits at assets/pvp_music/sounds.json where the game reads it

projects.name: rangedpumps
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rangedpumps.
projects.description:
A port of [Ranged Pumps](https://github.com/refinedmods/rangedpumps) (MIT, by Refined Mods) for Horizon. The pump drains still fluid sources in an expanding square scan and collects them in its own tank.

**Implemented so far**

- `rangedpumps:pump` with per-block range setting, the carried model, texture, language, recipe and loot, declared as one content pack inside the `.hnmod`.
- The scan: `range` starts at -1 (the single column directly **below** the pump); each later range is the **perimeter** of a `(2r+3)²` square — the 8, 16, 24… block ring at horizontal distance `r+1`. Inside a column the pump goes down one block per 8 ticks (upstream's `speed`) to the dimension's minimum Y, then starts the next column. The interior of a ring is not scanned, as upstream.
- Draining: only `minecraft:water` and `minecraft:lava` at `level=0` (a still source) are taken, one bucket at a time, into a 32-bucket internal tank; each drained source is replaced with air and then with the configured block (stone by default), so neighbouring fluid updates see the removal.
- The tank is declared as the block's fluid capability and pushed into neighbouring fluid handlers once per block tick, an equal share to each (upstream's `fillNeighbors`).
- `/rangedpumps` readout and configuration commands.

**Not yet ported**

- No energy (FE) gating: the pin has the energy API, but this slice has no FE source, so the pump runs as if `useEnergy = false`.
- No redstone pause: reading a neighbour's signal needs `LevelAccess`/`Ticks` at this pin.
- The pump's screen and its upgrade items; only the command path sets the range.

The scan no longer consumes a position it could not drain: a source the tank cannot take stays in the world and is retried on the next tick, and a column that starts below the dimension's floor (a pump on the bottom block) is skipped instead of descending forever. MIT; the original copyright and permission notices (Refined Mods) travel inside the archive at `mixins/rangedpumps/LICENSE`.

projects.name: refinedstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of refinedstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [Refined Storage 2](https://github.com/refinedmods/refinedstorage2) by Refined Mods for Horizon — slice 1, the item network.

**Implemented so far**

- **Network:** the connected component of the four network blocks over face-adjacent positions, capped at 512 blocks. A component with a controller is **online**; without one nothing works (upstream: the controller is the network's root and every node is inactive without it). The grid's `active` block state and the `/refinedstorage info` line both read it.
- **Cable connections** (upstream `computeConnections`): six boolean state properties (`north/east/south/west/up/down`), each written from whether the neighbour is a network block.
- **Disk Drive** with nine disk slots, and the **1k Storage Disk** whose items live in its item component, so the disk carries its contents when moved.
- **Grid:** a 9×6 menu that searches the network, withdraws and deposits. Two grids never show the same items — each grid's view sets aside what the other open grids already show — so the last ten diamonds cannot be taken twice.
- A deposit the network refuses stays in the slot **as its remainder only**, so a full disk cannot duplicate the items the player tried to add.
- The `/refinedstorage info|filter` commands, the four blocks' content (models, textures, loot, tags, creative tab) and the disk's component.

**Not yet ported**

- **No energy:** the controller is the network's on/off root but consumes and stores nothing; its `energy_type` state has two values where upstream has four.
- **The rest of the mod:** crafters, exporters/importers, external storage, interfaces, relays, network transmitters/receivers, the security manager, the wireless transmitter/grid, the portable grid, the crafting/pattern grids, autocrafting, fluid storage and disks, the other disk sizes (4k/16k/64k/creative), storage blocks, upgrades, the config file and the coloured variants of every block.
- **No recipes:** the five items need Refined Storage's own chain (`quartz_enriched_iron`, `machine_casing`, processors, cores, `1k_storage_part`, `storage_housing`) and NeoForge `#c:` tags, so they come from the creative tab.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/refinedstorage/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with Refined Mods' MIT notice) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 6, the upgrade items: the transmitter's four upgrade slots and the range upgrade that makes the sixteen-block rule a starting point rather than a ceiling. Only the range half is real here and the other eight upgrades are refused rather than shipped, because speed, stack, regulator and autocrafting bind to importers, exporters, destructors and the crafting grid, none of which this port has, and the four enchantment upgrades need a recipe type the pin does not offer. The numbers are read from the reference rather than guessed: eight blocks per upgrade, four slots, and the creative variant at the top of the priority chain. Proven in game with the differential the brief asked for: a use at seventeen blocks is refused at sixteen and accepted at twenty-four once one range upgrade sits in a slot, the creative upgrade takes the same transmitter to unlimited, the transmitter's own menu shows four slots, and a diamond shift-clicked into that menu does not enter an upgrade slot. The dimension rule is unaffected and still refuses a use from another dimension with an unlimited range in place. This version also fixes a port defect: the transmitter's template could never open a menu, because the game posts the open only for a container class, so the block keeps its nub shape and collision through declared shapes while carrying a container template, and the binding moved to the block's own click hook because the container's click runs first.

projects.name: Refined Types

**Not yet ported**

- The typed grid, exporters, importers, external storage, autocrafting and storage-monitor insertion — that half needs Refined Storage's Java API and is the recorded gap, not this slice.
- **Recipes are not carried.** Every one needs `refinedstorage:machine_casing` (the parent has no crafting chain), `c:dusts/redstone` (a NeoForge tag absent at 26.3) and `neoforge:conditions` (no such loader condition at 26.3); the 111 recipes and their advancement unlocks would be dead data, so the items come from the creative menu until the parent's chain exists.
- The storage-block and energizer screens, block contents surviving a break, and `fireResistant` as upstream declares it.
- The energizer does not refill its buffer from the network once drained — upstream does not either: the buffer is a load-time kick-start. The network is not shut down when unpowered (the parent has no such state); storage stays readable and `active` says whether the usage was covered.
- Source and Soul have no consumer at this pin (no exporters, and Ars Nouveau / the soul mod are not ported), so their role is capacity, totals and usage.
- A storage block beside a cable does not appear in the parent's cable connection state.

versions.changelog: This version makes the storage disks and storage blocks survive lava, as the reference declares them to. The interesting part is that the obvious field does not exist in this game version: there is no fire-resistant key on any of the one thousand six hundred and fifty-eight vanilla items, because the property now travels as damage resistance against the fire damage type, which is exactly how vanilla's own netherite items say it. So the port uses the field this version actually has, and proves the behaviour rather than the key. One thing the brief had too broad is fixed on the artefact's evidence: only the disks and the storage blocks are fireproof upstream, while the crafting parts and the energizer are not, so sixty of the eighty-eight declarations carry it and twenty-eight deliberately do not. Proven by dropping one of each into lava and waiting sixty ticks: the three disk families and the storage block survive, the part and a diamond are gone, and the inventory the red run used shows all six alive before the drop. A generator rule now derives the component from the item's own kind, so a future item cannot acquire immunity by being listed.

projects.summary: A Horizon port of repeatable_trial_vaults.
projects.description:
A port of [Repeatable Trial Vaults](https://github.com/Buuz135/Repeatable-Trial-Vaults) by Buuz135 for Horizon — the key-reset slice.

**Implemented so far**

- Right-clicking a `minecraft:vault` with `minecraft:trial_key` or `minecraft:ominous_trial_key` resets it **iff** the acting player's UUID is in `rewarded_players`: the click is cancelled (the block never sees it), the held stack loses the vault config's key count (normally 1; a keyless vault consumes 0; creative is skipped as `ItemStack.consume` does), the `used` stat is awarded once and the hand swings.
