projects.name: restrictions
projects.summary: A Horizon port of restrictions.
projects.description:
A port of [Restrictions](https://github.com/McJtyMods/Restrictions) (MIT, by McJty) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Attractor** and the **Pusher**: blocks that pull or push the mobs in front of them.

**Implemented so far**

- Attractor and Pusher: the cells in front of the block, `pos + facing*1 … pos + facing*signal` (the block's own cell excluded), where `signal` is the strongest neighbouring redstone signal (0 means off). Each server tick, every mob whose **bounding box intersects** one of those cells gets a velocity impulse along the facing: **−0.1** blocks/tick for the attractor (toward the block) and **+0.1** for the pusher (away). A cell is tested by intersection when the entity has a bounding box, with the feet-cell test as the fallback for entity kinds that have none — so a tall mob is drawn in even when its feet are a cell lower. No line-of-sight test (upstream has none).
- The block entity is created by the `block_entity` hook and ticks through `block_entity_ticks`; the facing is read from the block's `facing` property, and the redstone signal from the neighbouring cells each tick.
- The carried models, textures, language, recipes and loot, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/restrictions` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

- One Way and One Way Wall: upstream's One Way is `noCollission()` and applies its push on `entityInside`. Horizon's content format couples outline and collision and has no per-entity collision shape, and there is no neutral no-collision template with a block entity — deferred to an engine API.
- Players and item entities cannot be moved at this pin (there is no player velocity or position write, and item entities have no position setter), so the blocks move **mobs only**.
- Arrows, boats and orbs are out of scope, as is McJtyLib's two-block placement of the taller variants.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/restrictions/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the sweep is every entity rather than only mobs. Upstream pulls everything the host can move — dropped items, arrows, boats, minecarts, experience orbs — and the port's filter was a leftover from the retired hook that moved only mobs. The exclusion is now a player, whose client owns its motion, and the per-cell budget covers every kind. Proven in game with a differential on the same lane: a powered attractor pulls a dropped item from 3.5 blocks to 1.125 and an experience orb from 5.5 to 1.25, while both unpowered controls stay at their starting distance to four decimals. This version also fixes a defect in the port's own shipped data: both mover loot tables named a component from a library this package does not carry, so a real pickaxe break copied nothing and the block dropped nothing at all — the modifier is gone and a break now drops one block with a pickaxe and one by hand, with vanilla stone as the differential. One pin limitation is recorded rather than papered over: the needs-stone-tool tag has no tier gate at this pin, so a wooden pickaxe still drops the block. Every carried recipe is now crafted from the delivered package's own JSON, with ingredients consumed and the grid left empty.

projects.name: rftoolsbase
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rftoolsbase.
projects.description:
A port of [RFTools Base](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsBase) by McJty for Horizon — slice 1, the Machine Infuser.

**Implemented so far**

- `rftoolsbase:machine_infuser` on the stonecutter template with a horizontal `facing`, standard-iron properties and the jar's own model and front texture, placed facing the player.
- A 60,000 FE buffer through the block energy capability: any side may fill it 600 FE a call, nothing may drain it (upstream's `GenericEnergyStorage(…, canExtract = false)`).
- Two slots: slot 0 takes `rftoolsbase:shards`, slot 1 takes one infusable machine and is also the output; every face reaches both and automation may take from slot 1.
- The infusion rule from the jar: with a shard and an infusable machine below 256 it spends `(int)(600 × (2 − level/256) / 2)` FE plus one shard and infuses for 5 ticks, raising the machine one level. The cost comes from the block's own level, not the item's.
- The `rftoolsbase:infused` item component (0..=256), seeded from the placed item, with the `Infused: N%` tooltip, and a two-slot menu with four data slots (energy, capacity, `infusing`, block level).
- The carried blockstate, models, texture, recipes, loot, tags, creative tab and English names.

**Not yet ported**

- The tablet, the crafter, the storage scanner and the other RFTools machines (those live in RFTools Storage/Utility/Control, separate mods).
- The block-protector/security chain, the config file and the in-game documentation items.
- Recipes that need items from the unported RFTools mods.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/rftoolsbase/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: A repin rather than a new family, and it buys something no single port could: the RFTools family can now be built into one game. This port was pinned to an older build of the engine, and a game refuses two packages that disagree, so a sibling port could not craft its own recipe in the same world as this one. Moved to the campaign pin, rebuilt twice byte-identically, and the whole ladder re-run. The proof is the thing it unblocks: a three-package game carrying this port, the storage port and the power port, in which the storage scanner is crafted from a real machine frame in a real crafting table with the frame consumed, a stone in the frame's cell crafts nothing, and the coal generator is likewise crafted from its own frame, with the result taken out of the slot and the inventory asserted for every ingredient. A run against the unmodified game fails at the first give, as it must, and an inverted assertion fails too. Two harness facts came out of it: a give lands on the next tick, and the launcher reuses a build when the manifest is unchanged, so the version bump is what forces the recompile.

projects.name: RFTools Builder
projects.summary: RFTools Builder for Horizon: the Builder block and its shape cards. A card carries a shape (box, sphere, cylinder, capped cylinder, prism, cone, top and…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of RFTools Builder 1.21-7.0.8: the Builder block and its shape cards, plus the shape geometry behind them. A card carries a shape, a size, an offset and whether it is solid or hollow, and the Builder walks that shape placing blocks into it from a container above or below. Upstream: https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsBuilder — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The shape card `rftoolsbuilder:shape_card_def` carries shape, size, offset, solidity and the corner-selection state in its `rftoolsbuilder:shape_card` component, and a stack with no component is the jar's default solid 5×5×5 box.
- The jar's ten shape formulas — box, sphere, top and bottom dome, cylinder, capped cylinder, prism, torus, heart and cone — are transcribed cell for cell, with the float arithmetic, the integer truncation and the per-axis centre nudge.
- Solid and hollow follow upstream's border test, where a cell is in the shell when one of its six neighbours is outside, and the jar's quirks are kept (a hollow cylinder has no cap, only its rim).
- Dimension is clamped into 0–512 and offset into −260–260, and a card whose box exceeds 50,000,000 cells is refused with those numbers.
- Cards are authored by sneak-right-clicking a Builder and clicking two corners, and by `/rftoolsbuilder shape|offset|reset` for shapes corners cannot express.
- The Builder block entity walks the shape from the top down with x fastest at eight cells a tick, takes the first placeable block from the container above it or below if that one is empty, and waits at a cell it has no block for.
- A protection gate skips a cell outside the world border before anything is read or taken, so a protected cell is never built and never charged a block.
- `/rftoolsbuilder status <pos>` prints shape, size, offset, cell count, progress and the first refused cell, with the count bounded and cached so a huge sparse shape cannot stall the server thread.
- The upstream walk defect is fixed: a shape straddling a chunk boundary is built completely instead of losing the cells in the earlier chunk.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control and a selftest that both fail without it.

**Not yet ported**

- The quarry is not carried, nor its resource scan, silk and fortune drops, void list, replacement block or chunk loading; upstream's quarry is a card type with no geometry, so no quarry shape was invented.
- The movers with their control pages and vehicle builder, the shields with their projector and renderer, and the space chamber with the copy, move and swap modes it feeds are not carried.
- The composer, the projector and the scanner are not carried, which is also why the composition and scan shapes are missing.
- The GUI screens and the mod's own networking are replaced here by the commands and the action bar.
- The liquid and pump cards, the filter module (which is why the container has one slot) and energy are not carried, so this slice builds without power.
- A placed block's own placement hook does not run, because the pin has no fake player, so a bed or door appears only half placed.
- Chunk loading is replaced by waiting for a loaded chunk, and the hilight mode, progress HUD and renderer are not carried.
- Spawn protection is not enforced, because the pin cannot read it, so only the world border is checked.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two carried recipes, which were dead data: the builder and its shape card both used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` / `{"tag": …}` ingredient form, which 26.3 rejects at load, so the game logged `invalid ingredient` for every key and the grid sat full with an empty result — the mod could not be crafted at all. Both files now use bare item ids and `#tag` strings, with patterns, results and ids untouched, and the port gains a data guard that fails on the old shape. Proven in game: the shape card and the builder both craft with their ingredients consumed and the grid emptied, two wrong-ingredient controls return nothing, the game log has no `invalid ingredient` line, and a broken builder drops itself once.

projects.name: rftoolspower
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rftoolspower.
projects.description:
A port of [rftoolspower](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsPower) by McJtyMods. The generator and monitor recipes use RFTools Base ingredients, provided by `rftoolsbase` 0.2.2 on the matching SDK.

The first port of RFTools Power, and it opens with the coal generator: a machine whose whole loop closes inside one block — fuel in, burn, FE out, and a `lit` state that mirrors the burn. Upstream's numbers, not invented ones: 60 FE a tick, 600 ticks for a coal and 5,400 for a coal block, a 500,000 FE buffer, one insert-only slot. Proven in game across thirteen phases: a fresh generator reads 0 of 500,000 and unlit; one coal puts 780 FE in the buffer at 587 of 600 burn and empties the player's hand; the energy gain equals exactly sixty times the burn delta over fifty-three ticks; the store freezes when the burn ends; stone is refused and charcoal burns for its own 600; a hopper feeds the slot with no click at all; the full store survives a save and relaunch; and a generator broken in survival drops an item carrying its 3,000 FE, which restores on placing while a doctored 999,999 is clamped to the 500,000 ceiling. Two deviations are recorded rather than hidden: there is no GUI, so a right click fuels the machine, and the lit state is the same cube because the parent's glow overlay cannot run at this pin. The powercell family is recorded as blocked on the smart wrench, which the parent port does not carry.

versions.changelog: This version adds the blazing agitator, the machine that makes a rod better by standing it beside other rods. The reference's arithmetic is unusual and it is followed exactly: each rod's quality factor comes from its own quality and duration, each neighbour contributes the difference between its factor and its own, the sum is floored at one and divided by four, and that figure then drives time down and quality and duration up, so a full box beats a lone rod and the middle of a row beats its ends. Proven in game on the arithmetic rather than on a trend: the store falls exactly ten a tick over forty-seven ticks, the combined change across the whole box matches the machine's own readout to six decimal places, a lone rod rises at its own much smaller rate, a neighbour feeding it gains and loses exactly in step, outputs move in order, locks hold, a plain blaze rod converts, and an agitated rod leaves in a hopper. One defect only the game could show is fixed: a number stored as a double was read as a float, so a rod whose time read five hundredths came back as four and a half quintillion ticks. Two corrections from the artefact are recorded: a lone rod's factor is not one but a fifth, and the infuser's counter period is eleven ticks rather than ten.

projects.name: rftoolsstorage
projects.summary: Modular storage: a module block holding 6,400 items, sealed until locked.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [RFTools Storage](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsStorage) (MIT, by **McJty**) for Horizon. This first slice is **modular storage**.

**Implemented so far**

- **`rftoolsstorage:modular_storage`** holds a storage module and stores items in it: tier 1 is the jar's own **100 slots × 64 = 6,400 items**, with `StorageModuleItem.MAXSIZE = {100,200,300,500,…}` driving the tiers.
- **The block is inert until a module is installed and the storage is locked**, exactly as the jar's `insertItem`/`extractItem` both begin with `if (!isLocked())`.
- **The player surface:** a module held in hand installs into the block, a held stack inserts on right-click, an empty hand seals or withdraws, and the action bar reports `stored/capacity`; `/rftoolsstorage info|lock <x> <y> <z>` reads and seals it.
- **Contents survive a save, quit and relaunch**, one item kind per slot with the stack limit respected.

**Not yet ported**

- the storage scanner, the crafting manager, tiers 2–4, the remote module and remote block;
- the type, filter, dump and control modules and the storage tablet;
- the GUI (search, sort, compact, cycle, padlock) — this slice uses right-clicks and commands;
- the fill overlay: the jar declares its `amount`/`type` states but never writes them (upstream's `getRenderLevel()` is a commented `// @todo 1.14` stub), so the port does not invent one either.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 5, the storage scanner: a block that reads the inventories inside a cube around it and answers one command with what it found, charging its own energy for the question and refusing when it has none. The radius is settable because the reference exposes it as a slider, so here it is a command that clamps to the same bounds. Proven in game as a sequence of exact answers: a fresh scanner with no power says so with its buffer in the reply; at the default radius it sees nothing because the chest is two blocks away and reports its charge falling; at radius two it finds sixty-four stone and no dirt; at radius three it finds the dirt too, each answer costing the same fixed charge; with the buffer emptied it refuses and reads nothing, and recharging makes it answer again. A chest and a modular storage both answer that they are not scanners, the buffer and radius and answer all survive a relaunch, and a survival break drops the block itself. Two honest restrictions are recorded rather than worked around: the scanner's recipe needs a machine frame from a sibling port that is pinned at an older build and so cannot share this game, and the claimed-land check is blocked because the pin exposes a cancellable destroy hook rather than a permission query.

projects.name: rftoolsutility
projects.summary: The RFTools tank: 32,000 mB of one fluid, filled and drained with a bucket.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [RFTools Utility](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsUtility) (MIT, by **McJty**) for Horizon. This first slice is **the tank**.

**Implemented so far**

- **`rftoolsutility:tank`, 32,000 mB of one fluid** — the jar's own manual says "up to 32 buckets" and `TankConfiguration.maxCapacity` defaults to 32,000 mB.
- **Every face accepts and provides** the fluid, and the contents live in the block entity's saved data, so they survive a save, quit and relaunch.
- **The bucket loop:** a water or lava bucket fills it by 1,000 mB and leaves an empty bucket in hand, an empty bucket drains 1,000 mB and fills, and a full tank, a different fluid or a partial amount is refused.
- **A declared level 0–8** picks the jar's own `tank0…tank8` textures, and `/rftoolsutility info|tank` reads and sets the contents.

**Not yet ported**

- the mod's other four families: the teleporters, the screens and their 30 modules, the logic gates, the environmental controller, the spawner and the three crafters;
- the tank's own GUI (this slice uses the commands);
- fluid push/pull between neighbouring tanks (the slice is the bucket and tank loop).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 8, the matter beamers: a block that eats a stack of material and sends matter to a spawner it is linked to, which closes the feed half of the matter gate. The beamer reads a recipe's three material sources itself rather than trusting the recipe's older object form, and it carries the four living tags so the empty living form yields its own reduced amounts. Proven in game with parsed values across nine phases: a link to a stone block is refused, to a spawner four blocks away is made, a target twelve blocks away is refused and a beamer cannot link to itself; eight items and four thousand FE give exactly two sends, the store growing by two for the first material, two for the list form and three for the living form at its one and a half per block, with the buffer emptied; cobblestone is refused with both the items and the energy kept; no power and no redstone send nothing; and a broken beamer carries its link, its count, its energy and its contents back. Two defects in the reference are fixed rather than copied: it spends the energy before it knows the material is accepted and burns it on a refusal, and it consumes a zero-yield living item for no matter. The link is a command because no wrench exists in this port or its parent, and the twenty tick clock is the tick's own game time rather than a saved counter.

projects.name: Right-Click Crops
projects.summary: Right-click harvest for 16 plant families, with replanting and individual settings.
projects.description:
Harvest mature plants with a right-click, replant crops, and keep your garden growing.

### Features
- Supports 16 plant families.
- Replants crops using one planting item from the harvest, or from your inventory.
- Keeps the base of tall plants and the stems of pumpkins and melons.
- Lets you enable or disable each plant separately in **Options > Mods > Right-Click Crops > Config**.

### Supported plants
Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa, torchflower, pitcher crop, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp, twisting vines, weeping vines, pumpkin and melon.

### Good to know
- Harvesting works in survival, one targeted plant at a time.
- Without a suitable planting item, the crop is harvested but not replanted.
- Torchflower needs spare seeds; pitcher crop needs spare pitcher pods.
- Twisting and weeping vines can drop nothing when harvested by hand. Use shears for guaranteed drops.
- Bone meal, ordinary breaking and planting, sweet berries and glow berries keep their normal behaviour.

### Compatibility
For Minecraft 26.3. A WebAssembly mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, with nothing to build. Install it on every player's game for LAN play. Settings from the old native versions do not carry over. Tested Horizon builds and results: [Validation](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops/blob/main/VALIDATION.md).


[Watch the demo](https://youtu.be/kll-qvj5s54) · [Harvesting guide](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops/blob/main/docs/harvesting.md)

versions.changelog: WebAssembly mod on the new mod SDK: no build needed. Same harvesting for all 16 plant families; settings are on the mod's Config page and start ON. Validated in single-player and for LAN host and guest.

projects.summary: The three Roots Classic herbs, the jar's herb-forage table, and the food, effects and recipes built on them.
projects.description:
A port of [Roots Classic](https://github.com/Lothrazar/RootsClassic) by Elucent,
Lothrazar and Mrbysco for Horizon. This first slice is **the herbs and their
first uses** — the foraging loop and the food, not yet the rituals.

**Implemented so far**

projects.name: RReturn
projects.summary: Rewinds the world and player state to the last checkpoint on death.
projects.description:
Rewinds the world and player state to the last checkpoint when the player dies. Blocks, containers, entities, weather, time, dimensions, and inventory are restored to their state at the checkpoint.

### How it works
- **Return by Death:** On fatal damage, the world rolls back to the last checkpoint instead of showing the death screen.
- **Checkpoints:** An initial checkpoint is created when entering a world. New checkpoints are saved automatically during safe periods, after combat, and after defeating a boss, or on a fixed timer.
- **Multiplayer modes:** On a LAN or server world, a key player's death rewinds the world for everyone on it. Supports single key player, multiple key players, all players, or rotating key player, with an optional rollback cooldown.
- **Manual control:** With cheats enabled, `F6` (`/rreturn set`) creates a checkpoint, `F7` (`/rreturn load`) rolls back, and `F8` switches the key player mode.
- **World data:** Checkpoints and logs are stored inside the world save folder (`rreturn/`) and mod settings are saved in the client configuration.

Settings and keybinds are in **Options > Mods**.

projects.summary: Keypads, reinforced doors and the rest of SecurityCraft's block protection, ported to Horizon.
projects.description:
A port of [SecurityCraft](https://github.com/Geforce132/SecurityCraft) (MIT, by Geforce132) for Horizon. This first slice brings the **keypad** and the **reinforced iron door**.

**Implemented so far**

- Place a keypad, open it and type a code on its on-screen keypad. The code is stored **salted and hashed**, never in plain text: the typed digits live in memory only while the screen is open, and the block entity's saved compound holds just the salt and the digest — closing the screen, submitting, or saving the world cannot write a passcode to disk.
- The keypad powers a redstone signal for 60 ticks when the right code is entered, which opens a reinforced iron door placed beside it.
- A wrong code leaves the door closed; a keypad with no door powers but opens nothing; an empty code stores nothing; a bare hand cannot open the reinforced door.
- `/securitycraft info|code` for testing and for setting a code without the screen, with the carried keypad and door blocks, models, textures, language and recipe inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The owner and allowlist system (owner-only editing, allowlist modules, the `SECURITYCRAFT_OWNER` checks), and every other module.
- The reinforced block family beyond the iron door: reinforced stone, glass, stairs, slabs and the rest.
- The remaining machines (keycard reader, retina scanner, camera, alarm, laser block, inventory scanner, …) and their screens.
- The keypad's screen is drawn from shape primitives (panel, key grid, digits) rather than the jar's GUI atlas.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/securitycraft/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, the owner gate on setting a code: a keypad's code can now only be set by the player who owns it, at the moment the set screen would open and again when the code is submitted, which is the reference's two checks rather than one. Proven in game with the three refusals and their reasons: a stranger's right click opens no screen at all, a stranger's submit stores nothing, and a stranger's command answers that only the owner may set the code, while the owner's submit sets it and the check reads back. A keypad with no owner matches nobody, which is recorded rather than guessed. The testing needed a harness-only command that puts a stranger's identity in front of the block, because a single-player run has only one player; that command is op-gated and exists only for the leg. This version also carries the lock file its declared dependency needs, and its own clean build compiles from the archive.

projects.name: Server Flags
projects.summary: A flag beside each server in the Multiplayer list for the country it's hosted in
projects.description:
A small flag beside each server in your Multiplayer list for the country it's hosted in. Hover the flag for the country's name, and pick servers close to you for a better ping at a glance.

- **Pixel-art flags** after each server's name, or on its icon when the name is long.
- **67 drawn flags**, the countries servers are most often hosted in; any other country shows its two-letter code.
- **Country name on hover**, like "Germany (DE)".
- Private and local IP addresses are never sent to the country lookup service.
- A grey **?** marks a server whose location can't be shown; hover it for why (an ad blocker blocking the lookup, DDoS protection, or a wrong address).

Settings in Mods > Server Flags > Config: lookups on/off, flag position, hover tooltip, codes for countries without a flag.

**Privacy:** Location lookups are on by default. The mod resolves saved server hostnames through your configured DNS resolver. For a hostname with no explicit port, it first asks for a Minecraft SRV record using the system's `nslookup`. Eligible hostnames can be queried before the mod checks whether the resolved IP is local. For a public address, it sends only the resolved server IP to https://api.country.is (open source, no account or key) to get a country code. Local IPs, including IPv4 addresses written as IPv6, are never sent to that service. Lookups run in the background once per server per game session while "Look up server locations" is on. A failed lookup can retry up to three times, with one minute between attempts. Turning lookups off stops new jobs, and a job already in progress may finish. The country request uses `curl --disable` so it ignores your `.curlrc`.

The request is made by the system's `curl` program (built into Windows 10 and 11, macOS and most Linux systems), run with only the service address and the server's IP. Rust's HTTPS libraries bring a second copy of a native library the game already has, which a mod may not link. From 2.0.8, `curl` and `nslookup` are run only from the system's own folders (Windows\System32; /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, /run/current-system/sw/bin), never through PATH, and each is stopped after a few seconds; at most four lookups run at once, and the lookup setting is checked again before each step that sends anything.

Horizon has no hook for the server list, so besides the mod API this mod patches one game function (draw_title_screen_with_post_hook) to draw the flags. It works on the Horizon build it is made for.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/server-flags

Inspired by Server Country Flags by Khajiitos (https://modrinth.com/mod/server-country-flags). Written from scratch for Horizon: it contains none of its code or images (the flags are drawn in code) and is not made or endorsed by Khajiitos. Locations by country.is.

versions.changelog: Only public addresses are ever looked up: an IPv6 site-local address could still be sent before; now any address that is not globally reachable unicast (your own network, site-local, multicast, documentation and other special-use ranges) never is, nor are 6to4 addresses, the IETF protocol block 2001::/23 or the old 192.88.99.0/24 relay range. From 2.0.8: curl and nslookup run only from the system's own folders, never through PATH; each is stopped after a few seconds; at most four lookups run at once; the lookup setting is checked again before each step that sends anything. Built for Nightly 2026-11-22 f1bb66f.

projects.name: sfm
projects.summary: A Horizon port of sfm.
projects.description:
A port of [Super Factory Manager](https://github.com/TeamDman/SuperFactoryManager) (MPL-2.0, by TeamDman and the SFM contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Factory Manager** and the plain inventory cable: the program text, the label table the upstream disk holds, a compiled subset of SFML, and the item movement one program tick makes over the cable network.

**Implemented so far**

- The Factory Manager and the plain inventory cable, with the carried models, textures and language entries, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.
- A compiled SFML subset: `NAME "…"`, `EVERY <n> TICKS|SECONDS DO … END` (`SECONDS` is 20 ticks, offset 0, `LOCAL` alignment), `INPUT`/`OUTPUT` with an optional quantity, `EACH`, `RETAIN n [EACH]`, a resource list (`stone`, `minecraft:redstone`, `*ingot*`), `EXCEPT …`, a label list (bare or quoted), a `SIDE` list, and `FORGET`.
- Upstream's defaults: `INPUT` takes all and leaves none, `OUTPUT` accepts all it is offered.
- Item movement between the labelled inventories of one cable network, one program tick at a time, through the pin's hopper-rule helpers.

**Not yet ported**

- The rest of the language: `IF`/`THEN`/`ELSE`, `REDSTONE TRIGGER`, `EMPTY SLOTS IN`, slot ranges, `ROUND ROBIN`, per-block `EACH`, quoted regex patterns, `MAX`/`EACH` on retention per id combination, `WITH` clauses, fluid/energy/chemical/redstone resources, and the `SIDE` forms `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FRONT`/`BACK` (they parse and name no face here).
- The rest of the content: the disk, label gun, network tool, form and form base, printing press, buffers, water tank, XP goop and shard, the fancy/tough/tunnelled cables, every facade, their recipes, loot and advancements, `c:` tag compatibility, and the Manager's and printing press's GUIs and data recipes.

MPL-2.0, like the original; the full licence and the original copyright notice travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository. Later slices cover the language and the remaining content.

projects.name: Silent Gear
projects.summary: Assemble a pickaxe from a blueprint, head and rod; its stats fold the material properties.
projects.description:
A port of [Silent Gear](https://github.com/SilentChaos512/Silent-Gear) (MIT, by SilentChaos512) for Horizon. This first slice is gear assembly and the tool stat block, for **one tool**: the pickaxe.

**Implemented so far**

- `/silentgear assemble pickaxe <head> <rod>` assembles a pickaxe from a carried blueprint, head and rod; the three are taken from the inventory (then the off hand) and consumed.
- The pickaxe's stats are folded from each material's properties with Silent Gear's own maths — weighted average, max, multiply-base, multiply-total and add, clamped — and the result is written into the item's `silentgear:gear` component.
- The material table is the jar's own data for iron, wood, stone, diamond, gold, flint and the empty netherite entry.
- The two-part recipe chain is craftable: `silentgear:blueprint_paper` (4 paper + a blue dye, from the jar), the pickaxe blueprint from it, the heads and the rods.
- `/silentgear stats` prints the held gear's folded stats, tier and durability.

**Not yet ported, and one hard limitation**

- **The assembled pickaxe always behaves as a vanilla iron pickaxe.** The pin has no per-stack tool stats — a tool's speed, harvest tier and durability are read from the item, not from the stack's components (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §3) — so the folded numbers are a readout, not the mining behaviour. Assembly refuses a head/rod combination whose folded stats differ from the vanilla iron pickaxe rather than silently producing an item that would not honour them. This is the slice's biggest gap.
- The other tools and armour, traits, grading, salvage, compound parts and the custom recipe types, the blueprint book and the gear-slot system are later slices.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/silentgear/LICENSE`.

projects.name: Simple Backups
projects.summary: Scheduled, on-disk backups of the whole world, with retention. A backup saves the open world, then a worker thread walks the world folder into a…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Simple Backups 1.21-4.0.30: scheduled, on-disk backups of the server's world, with retention. A backup saves the open world, a worker thread walks the world folder into a `.zip.part`, publishes it by renaming, and the oldest archives are pruned down to the configured count. Upstream: https://github.com/ChaoticTrials/SimpleBackups — licence **Apache-2.0**.

**Implemented so far**

- The schedule counts server ticks when `interval_ticks` is set and otherwise uses `interval_minutes` of wall clock, with 0 disabling it, and due checks run at the end of a running tick.
- A save is requested from the open levels before the copy, and the copy starts only when the save cycle reports back.
- A worker thread writes `<world>/backups/<world>_<UTC>.zip.part` and publishes it by renaming, skipping `session.lock`, `.part` and `.tmp` files, symlinks and the backups folder.
- Retention prunes only `<world>_*.zip` files, oldest first, until `keep` remain, and never touches foreign files or a partial archive.
- A copy that a save overlapped is thrown away and redone, up to two retries, instead of publishing a possibly half-replaced region file; with retries off it is published and `/simplebackups status` reports `stale=true`.
- `/simplebackups backup [quiet]`, `status` and `list` work at permission level 2, a manual backup ignores `enabled`, and `config/simplebackups.toml` carries the schedule, `keep`, `compression_level`, `save_before_backup`, `retry_on_save`, `broadcast`, `backups_dir` and the ignore lists.
- Paths are hardened: an absolute or parent-traversing `backups_dir` is refused, and a backups folder or staging file that resolves outside the world is never written through.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control run that fails without it.

**Not yet ported**

- The consistency window cannot be closed, because there is no save-off or autosave-veto API at this pin, so a copy can still overlap an autosave and read a region file mid-replacement, a race upstream has too.
- Compression is unavailable, because an SDK mod may not add a registry crate, so the archive is written with `std` alone and entries are stored rather than deflated, which means `compression_level` is parsed and reported but cannot shrink a backup.
- The schedule is not persisted across restarts and starts at world open.
- Pause and unpause, `latest.log` capture, a disk-size cap, the empty-server policy, incremental backups, chains and merging, Cherished Worlds and mc2discord compat, regex ignores, and a synchronous copy mode are all deferred.
- Retention prunes after a successful publish and counts only the mod's own archives, both deliberate safety changes from upstream's delete-before-create behaviour.
- Naming is UTC and backups live in `<world>/backups`, where upstream used local time and the working directory.

Ported from the upstream mod (Apache-2.0); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: SkinsRestorer
projects.summary: Players change their skin on a Horizon server; the signed textures property is replaced before login.
projects.description:
SkinsRestorer lets players on a Horizon server change their skin. A stored skin replaces the player's signed `textures` property at login, before the server sends the profile, so the player's own client and everyone in the player list see it.

- `/skin set <name>` resolves a Minecraft account through the game's own profile resolver and stores its signed skin.
- `/skin clear` restores the player's own skin; `/skin update` refreshes the stored name; `/skin` shows what is stored.
- Operators can set or clear another player's skin.

The lookup runs in the background on the server tick, so the server never waits on Mojang. Skins are stored in `config/skinsrestorer/skins.json`.

This is a server-side native mod for the Horizon mod API. It is made for Nightly `8f83e5c` (2026-11-21), the first signed build with the `player_login_profile` hook and the `profiles` service from horizon-rust/horizon#18587. It is based on SkinsRestorer and licensed under GPL-3.0.

projects.name: solcarrot
projects.summary: A Horizon port of solcarrot.
projects.description:
A port of [Spice of Life: Carrot Edition](https://github.com/Cazsius/Spice-of-Life-Carrot-Edition) (LGPL-2.1, by Cazsius, Talonos, juliand665 and Mrbysco) for Horizon. This first slice is the food history and the max-health milestones it earns.

**Implemented so far**

- A history per player: a set of food **item ids**. A food is recorded when it finishes being eaten, and re-eating it adds nothing. Filtered foods (below the nutrition floor, blacklisted, or outside a non-empty whitelist) are still remembered but do not count, exactly as upstream's `FoodList.addFood` does.
- Milestones: `milestones` (default `5,10,15,20,25`) count unique counted foods. Each reached milestone grants `2 * hearts_per_milestone` health points on top of vanilla's 20; a `base_hearts` other than 10 adds `2 * (base_hearts - 10)` to the same modifier, so at the defaults 25 foods give 10 extra hearts.
- The modifier is reapplied on join, respawn and dimension change, and cleared on death when `reset_on_death` is on.
- The history is saved per world in `<world>/solcarrot/foods.tsv` (one line per player and food), flushed after every new food and on world close, so `/foodlist size` works for an offline player too.
- A `config/solcarrot.conf` `key = value` file with the upstream keys and defaults (`base_hearts`, `hearts_per_milestone`, `milestones`, `minimum_food_value`, the `blacklist`/`whitelist`, `reset_on_death`, `limit_progression_to_survival`).
- `/foodlist size|sync|clear [target]`.

**Not yet ported**

- The **food book** item, its recipe and its screen: the whole client half, with its tooltips, progress list and the "next milestone" line.
- The client sync packet upstream sends when the history changes; the server keeps the authority and `/foodlist sync` refreshes the count.
- Sounds and particles on a milestone.
- Using a per-player attachment instead of the world text file (the pin's attachments are online-only, while the file keeps `/foodlist` working for offline players).

LGPL-2.1-only, like the original; the licence text and the original copyright notice travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository.

projects.name: Solis PBR
projects.summary: Realistic PBR shader pack: physical sky, 3D clouds, Total Solar Eclipse (5800), coloured shadows, water caustics, puddles & AgX.
projects.description:
Realistic, physically-based WGSL shader pack built from scratch for Horizon's final **Shader API 0.2** (linear HDR pipeline).

## Features

- **Physical Sky & Celestial Bodies:** Rayleigh/Mie atmospheric scattering, HDR sun with limb darkening, cratered 3D moon with phases & earthshine, rotating starfield, Milky Way and cold-biome Aurora Borealis.
- **Total Solar Eclipse at `5800`:** Run `/time set 5800` for a 20-second Total Solar Eclipse with magnetic coronal streamers, H-alpha prominences, Diamond Ring flash, 360° twilight horizon and daytime stars.
- **The End & Relativistic "Gargantua" Black Hole:** Full End dimension overhaul featuring curved-spacetime Schwarzschild gravitational lensing, pitch-black Event Horizon, Photon Ring, Doppler-beamed golden Keplerian accretion disk, Einstein-lensed starfield, IMAX anamorphic flare, water reflections and directional GGX End lighting.
- **3D Volumetric Clouds:** Perlin-Worley cumulus clouds with Beer-Powder multi-scattering, temporal reprojection and high-altitude cirrus.
- **Lighting & Shadows:** Soft rotated Vogel-disk PCF shadows, stained-glass & water coloured shadows, normal-aware SSAO, coloured block lights, dynamic hand/particle lights and glowing mineral ore veins.
- **Water & Rain:** Multi-wave Gerstner normals, depth-checked refraction, Beer-Lambert spectral absorption, Voronoi seabed caustics, shore foam, planar water mirror, wet porous darkening, rain puddles with ripples and Screen-Space Reflections (SSR).
- **LabPBR & Camera:** LabPBR normal/specular/emission support with geometric relief, foliage wind, volumetric god rays, Karis HDR bloom, FXAA and AgX / ACES / Neutral tonemapping (48 in-game options).

## GPU Requirements

*No hardware Ray Tracing (RTX) required — runs on Vulkan 1.2 / DirectX 12 / Metal.*

- **Minimum (1080p ~60 FPS, 1024 shadows, Fast clouds):** GTX 1050 Ti / RX 560 / Intel Iris Xe / Radeon 680M / Apple M1 / Steam Deck (2 GB+ VRAM)
- **Recommended (1080p 90+ FPS / 1440p 60+ FPS):** GTX 1660 Super / RTX 2060 / RX 6600 / Intel Arc A580 / Apple M2+ (4–6 GB VRAM)
- **Ultra / 4K (4096 shadows):** RTX 3060 Ti / RTX 4060 / RX 6700 XT or higher (8 GB+ VRAM)

projects.description:
Sophisticated Backpacks and Sophisticated Storage with their shared library Sophisticated Core, in one package. Backpacks in six tiers keep their contents in the item: open one from the hand, with the Open Backpack key (J; the worn backpack first, then the first one in the inventory) or placed on the ground. Chests, barrels, limited barrels and shulker boxes come in six tiers and eleven woods; they are upgraded in place, packed with packing tape and reached by hoppers. A worn backpack isn't drawn on the player, mobs don't spawn with backpacks, and placed backpacks have no hopper access. Dyed storage is drawn untinted (the colours are kept), the controller, storage link, I/O blocks and decoration table are plain blocks, and flat-top barrels and barrel materials aren't ported.

A port of [Sophisticated Core](https://github.com/Salandora/SophisticatedCore) 1.2.7.15.166, [Sophisticated Backpacks](https://github.com/Salandora/SophisticatedBackpacks) 3.23.4.5.110 and [Sophisticated Storage](https://github.com/Salandora/SophisticatedStorage) 1.3.5.11.142 (Fabric 1.20.1) by P3pp3rF1y, Ridanisaurus, Salandora, published under their licence, GPL-3.0. projects.name: sound_physics_remastered
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Sound Physics Remastered.
projects.description:
Behavioral port of [Sound Physics Remastered](https://github.com/henkelmax/Sound-Physics-Remastered) (GPL-3.0-only) for the Horizon client. Port repo: `Sparticle62ops/horizon-sound-physics-remastered`; master copy in `horizon-modport/ports/sound-physics-remastered`.

## Status
- [x] Slice 1: the pure sound physics. Per-block sound materials (absorption + reflectivity from the block's sound type), direct-path occlusion raymarching (half-block sampling, one hit per voxel), distance falloff, and raytraced reverb estimation (deterministic LCG rays, bounce budget, mean-free-path decay). 10/10 tests.
- [ ] Slice 2: client glue, feeding the physics from Horizon's world snapshot and applying the computed occlusion/reverb to sound playback.

## Degradations
- Client-side world access for the raymarcher rides world snapshots (horizon-rust/horizon #10152, open).
- SPR hooks Minecraft's client sound engine to resample each played sound's volume/reverb per position; Horizon's native mod API has no sound playback hook yet. The client glue (slice 2) waits on that surface; filed: horizon-rust/horizon #10444 (sound playback hook).
- Nothing calls the physics yet, so players see no effect; slice 2 lands with the sound playback hook.

Package rebuilt on the current SDK (Horizon f00125f61f794aaa3d4e950d301f353b35b6ee3d, mixins e59da9094f0c2fdda6c627fe9eff22dec6a906f0) with a real `mod_api` entry in `lib.rs`; the package source and the repo match.

Licence: GPL-3.0-only, carrying upstream's license and credit. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-sound-physics-remastered

projects.name: stepcrafter
projects.summary: A Horizon port of stepcrafter.
projects.description:
A port of [Step Crafter](https://github.com/starforcraft/Step-Crafter) by Ultramega (Starforcraft).

The first port of Step Crafter, and it opens with the family the mod exists for: a machine that keeps a stock of one target item inside a minimum and maximum band by crafting one step at a time from its own inventory. Set the target and the band, load the ingredients, and it crafts until the maximum and then holds rather than overshooting; empty one ingredient and it reports not enough ingredients and resumes when the stock returns. Proven in game across a full band and a half one: a zero to sixteen run in steps of four consumes exactly four coal and four sticks and holds over sixty more ticks, taking eight torches moves them to the inventory, and a sixty-four to one-hundred-and-twenty-eight band fills to one hundred and twenty-eight with the active state reading true while running and false when idle. A survival break drops the machine and spills its eight torches, a non-operator is refused, and the carried recipe crafts with its ingredients consumed while a wrong grid makes nothing. Two things were only visible in game and are recorded rather than hidden: a stock kept in the block entity's own saved compound was lost between ticks, so it moved to a container the engine owns, and a moved machine must be re-targeted because a container block lets the engine spill rather than carrying a payload. The parts that need the parent's autocrafting network are recorded as blocked with their symbols instead of being shipped inert.

versions.changelog: This version gives the crafter a facing state, read from the artefact's twelve blockstate variants: six directions crossed with active on and off, each with its own model rotation. The direction is the clicked face, not yaw or its opposite, and is set at placement through the pin's state hook. Proven on two placements: north reads north and passes a north predicate, south reads south and fails north, while vanilla stone has no such state. A first draft attached one part type twice and the launcher refused the game; a dedicated placement part fixed it and the whole ladder was rebuilt. The remaining gap families all need a Refined Storage grid or upgrade surface the pin does not expose, so this port waits for a repin rather than a speculative slice.

projects.name: sushigocrafting
projects.summary: A Horizon port of sushigocrafting.
projects.description:
A port of [Sushi Go Crafting](https://github.com/Buuz135/SushiGoCrafting) (MIT, by Buuz135 and the Sushi Go Crafting contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **cutting board**, the mod's smallest machine loop: an ingredient in, six knife strokes, the prepared item out.

**Implemented so far**

- `sushigocrafting:cutting_board` on the `minecraft:oak_planks` template with upstream's own numbers (hardness 3.0, blast resistance 3.0, wooden sounds, no occlusion), the four-way `subfacing` state the jar's blockstate selects on unchanged, and upstream's two outline/collision shapes (north/south and east/west).
- Placement rotation: `subfacing` follows the placer's yaw, as upstream's placement code does.
- The board's block entity (one item slot plus the saved knife-stroke count) and its one-slot container, reachable from every face, with no menu — upstream's shape exactly.
- The interaction, in upstream's order: a knife on a loaded board adds a stroke; an ingredient on an empty board fills the slot; sneak with an empty hand takes the stack back. The sixth stroke cuts: the recipe's amount item, with `sushigocrafting:amount` rolled between the recipe's minimum and maximum, goes to the player and one ingredient leaves the slot.
- The jar's six cutting-board recipes, the block and the eleven item models/textures, the lang strings, the tags and the loot table, all carried and shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/sushigocrafting board|clicks` readout and stroke setter for testing (upstream has no commands).

**Not yet ported**

- The other four machines: `rice_cooker`, `fermentation_barrel`, `roller` and `cooler_box`.
- Every crop (rice, cucumber, soy, sesame, wasabi) and the avocado tree. A content crop does not random-tick at this pin, so growth and drops are not ported and the crop blocks were not carried; the board's ingredients therefore come from creative or from another mod.
- The fish and their drops (`ShrimpEntity`, `TunaEntity`, the sushi food items), the Patchouli guide book, and the knife tiers beyond the tag.
- The board's client renderer (the item on the board and the knife animation) and the per-`subfacing` model orientation; there is no screen upstream.
- `container_accepts` is still pending at this pin, so a hopper can insert an item the board would refuse by hand.

Knives are accepted under both `c:tools/knife` (upstream's spelling) and `c:tools/knives` (what the mod's own data declares), so the mod's own cleaver cuts on its own board without Farmer's Delight. MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/sushigocrafting/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the fermentation barrel: the port's first machine with a fluid in it. One input, one output, a 2,000 mB tank and a 100-tick bar; a soy bean or an empty slot picks the soy or the cheese recipe, the tank must hold the recipe's own fluid and enough of it, an output already holding the item rolls up to its cap, and finishing drains a batch and rolls the output. It is the machine of the four whose own recipe is all-vanilla, so it is the one that can be crafted in a bare 26.3. Proven in game: the block places from its item and reads back; 7 oak planks, a pressure plate and a furnace craft exactly one barrel with the grid consumed, and the same ingredients in another pattern craft nothing; milk through a bucket and a soy bean through the menu reach the tank and the slot, and 100 ticks turn them into cheese and soy sauce with the buffers asserted before and after; a bean with no water runs 120 ticks and produces nothing; and `/sushigocrafting tank` clamps 2,500 to 2,000. Two engine facts are recorded rather than worked around: milk is not a fluid Horizon models, so the port moves that bucket itself while water and lava go through the engine path, and `Action.FILL` is taken at its word so a bucket never drains the tank.

projects.name: theurgy
projects.summary: A Horizon port of theurgy.
projects.description:
A port of [Theurgy](https://github.com/klikli-dev/theurgy) (MIT for the code, CC-BY-SA-4.0 for the assets — by klikli-dev) for Horizon. This first slice is the **calcination** chain: the pyromantic brazier, the calcination oven and the alchemical salts they produce.

**Implemented so far**

- `theurgy:pyromantic_brazier` (the `minecraft:copper_block` template, declaring `lit`): one fuel slot, ticking exactly as upstream's `PyromanticBrazierBlockEntity.tickServer` — burn down first (`remainingLitTime -= 1`), then, only when out, load the next item's burn time and consume one item (a crafting remainder such as a lava bucket's bucket replaces it). `lit = remaining > 0`, written to the block state only when it changes. One coal or charcoal is **1,600 ticks, 16 calcination crafts**.
- `theurgy:calcination_oven` (the same template, declaring `lit`): input slot 0, output slot 1; the heat source is the block **below** being a lit brazier, sampled every tick.
- The calcination recipes the jar ships for the carried items, with their alchemical salt outputs, plus the carried models, textures, language, recipes and loot inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/theurgy` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

- The other nine processes: distillation (mercury shards, 45 recipes), liquefaction (sulfurs, 358, needing the sal ammoniac fluid), fermentation (286), digestion (31), incubation (287), reformation (631), accumulation (4) and catalysation (2) — with their machines, fluids and menus.
- The other items: 287 alchemical sulfurs, 19 niters, the mercury shard and crystal, purified gold, jars, divination rods (4 tiers × 4 attunements), filters and ceramic jars.
- The apparatus not carried: distiller, liquefaction cauldron, fermentation vat and the rest; and the guide book.

projects.name: Time in a Bottle
projects.summary: A bottle that stores time and spends it to accelerate a furnace at up to 128x, with the jar's own caps.
projects.description:
A port of [Time in a Bottle](https://github.com/RealMangorage/time-in-a-bottle) by RealMangoRage for Horizon. A bottle that stores time and spends it to accelerate a block.

**Implemented so far**

- **`tiab:time_in_a_bottle`** — a clock-template item carrying its own `tiab:stored_time` component, with the jar's cap of **622,080,000 ticks** and **20 ticks stored per second** while it sits in the inventory.
- **Spending it** — one use costs **exactly 600** stored ticks and runs the target **600 game ticks** at rate 1; clicking again doubles the rate (and the cost), up to the jar's 128x; creative mode pays nothing.
- **Acceleration** — the furnace's own tick routine is run `rate` times per game tick, following the block's `lit` state and dropping fuel remainders; `#tiab:un_acceleratable` (chest, grass block) is refused.
- **Commands** — `/tiab time add|remove <player> <seconds>` (level 2) and `/tiab info <x> <y> <z> <n>` for a one-line clock/account/furnace readout.

**Not yet ported**

- There is no mod entity at this pin, so the accelerator is per-block state on `level_tick_post`: it is not saved with the world and shows no floating text or sound.
- Only furnace-class targets (furnace, smoker, blast furnace) — hoppers, campfires and other random-ticking blocks are not accelerated.
- No config file (the upstream defaults are constants here), no JEI/EMI integration, and the command reaches only the acting player.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository (MIT, RealMangoRage). Pinned to Horizon `1d63e0a` and horizon-mixins `5a64af93` for game 26.3.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the campfire family: campfires and soul campfires are now accelerated targets beside the furnace family. A lit campfire's four cooking timers advance by the game ticks plus the delivered ticks, an unlit one cools two ticks a tick, and a timer stops at its cooking time; the click acceptance, the tick check and the readout all name the family now, so a click on a chest is no longer claimed. Proven in game: over 105 game ticks the accelerated campfire's timer advanced 210 against the control's 134, the accelerated potato finished and dropped while the control was still cooking at 406, and the bottle recipe crafts with both controls empty. This version also corrects an over-tight assertion in the existing furnace leg: a cook that starts exactly at its cooking time completes and discards the increment it added, so the fast-forward can lose up to one tick per completed cook — measured as 59 of 60 sampled intervals exact and one short by exactly one — and the legs now bound by rate times cooks instead of demanding exactness. That is the honest shape, and it replaced an assertion that would have failed intermittently.

projects.name: Tool Belt
projects.summary: A belt that holds two to nine stacks of tools on your person, with its own menu and commands.
projects.description:
A port of [Tool Belt](https://github.com/gigaherz/ToolBelt) by gigaherz for Horizon — this slice is the belt item and its on-item storage.

- The belt holds two to nine slots. Hold it and right-click with an allowed item in your off hand to insert it; sneak-right-click to take the first slot back out; right-click otherwise to open a menu that lists the belt's contents.
- Allowed means upstream's rule: non-stackable items by default, no bundles and no other belts; equal stacks with the same components merge into one slot.
- The size and contents live in two item components, so a belt keeps its slots and their positions when it travels between players and machines.
- An extraction only removes what the player's inventory (or a guest's) actually accepted, and insertion moves the real stacks, so a full inventory never deletes a tool and a named or damaged tool keeps its name, enchantments and damage.
- `/toolbelt put|take|info|menu` for headless testing.

The radial key menu, wearing it on a curios slot, the upgrades and the pouch are later slices. BSD-3-Clause — the original copyright, conditions and disclaimer travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/toolbelt/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the pouch and the anvil upgrade: the pouch item and its recipe, and the forge-anvil path that grows a belt from two slots to nine. The upgrade costs are the jar's own — 3, 5, 8, 12, 15, 20 and 30 experience levels — and a belt at nine slots refuses a tenth pouch. The sewing-kit upgrades stay out because `neoforge:mod_loaded sewingkit` is not in the registry, and the config family is still a gap, so the port behaves as upstream's AUTO default. Proven in game: the belt and pouch recipes craft with their ingredients consumed, a wrong pattern crafts nothing, the anvil returns a belt at the next size with the cost taken from the player's level (2 to 3 for 3 levels; 8 to 9 for 30) and the pouch count falling, and a nine-slot belt with a pouch returns no result and consumes nothing. This version also fixes a `uses` record: a local `CommandArgumentValue::Item` match was recorded as building the SDK `Item` field by field, which made `fits` against another build refuse the package; the match now lives in a small macro the scan does not expand, so `type:Item` records `built: none` and `0b14f8a fits`.

A port of [Torchmaster](https://github.com/Xalcon/TorchMaster) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The **Dread Lamp** and the terrasteel/mega-torch family's carried blocks, models, textures and recipes from the jar.
- The lights are persisted per world (a `lights.tsv` file beside the world), block changes register and prune them, and the spawn veto answers through the pin's `potential_spawns` hook with an installed minimal API shim.
- `/torchmaster info` reports the registered lights and their ranges.

**Not yet ported**

- **Spawners are deliberately not blocked.** Upstream's `blockOnlyNaturalSpawns` defaults to true and the pin's pre-spawn hook only fires for the natural path; the "block spawners too" mode has no hook and is not carried.
- **Phantoms and village sieges.** Upstream also vetoes phantom spawns and village sieges; the latter has a pin hook (village_siege), but phantoms do not pass through `potential_spawns`. Both are later slices.
- The faint/feral lantern variants and the config file are not carried.

versions.changelog: Carry-dialect repair: two recipes and two loot tables were in the 1.21.1 dialect. `megatorch` used the object ingredient form 26.3 rejects, so the mod's centrepiece could not be crafted, and both tables carried the array `"conditions"`, so the blocks dropped nothing. Converted. Proven in game: `megatorch` crafts with a diamond consumed and drops itself, while the pre-fix package failed both — `expected 1 torchmaster:megatorch, got None` and `dropped 0 of torchmaster:megatorch`.

projects.description:
Explore with a minimap and a world map that remembers visited terrain. Find waypoints by name, organize them into groups, and jump to their map locations from the waypoint list.

- **M** opens the world map, **N** opens the waypoint list, **K** adds a waypoint, and **Y** opens minimap settings. The waypoint panel opens from the bottom-right corner of the world map.
- Filter waypoints by dimension, share waypoint links, and enable automatic death waypoints. Import tools read supported map, settings, and waypoint formats from existing Xaero data.
- On servers, the map can select a different terrain cache and waypoint list when the server reports a distinct world. Choose or bind a map manually in **M → Server worlds**.
- Right-click the world map to build it from the generated chunks of a local save or a copy of a server save. Mob icons use textured 3D models.
- In 0.1.11, **F2** edits the selected waypoint and **/mapdeaths** shows recent death waypoints.
- English is the default. The interface also follows supported game languages.
- Requires Minecraft Java Edition 26.3 and the matching Horizon Nightly. Use 0.1.17 for the November 22 build `f1bb66f`, 0.1.13 for the November 22 build `2b77287`, 0.1.10 for November 21 (`8f83e5c`) or 0.1.0 for November 20 (`0a875da`).

projects.name: transfer_labels
projects.summary: A Horizon port of transfer_labels.
projects.description:
A port of [Transfer Labels](https://github.com/Buuz135/Transfer-Labels) (MIT, by Buuz135) for Horizon. This first slice is the **item-stack extract label**.

**Implemented so far**

- `transfer_labels:itemstack_extract_transfer_label`, attached by right-clicking a block face with the label in hand (one item is used up) and removed by left-clicking the labelled face with the label in hand, which returns the item and the copies its upgrades stand for. Cancelling the click is what keeps a chest from opening and the block from breaking.
- One label moves items out of the block it is attached to, on `level_tick_pre`, once per label when `gameTime % (20 - min(speed, 38) / 2) == 0`: one item every 20 ticks with no upgrades, one a tick at 38 speed upgrades. Each operation moves `1 + amount` items (1 to 64) through the pin's hopper-rule helpers, so an item the destination refuses stays in its slot and nothing is lost.
- Filters: whitelist or blacklist (blacklist is the default, as upstream), with the `normal` (same item id), `mod` (same namespace) and `regulating` (keep N at the destination, at most 4 per operation) kinds, 20 slots and one count per slot.
- Labels are level state, saved with the dimension's attachments, so a label survives a save and a reload.
- `/transfer_labels list|info|filter|type|entry|clear|amount|speed|remove` configures a label by position and face (upstream configures it in a GUI this slice does not carry).

**Not yet ported**

- The `tag` and `exact_count` filter kinds: `runtime.rs` names and refuses them instead of silently moving nothing. There is no item-tag lookup helper at this pin, and `exact_count` gathers one item from several source slots, which the hopper helper cannot do.
- The label's menu and screen. The command path sets the amount and speed upgrade counts without consuming label items, where upstream puts the upgrade items in slots; the economy contract of that path is not exposed as a player feature.
- The insert label, the four fluid labels and the label-to-label conversions; the client billboard and its own click shape; removing a label when its block is broken; and comparing item components in the filter (the filter matches the item id, plus the namespace for `mod`).

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/transfer_labels/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the insert label: `itemstack_insert_transfer_label`, the other half of the mod's core mechanic, so both directions the jar ships now exist. Same carrier and same once-per-activation move as the extract label, with source and destination swapped: with a chest above and a labelled chest below, eleven items drop into the labelled one while the pair still holds exactly thirty-two between them, which is the invariant that proves nothing was created. The flow is saved and reads back as `flow=insert` after a relaunch, and an old saved label with no flow field reads as extract. Twelve carried recipes are crafted in game with their ingredients consumed and a wrong grid that makes nothing. Four fluid labels were deliberately left out: `enderstorage` measured that a tank write over the API is lost at this pin, so that half needs a re-measure, not a guess.

projects.name: The Twilight Forest
projects.summary: The Twilight Forest's portal and its dimension for Horizon: a water pool that a diamond lights into twilightforest:twilight_portal, and…
projects.description:
A partial Horizon port of The Twilight Forest 4.8.3345: the mod's portal and its dimension, with the dimension type, the biome source and the world data the jar ships. A water pool ringed by a plant-topped frame lights into `twilightforest:twilight_portal` when a diamond is dropped into it, and `twilightforest:twilight_forest` is registered with the jar's own dimension type and biome grid. Upstream: https://github.com/TeamTwilight/twilightforest — code **LGPL-2.1-or-later**; the upstream art is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, so no upstream art travels in this package.

**Implemented so far**

- The portal rule is upstream's own: four or more water blocks on a sturdy floor, ringed by grass, dirt, farmland or dirt path with a plant standing on each frame block, lit by a dropped diamond, at most 64 pool blocks.
- A protection gate runs before any write or lightning, so the ticked player must be allowed to build and use the item there, inside the world border and outside a dedicated server's spawn protection, and only that player's own drop counts as the catalyst.
- The lit portal block keeps upstream's light 11, no collision, glass sound and 0–13/16 outline, and the catalyst is consumed while lightning strikes the pool.
- The dimension uses the jar's dimension type: `min_y` −32, height 288, coordinate scale 0.125, ambient light 0.01, fixed time, no ceiling, skylight, monster spawn light 0–7, no raids, working beds and zombifying piglins.
- A biome source reproduces `twilightforest:twilight_biomes` by rebuilding the jar's whole layer stack over its biome grid in pure Rust, exactly for all 22 biomes, of which 14 are carried.
- The three `deadrock` blocks the jar's surface rule places are carried, and so are the surface rule and the noise settings, converted and ready for the terrain slice.
- The world data is registered as an always-active, hidden server data pack, so the biomes and the noise settings load in every world, and `/twilightforest dimension` prints the level, its biome count and the grid's answer for a cell.
- No packaged file is an upstream byte: every texture, model, blockstate, tag and lang file is written or drawn by the port's own tools, and a provenance check proves none of the 63 packaged files matches the jar's 10,437 entries.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1: the portal legs, the dimension and the readout pass, a game without the package lights nothing, and a selftest fails as designed.

**Not yet ported**

- The terrain is `blocked(density-function type)`, because the jar's density graph names two density-function types this pin's registry cannot decode and that registry loads atomically, so the chunk generator deliberately writes nothing and the level is empty rather than a vanilla stand-in.
- Eight of the 22 biomes are not carried, though the grid's placement is exact for all of them; a biome outside the carried set answers the nearest carried biome of its family.
- Decoration, carvers, structures, mobs, bosses, progression and the client effects are not carried, and the biomes' spawners are empty.
- The portal's travel is decided and unit-tested but not wired, because the destination has no terrain and a player sent there would fall out of the world.
- The dimension's fixed-time value and its sky effects cannot be expressed, because the pin's dimension settings have no field for them.

Ported from the upstream mod and published under LGPL-2.1-or-later with its complete corresponding source and the original copyright notice; `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the licence split and `PROVENANCE.md` the origin of every packaged file.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.
authors: Benimatic (Ben Mazur) and the Twilight Forest contributors

versions.changelog: First publication in the SDK format.

projects.name: twinsession
projects.summary: A Horizon port of TwinSession.
projects.description:
A Rust port of [TwinSession](https://github.com/TheMisterFish/Fabric_TwinSession)
(CC0-1.0, by TheMisterFish), which lets several clients join one server from the
same Minecraft account: the server mints each duplicate a fresh UUID and name so
they play side by side without kicking the original.

## Ported (1:1)

- The twin registry: live duplicates per original UUID, lowest free join
  position, cleanup on leave (TwinSession.twinMap, playerLeft).
- createNewGameProfile: the N_name name truncated to 16 chars, its MD5-v3 UUID
  (hand-rolled MD5, byte-exact with Java MessageDigest), the texture property
  copied when copyTexture is on, the number prefix toggle.
- canJoin with the original inequality (size + 1 < maxPlayers).
- The spawn-nearby placement: sample points in the configured radius, relaxed
  minimum distance, safe-Y scan top down, nether-roof guard, creative-flight
  passthrough, source-position fallback; the sampling loop is bounded so a
  radius of 2 or less terminates instead of stalling.
- All seven config values with the original defaults (maxPlayers 8,
  autoWhitelist on, autoOp on, spawnNearPlayer on, radius 10, copyTexture on,
  prefixWithNumber on).

## Horizon seam

The native-mod API hears a joining player once accepted through
native_player_login (API 172) and may cancel the join with a reason, but it
cannot rewrite the joining player's profile. The heart of TwinSession is that
rewrite: the duplicate's UUID is replaced before placement so two sessions of
one account coexist. Without it the port can detect a duplicate and place it
near the original, but cannot mint the fresh UUID and profile, so the mod does
nothing in game yet. It ships as the tested 1:1 library until that surface
lands (horizon-rust/horizon #10057).

Pinned to Horizon f00125f61f794aaa3d4e950d301f353b35b6ee3d and horizon-mixins e59da9094f0c2fdda6c627fe9eff22dec6a906f0.

Licence: CC0-1.0. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-twinsession

versions.changelog: Rebuilt on Horizon f00125f / mixins e59da90 (api 0.2): real mod_api entry, bounded spawn sampling, honest placeholder status (profile rewrite is horizon-rust/horizon #10057), CC0 text ships.

projects.description:

Read upstream at commit 233932b (ArmorHudConfig.java 134 ln,

projects.name: Universal Viewer
projects.summary: See inside maps, shulker boxes and bundles without opening them. Client-side, works on any server.
projects.description:
Look inside things without opening them.

- **Maps on their slot**: a loaded filled map shows its own picture as its inventory icon, edge to edge (inventory, chests, hotbar). The stack count stays on top. In the Creative screen, where the engine gives no slot positions, the mod places them from the vanilla layout: maps show along the hotbar row in every tab and across the whole inventory in the inventory tab; items in other tabs' grids keep their vanilla icon.
- **Map tooltip**: hovering a map adds its picture, inside the game's own held-map frame, to the normal tooltip, with its scale (1:1 to 1:16) and lock state. The picture can be shown at 64, 96 or 128 px (a setting; 128 by default). Every other tooltip line stays: vanilla's, a server's lore and prices, other mods'.
- **Shulker boxes and bundles**: hold **Shift** while hovering to see the full contents as a slot grid drawn like a vanilla inventory, tinted in the box's or bundle's colour, or **Alt** to see them as a list: one row per kind of item with its total, largest first. Hold **Ctrl** to lock the preview in place and hover its items (a setting switches to press-to-toggle). All three keys can be rebound on Options > Controls.
- **Slot marks**: a shulker box shows a fill bar under its icon, and shulker boxes and bundles show a small icon of the item they hold the most of (a setting picks both, either or none).
- **Ender chest memory**: the contents of an ender chest are remembered while it is open, per server or world, and shown when hovering an ender chest item, marked as last opened. Kept in memory only until the game closes.
- **Item search**: a field above the inventory and container screens outlines every slot whose item matches the typed name, or whose shulker box, bundle or remembered ender chest holds a match, and dims the rest (a setting hides it; not on the Creative screen, which has its own search).
- **Placed shulker boxes**: opening one tints the inventory panel and slots in the box's colour.

**What it does and does not do.** All rendering runs on the client. One mixin (HEAD of `remote_map_item_data`) copies the map pictures a server already sends to the client, and the game's own map colour palette, so maps show on vanilla servers; it changes nothing in the game's handling of the packet. Separately, the mod registers an optional payload pair (`universal_viewer:map_request` / `universal_viewer:map_data`): when the server also runs the mod (or in singleplayer), the client may ask it for a map's picture by id, so maps sitting in a chest show at once. The server answers only for a map the player can see (in their inventory or the menu they have open, including inside shulker boxes and bundles there), at most 10 replies per second per player; clients ask at most once every 2 ticks. A server without the mod never answers. No other network access, no files written (the ender chest memory lives in memory only), no data collected. It gives no advantage over what a player could see by holding the map or opening the box.

The mod ships no Minecraft data: map colours come from the running game and the frame is the game's own `map_background` sprite.

Pinned to Horizon f1bb66f (Nightly 2026-11-22) and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: universalgrid
projects.summary: A Horizon port of universalgrid.
projects.description: The first port of Universal Grid, a Refined Storage add-on with two items and no blocks, and it implements the family the mod exists for: the wireless universal grid, an energy-buffered item that opens a network's view from any distance. Bind it to a placed grid by right-clicking that block, then use it anywhere to open the same fifty-four slot network view as a native menu, withdrawing and depositing whole stacks while the parent's own grid tick stays the only writer to the network. The costs are the parent's: a thousand FE buffer, five to open and five per transfer, with the creative variant free. Proven in game with the parent installed: bind, walk twelve blocks away, open, and the view shows the stock it should while the energy falls from a thousand to nine hundred and eighty-five over three transfers and the network moves eight to five to seven items; a grid with three FE refuses to open, an unbound item refuses, the creative item opens at zero, and a broken grid is refused by its own name. Three behaviours the item would delegate to are recorded as blocked with their symbols, because the parent has not shipped the wireless grid, the wireless autocrafting monitor or the network-bound model property, and the jar's recipe is deliberately not carried since three of its five ingredients are those items and it could never match.

projects.name: Useful Stuff
projects.summary: Survival tools, a slingshot, customizable ammunition, quiver storage and a torch pouch.
projects.description:
Useful Stuff adds tools and ammunition to survival play, with 16×16 item artwork and a new original quiver design.

Use the obsidian hammer for directional 3×3 mining, cook eggs into food, collect drops with a held magnet, and carry torches in a four-stack pouch whose artwork changes when filled. The slingshot has four charge frames, first- and third-person poses, its own elastic snap and a matching subtitle. Flint is consumed when charging completes.

The fletching table has an offset flint junction and a diagonal arrow assembly. Combine different cores, shafts, dyes and 42 modifier ingredients for abilities including ricochets, fire, freezing, slowing, poison, glowing and levitation. Ability lore is color coded, and existing modified ammunition can be upgraded. The nine-stack quiver selects flint for the slingshot. Grasping I–IV recalls missed flint after progressively shorter delays and over greater distances.

Requires an SDK-capable Horizon Nightly; server compilation was verified on the Nov 22 SDK (2b77287), with the package authored and checked against the registry pin (f037744).

The review correction moves all owned IDs to useful_stuff and replaces the quiver with original artwork; temporary player/menu unavailability no longer discards fletching-session inputs.

This is an experimental native Horizon adaptation of the author's Java mod, not complete Java feature parity. Menus currently use Horizon's standard container screen. Automatic quiver feeding for bows/crossbows, ordinary base-potion conversion, the original potion brewing integration and the hammer's extra-block outline/crack rendering are not implemented. Protection compatibility and in-game visuals still require gameplay testing; no runtime-playtest claim is made. See the source README for the full compatibility notes.

Made by tjtjklra529 using MCreator originally, with this Horizon adaptation developed with AI assistance. Original mod: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/useful-stuff-tjtjklra529 . No Java loader or JVM is required by this native port.

versions.changelog: Review correction: unique useful_stuff namespace, original 16x16 quiver, retained fletching inputs and dimension-aware torch placement. Mod version remains 0.0.1.
