projects.name: Vast Adventures
projects.summary: Loot with rarities and affixes, gems and sockets, bosses, elites, rogue spawners and boss dungeons.
projects.description:
A native mod for an adventure layer over the game, built from the MIT code and data of [Apotheosis](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apotheosis)' adventure module (by Shadows_of_Fire), with names, words and art of its own, on Horizon's mod API. One package: the code, the gems, materials, seals, names in English and Brazilian Portuguese, and the world generation.

- **Affix loot**: chests, mob drops and fishing give weapons, tools and armour with a rarity (Common to Mythic) and affixes: attribute bonuses, status effects on hit or when hurt, damage reduction, enchantment bonuses, executing, thunderstruck, cleaving, radial mining, telepathic and festive drops, and combat stats (crit chance and damage, life steal, fire and cold damage, armour pierce and shred, dodge, healing received, experience gained, draw speed...). The tooltip shows them.
- **Gems and sockets**: 21 gems at six purities, socketed at the anvil.
- **Salvaging, reforging and gem cutting** at the grindstone and anvil, and the Seals of Sockets, Extraction and Erasure.
- **Bosses and elites**: now and then a monster is a boss with better stats, gear and a gem, or an elite; some bosses only in their biomes. `/vastadventures boss` summons one.
- **World tier** (`/vastadventures tier`: Calm, Wilds, Rising, Peril, Apex): one per world; higher tiers roll rarer loot and give luck.
- **Rogue spawners and boss dungeons** in new chunks (from the content mod); a boss dungeon's spawner becomes a boss when a player comes near.

**What it changes in the game**: loot tables (adds affix loot and gems), the player's attributes from their gear, melee and projectile damage, healing and block experience for the player, natural monster spawns (bosses and elites), the anvil and grindstone results, and block drops for radial and telepathic tools. It adds the `/vastadventures` command. Its combat stats are attributes of its own the game applies and shows like vanilla's. It works through the mod API (hooks, Parts and attributes; no mixins) and reads and writes only the world's `world_tier.txt` in its mod data folder; no network, no other files.

0.10.0 replaces 0.9.0's two files (`vastadventures_native` .hnmod and the `vastadventures` content mod); gear, gems and sockets made with 0.9 keep working, and a world's tier goes back to Calm until set again. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a. Not yet: the augmenting and reforging tables, the tier screen, and the effects Horizon has no equivalent for (listed in the README). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apotheosis' authors; none of its assets or lang are used.

versions.changelog: First release on Horizon's mod API: one native package (code and content). Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-18 (0b14f8a). Gear, gems and sockets made with 0.9 keep working; combat stats are now attributes of the mod's own. Setting the world tier needs an operator; socket counts and malformed item data are bounded; projectile effects only follow a permitted hit; cooldowns are cleared.

projects.name: Vast Packs
projects.summary: Backpacks: right-click to open like a chest, from 18 to 54 slots (and up to 180 in pages with Vast Depths); what they hold travels with them.
projects.description:
Backpacks on Horizon's mod API: hold one in your main hand, right-click, and it opens like a chest. One package: the code, the items, their sprites, recipes and names in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

| Backpack | Slots |
| --- | --- |
| Leather | 18 |
| Iron | 27 |
| Gold | 36 |
| Diamond | 45 |
| Netherite | 54 |
| Stellarite, Infernium, Voidium (need Vast Depths) | 90, 135, 180, in pages of 45 |

- **Upgrades** in the crafting grid (the backpack and a block of the next material) keep everything it holds.
- **What it holds is in the backpack itself** (its container, as a shulker box's): drop it, trade it, keep it in a chest, it travels with its contents.
- **Safe by design**: the menu's slots are the backpack's own storage, so every move goes through it in one transaction; the backpack in your hand can't go into itself, and the menu closes once it leaves your hand.

**What it changes in the game**: through the mod API (an item container on each backpack, a chest menu backed by the held backpack, the `use_item`, `menu_clicked`, `menu_closed` and `mod_mismatch` hooks; no mixins). Backpacks of 0.1.0 (which kept their contents in `<world>/vastpacks/`) get them back once, the first time one is opened while an operator holds it; that file is then renamed, never deleted. No network of its own.

The project's id is `vastbackpacks`: `vastpacks` stays the registry's content-only 0.1.0 (the half whose native part was never published). The items keep their `vastpacks:` ids, so backpacks saved with 0.1 and 0.2 stay in their worlds, and a world that recorded the old `vastpacks` code mod opens without the missing-mods question (the mod resolves that id when no `vastpacks` mod is loaded). Turn the old `vastpacks` content mod off: two mods can't own one namespace. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a.

Known issue: on the pinned engine the backpack menu closes as soon as it opens in single player, and can on a dedicated server too, because Horizon can't yet back a menu's slots during the player's own turn (horizon-rust/horizon#18513; fix: horizon-rust/horizon#19593). In creative a shift-click can fill a second backpack instead of the held one (horizon-rust/horizon#18515), fixed in the game by horizon-rust/horizon#19595 after this pin.

versions.changelog: A world saved with the old `vastpacks` id opens without the missing-mods question: the mod answers `mod_mismatch` and resolves `vastpacks` when no mod by that id is loaded (an old `vastpacks` mod that is still loaded is left alone). Tested in single player on a copy of a 0.2.3 world with a filled backpack: no question, contents kept, and the world then records `vastbackpacks`. Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-18 (0b14f8a).

projects.summary: The game's blocks packed nine at a time, from I (9 blocks) to IX (387,420,489), and back.

The overlays are hand-drawn pixel art made in the repository; a block shows the game's own texture by name, none is shipped. Inspired by AllTheCompressed by the All The Mods team; not affiliated with or endorsed by All The Mods.

projects.name: Vast Enchanting
projects.summary: An enchanting table that reads its shelves and goes past max levels, tomes for the anvil, and archives that store enchanted books.
projects.description:
A native mod for enchanting, whose table follows the MIT code of [Apothic Enchanting](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apothic-Enchanting) (by Shadows_of_Fire), with blocks, art, recipes and words of its own, on Horizon's mod API. One package: the code, blocks, items, art and words in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

- **The Vast Enchanting Table** reads the shelves around it (the ring a vanilla table reads) for four stats: power (up to 100, the top offer's cost), chaos (how much offers vary), rarity (rare enchantments favoured, more enchantments per offer) and clues (how many are shown). Its offers go past vanilla's maximum levels. Its own screen shows the offers and the stats.
- **18 shelves** in families (ember, tide, abyss, void, sight, and Vast Depths' metals), each raising power up to its own limit. A **relic shelf** lets the table offer treasure enchantments; a **veto shelf** holds five enchanted books whose enchantments the table won't offer.
- **Infusions**: with the right stats the table turns an item into another (shelves into infused ones, tomes into better tomes, an archive into the next).
- **Tomes** at the anvil take an item's enchantments into a book: about half (tattered), all of them (bound), or all of them and the item back plain and worn (siphon).
- **Archives** keep enchanted books as points (two books of a level make one of the next) and write enchantments back onto books, one level at a time or as high as the points allow: up to level 16 (arcane) or 31 (void). A broken archive keeps everything in its item.

**What it changes in the game**: the Vast Enchanting Table's offers and the levels and lapis they take, the anvil's result when a tome is on its right, a broken archive's drop (it carries what it held) and its contents when placed. It works through the mod API (block entity, menu and item Parts, the anvil and drop hooks; no mixins). Everything lives in the blocks' own data; no files, no network.

0.2.0 replaces 0.1.0's two files (`vastenchanting_native` .hnmod and the `vastenchanting` content mod); blocks placed with 0.1 keep what they hold. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a. Not yet: Apothic Enchanting's own enchantments (Horizon loads only the game's), typed tomes and the prismatic web. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apothic Enchanting's authors; none of its assets or lang are used.

versions.changelog: First release on Horizon's mod API: one native package (code and content). Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-18 (0b14f8a). Blocks placed with 0.1 keep what they hold. Archive levels are bounded by the archive's cap, so a malformed archive can't stall the server; tables keep no global state.

projects.summary: Ten metals, three gems and nine alloys with dusts, plates, gears, rods and an ore hammer, generated in the overworld.
projects.description:
A content mod: data only, nothing to build.

- **Ten metals:** aluminum, lead, nickel, osmium, platinum, silver, tin, uranium, zinc and iridium. Each has a stone and a deepslate ore, raw ore, raw block, ingot, nugget, block, dust, plate, gear and rod.

projects.name: Vast Rifts
projects.summary: Rifts that bring waves of mobs, stronger wave by wave, and rewards for beating them.
projects.description:
A native mod of combat events on Horizon's mod API, whose waves follow the MIT data of [Gateways to Eternity](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/GatewaysToEternity) (by Shadows_of_Fire), with names, art and words of its own. One package: the code, the sigils, their art, recipes and words in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

- **Place a rift's sigil** and the rift opens: a swirl of its colour and a bar at the top of the screen. Each wave has a few seconds of setup, then its mobs come out around it; kill them all before the wave's time runs out and its rewards drop on the rift. Beat the last wave and it closes with its own rewards.
- **Seven rifts**: Ember (blazes), Warp (endermen), Mire (slimes), Pasture (crops and animals), Night (the overworld's night mobs), Inferno (the nether fortress) and Golem (iron golems), from small to large, with named mobs in their own gear.
- **Stronger wave by wave**: health, speed, damage and knockback go up.
- **Collapse**: if a wave runs out of time, or no player stays within 32 blocks, the rift collapses, its mobs vanish and some strike back (an explosion, blindness, a few mobs). Rifts of hostile mobs don't open on Peaceful.

**What it changes in the game**: through the mod API (hooks, Parts and the Host; no mixins) it summons the rifts' mobs and rewards (items, experience, a few animals) around a rift block, runs a few commands for its effects, tells nearby players in chat and shows them a boss bar. A rift's progress lives in its block entity's data; no files, no network.

0.2.0 replaces 0.1.0's two files (`vastrifts_native` .hnmod and `vastrifts` content): remove both. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a (the mod API). Not yet: endless rifts. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Gateways to Eternity's author; none of its art or words are used.

Replaces 0.1.0's two files (`vastrifts_native` .hnmod and the `vastrifts` content mod, never published). Reward tables are the mod's own; a rift's cleanup only touches its own dimension; an out-of-range saved wave no longer stops the rift's tick.

projects.name: Vast Spawners
projects.summary: Change spawners with items, mine them with Silk Touch, and shape the mobs they make.
projects.description:
A native mod for spawners, built from the MIT code and data of [Apothic Spawners](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apothic-Spawners) (by Shadows_of_Fire), with names and words of its own, on Horizon's mod API. One package: the code and its words in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

- **Change a spawner** by right clicking it with an item, used up: sugar and a clock shorten its waits, a fermented spider eye, a ghast tear, prismarine crystals and a piston raise its batch size, crowd limit, player reach and spread. With quartz in the other hand the change goes back.
- **Switches**: a nether star makes it work with no player near, a conduit or a soul lantern lets it spawn anywhere or in any light, a comparator makes it work only with a redstone signal, and chorus fruit, wool, a golden dandelion and a campfire make its mobs dazed (no AI), hushed, young or burning.
- **Echoes** (echo shards, up to 3): its mobs' loot drops once more per echo. **Vigour** (pointed dripstone): its mobs spawn with less health.
- **Silk Touch** mines a spawner with all of that and its mob; placed again, it is the same spawner. Its tooltip lists them.
- Every modifier's tooltip says what it does.

**What it changes in the game**: a right click on a spawner with those items (the item is spent, the spawner's data changes), a spawner's drop when mined with Silk Touch and its data when placed, the range a wired spawner looks for a player in, the health of a weakened spawner's mobs, and the loot of an echoing spawner's mobs. It works through the mod API (hooks and Parts on the vanilla spawner; no mixins). Everything it keeps lives in the spawner's and the mob's own data; no files, no network.

0.3.0 replaces 0.2's two files (`vastspawners_native` .hnmod and the `vastspawners` content mod); spawners changed with them keep their changes. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a. Not yet: Jade and JEI lines (0.2 compiled them into those mods' builds; the mod API has no way yet), the egg-catching enchantment, unstable spawners and advancements. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apothic Spawners' authors; none of its assets or lang are used.

versions.changelog: First release on Horizon's mod API: one native package (code and content). Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-18 (0b14f8a). Spawners changed with 0.2 keep their changes; the Jade and JEI lines are left out for now. A placed spawner only takes the mod's own, validated settings from its item; arbitrary spawner data still needs an operator.

projects.name: Vast Star
projects.summary: The last craft of the Vast family: five cores, a Star Seed and the Vast Star. Needs Vast Depths, Vast Ores, Vast Compressed and Vast Adventures.
projects.description:
A content mod: data only, nothing to build. The goal at the end of a long game.

- **Core of the Deep** (Vast Depths' Stellarite, Infernium and Voidium blocks), **Core of Alloys** (a block of each of Vast Ores' nine alloys), **Core of Pressure** (Vast Compressed's VI and V tiers), **Core of Valor** (Vast Adventures' gems, seals and a Titan Pearl) and **Core of the Wild** (a totem, a dragon head, a sniffer egg, a heart of the sea, a trident, an enchanted golden apple and more).
- **Star Seed:** four nether stars, four echo shards and a heavy core.
- **Vast Star:** the five cores, the Star Seed and four end crystals. Nine make a **Block of Vast Star**, which shines and serves a beacon.
- English and Brazilian Portuguese; every sprite drawn for this mod, the star shimmering.

**Install Vast Depths, Vast Ores, Vast Compressed and Vast Adventures too.** Inspired by the All The Mods packs' ATM Star; nothing of it is used, not affiliated with or endorsed by All The Mods.

versions.changelog: Fix: the Block of Vast Star drops itself again. 0.1.0's loot table used the old condition shape, which 26.3 reads as a failed condition, so breaking the block dropped nothing.

projects.name: Vast Tweaks
projects.summary: KubeJS-style scripts for your recipes: remove, replace, unify, add and override recipes and tags from config/vasttweaks/*.vt, with /reload.
projects.description:
Change any mod's recipes with a small script, the way KubeJS does on Java, for modpack makers and players.

1. Install it and build natives. Open a world once: you get **`config/vasttweaks/`** with a README and an example.
2. Write **`<anything>.vt`** files there and run **`/reload`**. The recipe book and JEI show the changes.
3. **`last-load.txt`** in that folder says what loaded and points at any mistake by file and line.

```
remove output minecraft:iron_pickaxe
replace input stick with vastores:steel_rod where id minecraft:*_pickaxe
unify othermod:tin_ingot -> vastores:tin_ingot as #c:ingots/tin
shaped minecraft:saddle
  "LLL"
  "S S"
  L = leather
  S = string
end
shapeless minecraft:string x4 = #minecraft:wool
smelting minecraft:rotten_flesh -> minecraft:leather xp 0.1
override minecraft:furnace shapeless minecraft:furnace = #minecraft:stone_crafting_materials x8
tag item c:ingots/tin add othermod:tin_ingot
```

It also works on a server: the server's scripts apply, and Horizon players get its recipes in their book and JEI.

**What it changes in the game:** on each data load (a world opening, `/reload`) it reads `config/vasttweaks/*.vt` and adds the recipe filters, recipes and tags they say to that load (the mod API's `data_pack_files` hook); when there are scripts, it asks the server to send its clients the recipes of the game's own crafting, cooking, stonecutting and smithing types (`datapack_sync`), so their viewers match. Hooks only, no mixins. It writes only in `config/vasttweaks/` (the first README and example, and `last-load.txt`). No network of its own.

Also a Python tool in the repository compiles the same scripts into a content mod to share (with item renames).

1.2.0 is the same mod on Horizon's mod API (1.1.0 was a `.hnmod`, which launchers from 0.2.70 no longer load). Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a.

versions.changelog: Opening a world no longer crashes: 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 asked the game for its folder while the server loads its data, which Horizon refuses with a panic. The folder is now taken once at registration; scripts load on every world open and `/reload`. Tested in game.

projects.name: Vast Unify
projects.summary: Other mods' metals, dusts, plates and gems made and taken as Vast Ores' own, so a pack has one tin, not five. Needs Vast Ores.
projects.description:
A content mod: data only, nothing to build. **Install Vast Ores too.**

- Every recipe that made another mod's tin dust, steel ingot or ruby now makes Vast Ores' one, and every recipe that asked for theirs takes the `c:` tag, so ours and theirs both fit.
- 130 items: what the Horizon ports of Ender IO, Mekanism, Modern Industrialization, Voltz, Big Nukes and Silent's Gems have now, and the ids Create, Mekanism and Tech Reborn use in Java for what their ports will add. A line for a mod that isn't installed does nothing.
- The game's own iron, gold and copper ingots, nuggets and blocks stay; only their dusts, plates, gears and rods are unified.

Uses Horizon's recipe filters, so it reaches every recipe written as data; ore drops and machines that compute their results in code are out of its reach. Made with [Vast Tweaks](https://github.com/voltzz900/vast-tweaks).

versions.changelog: First release (0.1.0): 130 items of other mods made and taken as Vast Ores' own.

projects.name: VeinSweep
projects.summary: 按住触发键挖方块，同种相连方块一起挖掉，可随时关闭。/ Hold the trigger key to chain-break connected blocks of the same type; can be switched off.
projects.description:
VeinSweep 是连锁挖掘模组：按住触发键（默认潜行键，可在控制中改）挖掉一个方块，与它相连的同种方块会一起被挖掉。

- 矿脉和原木整条带走；泥土、石头等普通方块在附近连成一小片不规则区域。
- 只在同种方块内扩散：泥土不会蔓延到草方块，沙子不会蔓延到砂砾。
- 与手持物无关；工具在连锁中途损坏时会立即停止。
- 黑名单：`/veinsweep blacklist add|remove|list|clear`，支持 Tab 补全，重启后仍有效；修改黑名单需要权限等级 2，`list` 公开。
- 设置页：总开关、最大方块数（8–256）、保留工具耐久、创造模式连锁。
- 连锁由客户端按键触发，只在单人游戏或自己主持的局域网世界生效；专用服务器上不触发（模组仍会正常加载）。

---

VeinSweep is a chain-mining mod: hold the trigger key (sneak by default; rebindable) and break a block to break the connected blocks of the same type.

- Ores and logs come out as a whole vein; dirt, stone and similar blocks break in a small irregular patch nearby.
- It only spreads through the same block type: dirt does not spread to grass, sand does not spread to gravel.
- It works with any held item, and stops at once if the tool breaks mid-chain.
- Blacklist: `/veinsweep blacklist add|remove|list|clear`, with tab completion and persistence across restarts. Changing it needs permission level 2; `list` is public.
- Settings: master switch, maximum blocks (8–256), keep tool durability, and chaining in creative mode.
- Chaining is client-triggered: it works in single player and in a LAN world you host. A dedicated server has no client key input, so chaining does not trigger there (the mod still loads).

versions.changelog:
移除「掉落直接入包」设置，掉落一律在世界中散落（与原开关关闭时一致）；设置页现为四项：连锁破坏、最大方块数、保留工具耐久、创造模式连锁。构建固定更新为 Nightly 2026-11-22 最新构建（f1bb66f）与 Horizon Mixins e59da90（未变），已在生存模式实测连锁触发、同种方块扩散、矿脉整条带走、上限、黑名单、总开关与工具中途损坏即停。

Removed the "Drops go to inventory" setting; drops always scatter in the world (the behaviour of the old switch when off). The settings screen now has four entries: chain breaking, maximum blocks, keep tool durability, and chaining in creative mode. Repinned to the newest Nightly 2026-11-22 build (f1bb66f) with Horizon Mixins e59da90 (unchanged); chaining, same-type spread, whole-vein mining, the limit, the blacklist, the master switch and stopping when the tool breaks were re-verified in-game in survival.

projects.name: Vivid Horizon
projects.summary: Vivid colours, volumetric clouds, clear water with gentle waves, rain that soaks the ground and warm torch-lit nights.
projects.description:
An original shader pack in the spirit of the classic vibrant shaders: a soft blue sky with volumetric clouds and the Milky Way, warm sunlight and cool blue shadows, ambient occlusion, god rays, coloured block light, turquoise water with soft reflections, gentle waves and caustics, raindrop rings and wet ground that reflects the world, depth of field and lens flare.

Every effect can be tuned or turned off in Shader Options (Colour, Light, Sky, Water and plants). About 4.5 ms of GPU at 1440p on an RTX 5070 Ti; on a slower GPU, lower Shadows, Volumetric clouds and Wet ground reflections first.

versions.changelog: Ported to shader API 0.2 (vanilla fog now comes from the pack). Fixes the black picture on 0.2. Much thinner distance haze (no more white film), bluer sky, a more vivid grade, softer water reflections (physical Fresnel) with the gentle animated waves kept, rain and wet ground that fade across biome borders.

projects.name: Vivid Horizon Raytracing
projects.summary: Ray-traced light for Horizon: soft indirect light, sun shadows, light shafts, physical water, painted sky and cubic clouds, vibrant style. Beta.
projects.description:
**Beta.** A ray-traced shader pack for Horizon's shader API 0.2, written from scratch in WGSL. It is the vibrant-colour style on top of a physically based ray-traced lighting base.

- **Ray-traced indirect light**: two bounces of diffuse light from the sun, the sky and glowing blocks, denoised over time and space. Caves and shade pick up colour from what is around them.
- **Soft sun shadows** and light shafts through trees, and underwater beams.
- **Water**: colour follows depth (light loses red first, then green), the seabed shows through in the shallows, waves fade with distance, with sun glitter.
- **Sky**: a painted gradient with Rayleigh and Mie scattering, stars, a Milky Way, and a moon with its phase.
- **Clouds**: soft-edged cubic clouds, lit by the sun and shaded underneath.
- **Image**: glare, bloom, edge anti-aliasing and a tone curve.

Each departure from physics is named in the source comments. For the non-ray-traced vibrant pack, see Vivid Horizon.

## Needs

- Horizon with shader API 0.2 and **ray tracing turned on** (it is opt-in), on a GPU with hardware ray queries.
- HDR frame format set to float.

## Performance

About 150 frames per second in a forest at 1440p on an RTX 5070 Ti (measured by the author, one machine only).

## Known issues

- Vanilla particles (torch smoke, rain splashes) do not get the pack's light and fog fully.
- Lamps follow the game's light level and cast no shadow of their own yet.
- Swamp and mangrove water has had little testing.
- Some flicker remains in caves and on block edges.
- Water caustics stop on sharp block edges.
- The cubic clouds are made of rather small cubes.

versions.changelog: Fixes streaked, stretched bands when the resolution scale is below 100 percent. Water keeps its waves, sky and sun mirror and depth when ray tracing is off (a GPU without ray queries, or a game not restarted after picking the pack).

projects.name: vmp_fabric
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Very Many Players (Fabric).
projects.description:
Slice 1 of a Horizon port of [Very Many Players (Fabric)](https://github.com/RelativityMC/VMP-fabric)
by ishland (MIT, upstream read at ver/26.1.1, commit 7e89476). Credits and
license preserved; the upstream LICENSE is carried verbatim in the package.

## What slice 1 holds (1:1 logic core, 27 passing tests)

- **Config model** (`config.rs`): the complete `vmp.properties` set with
  upstream defaults, per-key fallback to the default on a missing or
  malformed value, the normalized write-back under the "Configuration file
  for VMP" comment, the java.util.Properties reader subset (comments,
  =/:/whitespace separators, escapes, continuations), and the
  `vmp:incompatibleConfig` forcing pass with upstream's exact warning
  wording and the `vmp.ignoreIncompatibleConfig` override.
- **Coordinate keys** (`mcutil.rs`): `MCUtil.getCoordinateKey/X/Z` and the
  `ChunkPos` packed helpers the watching maps run on.
- **SimpleObjectPool** (`pool.rs`): the fixed-size pool state machine
  (alloc reuse, oversized fallback without the initializer, release no-op
  when full). Upstream synchronizes access; this port is single-threaded,
  wrap at the call site.
- **AreaMap** (`area_map.rs`): the spatial index behind player watching,
  with add/remove/update diffing, per-cell object sets, the sorted listener
  walk by Chebyshev distance, and the same update-diff asymmetry upstream
  ships (adds iterate the new square minus the old, removals the old minus
  the new). Upstream's pooled insertion-ordered identity sets run on plain
  sets here with identical observable behavior.
- **AreaPlayerChunkWatchingManager** (`chunk_watching.rs`): the two-map
  bookkeeping (player map at view distance, general map at
  `GENERAL_PLAYER_AREA_MAP_DISTANCE` = 6, computed from the upstream
  `ceil(max immediate despawn range / 16.0)` formula over the vanilla
  SpawnGroup table), add/remove/move and on-watch-distance-change.

## Status

Ships as the tested 1:1 logic core; nothing is wired in game yet (no hooks).
The server-coupled surfaces (Netty event loops, async chunks, portals, async
logging, entity tracking, ticket propagator, biome access, spawn density cap)
are seams noted in the README for slice 2+.

Pinned to Horizon f00125f61f794aaa3d4e950d301f353b35b6ee3d and horizon-mixins e59da9094f0c2fdda6c627fe9eff22dec6a906f0.

Licence: MIT. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-vmp-fabric

versions.changelog: Full-source rebuild on the current SDK: package carries the repo's modular layout with a real mod entry in lib.rs (no game.rs splice), upstream's MIT LICENSE in the package, corrected authors, description and pins.

projects.name: Voice Chat
projects.summary: Simple Voice Chat client for Horizon: proximity voice, positional audio, groups, push-to-talk, and voice activation.
projects.description:
An unofficial native client for the [Simple Voice Chat](https://github.com/henkelmax/simple-voice-chat) protocol on Horizon. Join a compatible Minecraft server and talk with other players through proximity voice or private groups.

- Proximity voice with distance attenuation and stereo positioning.
- Push-to-talk and voice activation with a live microphone meter.
- Password-protected groups and a group member roster.
- Per-player and per-source volume controls, including compatible modded audio sources.
- Input and output device selection without rejoining the server.
- Speaking indicators, player heads, and group icons in the HUD and name tags.
- A localized in-game menu with vanilla-style controls and feedback sounds.

Simple Voice Chat 2.6.x and 2.7 are supported. The server must run Simple Voice Chat and expose its voice UDP port.

While voice chat is enabled, the microphone remains open for the live level meter. Push-to-talk sends audio only while PTT or Whisper is held, plus a short release tail. Disable Voice Chat closes the audio streams and clears queued microphone samples. Audio is not written to disk.

Voice traffic uses client-server UDP only, with no peer-to-peer connections. The server selects the voice host and port, with a fallback to the game server's address. Local storage contains audio/interface preferences, device names, per-player/source UUID volume overrides, and per-server protocol versions. It does not contain audio, group passwords, or voice encryption secrets.

This is a native source package: Horizon Launcher builds it against the pinned SDK. Native code is not sandboxed and runs with the player's permissions.

Not affiliated with Max Henkel or the Simple Voice Chat project.

versions.changelog: Targets Horizon Nightly 0a875da. Includes the audio lifecycle and documentation fixes from 1.0.2.

projects.name: Voltz (assets)
projects.summary: The blocks, items, textures, text and recipes of Voltz. Needs the Voltz native mod.
projects.description:
**This is one of the two parts of [Voltz](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/voltz_core), and does little alone.** Install both: this one, the assets, and the native part.

It holds the blocks, items, creative tabs, textures, text and recipes of Voltz. It has no code. The code, and the description of what the mod does, are in Voltz.

All the art is original and drawn for this project. No Minecraft assets and no art from other mods are included. MIT licensed.

projects.name: Wayfarer Stones
projects.summary: Place stones around your world, activate them, and travel between the ones you know.
projects.description:
**One mod, one file, on Horizon's new mod API.** 0.8.0 carries the textures, text, recipes and villages inside it. If you still have [Wayfarer Stones (assets)](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/wayfarer_stones), remove it: both use the same namespace. Your stones, their names and each world's settings stay.

- **Place** a stone, or find one in a village. Right-click it once to add it to your list.
- **Travel** from any stone you know: pick a destination on the screen, or search for it. You land beside the stone, on solid ground.
- **Pay** in experience levels: 1, plus 1 for each 500 blocks, up to 5. Travel between dimensions costs 3.
- **Carry** a Wayfarer's Scroll to travel from anywhere. Each travel uses one up.
- **Stones are safe:** only the owner or an operator can break one, and pistons won't move it.

Every world has its own settings: cost, cooldown, warmup and more. English and Russian.

**Commands:** `/wayfarer`, `/wayfarer list`, `/wayfarer to <name>`, `/wayfarer name <name>`, `/wayfarer forget <name>`. Operators also have `/wayfarer global <name>` and `/wayfarer remove <name>`.

Native source mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, press Build there, and confirm the native-code warning. The launcher compiles it against the Horizon build it is pinned to, named in each version's changelog. It runs with your account's permissions.

No Minecraft code or assets are included. All the art is original. MIT licensed.

versions.changelog: Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-22 (2b77287) and Horizon Mixins e59da90, so it builds on that Nightly (a launcher there left 0.8.0 out). No change in the mod itself.

projects.name: WhenChat
projects.summary: Prefixes an [HH:MM:SS] stamp on every chat message.
projects.description:
Adds a local-time `[HH:MM:SS]` stamp to the front of every incoming chat line, so you can tell when something was said.

This is an unofficial Rust port of [WhenChat](https://github.com/ErikEdits/WhenChat) by ErikEdits (MIT), written against Horizon's native mod API. The original's credit and MIT licence are kept in the package and in [`native/whenchat`](https://github.com/Jorungandr/horizon-rust-mods/tree/main/native/whenchat).

- The stamp follows your computer's clock on Windows; on other platforms this release displays UTC instead of local time.
- Nothing is sent anywhere; it only changes how chat is drawn.
- It has no settings yet: every chat line gets the stamp, your own messages included. Action-bar (overlay) text is left alone.

versions.changelog: First release.

projects.name: World Atlas
projects.summary: Minimap, world map with cave and Nether layers, entity radar and waypoints with beams.
projects.description:
A minimap and a full-screen world map of everything you have explored, with waypoints you can see from afar.

- **Minimap:** square or round, north up or turning with you, in any corner. It shows terrain shading, waypoints, mob faces and structure markers. [ and ] zoom it; hold Z to enlarge it.
- **World map (M):** drag, zoom about the cursor, and switch between the surface, cave layers and the Nether's roof. The bottom line shows the biome and the matching Nether/Overworld position.
- **Waypoints (J):** name, exact X Y Z, colour and icon. Each can have a light beam you can see from far away with a fade distance, and can be temporary. You can search, track, share or link them through portals. Your last three deaths are kept as waypoints.
- **Compass bar** (optional) at the top of the screen, with your waypoints at their bearings.
- **Overlays from the seed:** chunk grid, slime chunks and structures.
- **PNG export** of the explored map.

Client-side, API only: no injections and no native code. It sees what your client is shown, nothing more.
Its source and a picture tour are at [publicusr/atlas](https://github.com/publicusr/atlas).

projects.name: wstweaks
projects.summary: A Horizon port of wstweaks.
projects.description:
A port of [Wither Skeleton Tweaks](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Wither-Skeleton-Tweaks) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- **Wither Skull Fragments** — a wither skeleton that does not drop a Wither Skeleton Skull drops a `wstweaks:fragment`. Upstream gates the drop on `Shard Drop Chance` (default 1.0, i.e. always) with a `nextFloat() <=` roll; the port reads the same key from `config/wstweaks.toml`.
- **Skeleton Conversion** — any skeleton **or stray** that spawns in the Nether becomes a wither skeleton, and (with `Give Bows`, default true) the converted mob is given a fresh undamaged bow, as upstream's `WSTEvents` does.
- **The Immolation Blade** — burns its target for 150 seconds and kills skeleton-family mobs with one hit; a blade kill drops the skull.
- The fragment item, both blades and their content (models, textures, recipes, tag, creative tab, language) from the jar.

**Not yet ported**

- **Blade damage source.** Upstream's beheading deals a 150-damage fake-player blow so the loot table sees a player kill; the pin cannot label the hit `minecraft:fireworks`, so the guaranteed skull is granted by the port's own drop path instead of through the blade's damage type.
- **Blade held by a player.** The pin's loot context carries a different uuid for the same player than the acting-player helper, so a loot condition that tests the blade in hand can never be true; the port therefore grants the skull directly rather than through a loot modifier.
- Only `Shard Drop Chance` is configurable; the blade's stats are fixed in content, and modded skeleton subclasses match by id.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2019 Brennan Ward`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: First release

projects.name: xnet
projects.summary: A controller, its cable network and an item channel that moves one item per ten ticks.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [XNet](https://github.com/McJtyMods/XNet) (MIT, by **McJty**) for Horizon. This first slice is the **controller**, its **cable/connector network** and the **item channel**.

**Implemented so far**

- **The controller** (`xnet:controller`) saves **eight channels** in its block entity, and the network is walked with upstream's own rule: the controller owns the network of the connector it touches.
- **The network blocks:** `xnet:netcable` and `xnet:connector`, plus their blue variants.
- **The item channel** moves one item per operation, at the jar's default **one item per 10 ticks**, with inserters ordered by priority and whitelist/blacklist filters.
- **Inspection and configuration:** `/xnet info` reports the network, and eight operator settings commands change the channel.

**Not yet ported**

- the energy, fluid, gas and other channels;
- the controller's RF cost: upstream burns 1 RF/t per channel plus 2 RF/operation from a 100,000 FE buffer, and this slice runs the item channel unpowered while the energy slice adds the buffer, the capability and the cost;
- the controller's GUI (this slice configures with commands);
- the other XNet blocks (advanced connectors, the router, the antenna and the wireless router).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the item channel's amount and destination policy: `SINGLE`/`STACK`/`COUNT` with `extractAmount`, the stock-keeping `count` on either end, and `PRIORITY`/`ROUNDROBIN` destinations — the rules upstream's `tickItemHandler` and `fetchItem` already carry, now saved per connector and surviving a relaunch. Three carried artefacts were dead and are fixed: the recipes were in the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` form the pin rejects, so every one logged `invalid ingredient` and crafted nothing; the cable and connector loot tables dropped a block id that has no item, so breaking one gave nothing usable; and the recipes' `c:` tags were declared by no mod, so the four tags are carried with their vanilla members. Proven in game: stack mode moves 20 of 20 in one operation where single moves 1; a count of 16 moves 160 in 100 ticks; `stock 5` fills the target to 5 and `keep 5` leaves 5 at the source; round robin sends 10 east and 10 south where priority sends 0 and 20; an unknown mode is refused with the readout unchanged; and the settings survive a relaunch and keep moving items.

projects.name: Zenith
projects.summary: Clean-room PBR shader pack for Horizon 0.2 with PCSS shadows, volumetric light, custom skies, water refraction, GTAO, and AgX tone mapping.
projects.description:
**Zenith** is a clean-room, MIT-licensed PBR shader pack built natively for **Horizon** (Shader API `0.2`, `schema = 1`).

### Features
- **Physically-Based Materials:** LabPBR 1.3 support with per-sprite detection and procedural PBR fallback, parallax occlusion mapping (POM) paired with native vertex displacement, copper oxidation finishes, amethyst scatter, foliage subsurface scattering, and rain wetness/puddles.
- **Lighting & Shadows:** Variable-penumbra PCSS shadows, translucent colored shadows through stained glass, cloud shadows, multi-bounce GTAO, directional interior lamp shading, and colored voxel & dynamic particle lighting.
- **Water & Underwater Optics:** Multi-swell animated water waves with distance shimmer fade, planar & sky-LUT reflections, depth-aware screen-space refraction, dispersive RGB caustics, cellular rain ripples, Snell-refracted underwater light shafts, and calibrated underwater visibility.
- **Atmosphere & Weather:** 64x33 Hillaire sky-view LUT with biome climate adaptation, volumetric cumulus and high cirrus clouds, night stars, Milky Way, and northern aurora, 3D domain-warped dawn mist, snowstorms, and powder-snow immersion.
- **The End & The Nether:** Custom cosmic nebula, dual-scale starfield, and End Warp Rift portal in The End; volcanic ash haze and lava underglow in The Nether.
- **Post-Processing:** Screen-space reflections (SSR), multi-level bloom pyramid, AgX-inspired HDR tone mapping, log-luminance histogram auto-exposure, FXAA and morphological anti-aliasing, and optional cinematic optics (depth of field, motion blur, lens flare, color moods).

### Performance & Presets
Includes **Performance**, **Balanced** (default), and **Quality** presets plus 61 configurable options organized by category in Horizon's shader settings.

### Requirements & Source
- Built for **Horizon Shader API 0.2** (`schema = 1`, Horizon `nightly-2026-11-21` / `8f83e5c` or compatible builds).
- Full source code, optional **Zenith RT** hardware ray-tracing overlay (`variants/zenith-rt`), and algorithm citations (`PROVENANCE.md`) are available in the GitHub repository.

versions.changelog:
Zenith 0.2.0:
- New Ultra quality mode: the most samples everywhere (GTAO, SSR, subsurface scattering, contact shadows, light shafts, clouds) and full-resolution clouds; shadow map up to 8192 texels and 384 / 512 blocks
- Physically based atmosphere: one haze medium (air, aerosol haze, valley fog) for aerial perspective, the horizon and the sun shafts; distant terrain and LODs fade into the horizon colour, valley fog at dawn, in rain and in humid biomes
- Volumetric cumulus clouds with a 3D billow detail and self-shadowing, steps by quality mode
- Glossy screen-space reflections with roughness and contact-hardening blur, Hi-Z accelerated
- Subsurface scattering for skin, wax, snow, ice and other LabPBR subsurface materials
- Faster: clouds baked at half resolution in a separate pass (sky with clouds 7-13 ms -> 3-4.5 ms on Quality), Hi-Z depth 1.24 -> 0.24 ms
- Fixed: clouds jumping with view bob; looking at the sun washing out half the screen (sun shafts were about 5x too bright, the default Volumetric light 0.6 now looks like the old 0.1); dark flickering dots in the haze on leaves
